title: It’s Alive! Jane Aaron
description: A Brand New Day. 1974. 3 min. DCP. In Plain Sight. 1977. 3 min. DCP. Kuumba. 1978. 7 min. Codirected by Robert Bloomberg. 16mm. Interior Designs. 1980. 4 min. Selections from Sesame Street. 3 min. DCP. Remains to Be Seen. 1981. 6 min. DCP. Traveling Light. 1985. 2 min. DCP. Selections from MTV and Nick at Nite. 6 min. DCP. Set in Motion. 1986. 4 min. DCP. This Time Around. 1989. 5 min. DCP. American Pixilation Dance Theatre Presents. Codirected by Skip Blumberg and Alice Wexler. 3 min. DCP. Total runtime 47 min. A New York City native, Jane Aaron was an essential voice in its independent animation scene beginning in the 1970s. She employed a number of sophisticated rigs and stop-motion techniques throughout her career to innovate and celebrate intersections of movement, color, and play. Highlighting both her independent and commercial films, this program underscores Aaron’s legacy as an individual talent and steadfast collaborator, working alongside life partner and fellow filmmaker Skip Blumberg and composer Donald Fagen (Steely Dan). Blumberg donated her film and video work, as well as her production art, to The Museum of Modern Art in 2021.

title: Malá mořská víla (The Little Mermaid)
description: Malá mořská víla (The Little Mermaid). 1976. Czechoslovakia. Directed by Karel Kachyňa. Screenplay by Kachyňa, Ota Hofman, based on the book by Hans Christian Andersen. With Miroslava Šafránková, Radovan Lukavský, Petr Svojtka, Libuše Šafránková. 4K digitization by Národní filmový archiv; courtesy Národní filmový archiv. In Czech; English subtitles. 84 min. After a decade directing one blistering anti-totalitarian allegory after another, director Karel Kachyňa survived the purges that followed 1968 by distancing himself from that earlier body of work. His longtime writing partner Jan Procházka was blacklisted, but Kachyňa was allowed to continue directing after renouncing their collaboration. Made at the peak of what historians call the “offensive” phase of normalization, and coproduced by Barrandov and the Soviet studio Mosfilm, Kachyňa’s The Little Mermaid is one of those rare films that resembles an unusually uncanny dream. Having been forced to abandon overt political subjects, Kachyňa retreats into a world almost entirely without realism: The mermaids’ Sea Kingdom, draped in cloth and soft light, remains one of the most beautifully artificial environments in Czechoslovak cinema. This is the world premiere of a new 4K scan courtesy of the Národní filmový archiv.

title: State Funeral (ГОСУДАРСТВЕННЫЕ ПОХОРОНЫ)
description: State Funeral (ГОСУДАРСТВЕННЫЕ ПОХОРОНЫ). 2019. Netherlands/Lithuania. Written and directed by Sergei Loznitsa. DCP courtesy MUBI. In Russian; English subtitles. 135 min. The shock of the nation was palpable on March 5, 1953, as though a god had forsaken his people: Comrade Stalin is dead! Long live Comrade Stalin! Sergei Loznitsa provides a riveting forensic study of Josef Stalin’s cult of personality, stitching together largely unseen archival images of his funeral and the gatherings of thousands of mourners across the Soviet Union, from the streets of Leningrad to the steppes of Eurasia. Described in Pravda, the Soviet newspaper, as “the Great Farewell,” the ceremony carried on for days, with loudspeakers blaring rhapsodic tributes and pledges to redouble efforts to carry out the great leader’s Five-Year Plans, with factories ceremoniously shut down and mountains of flowers piling up, with leaders of the Eastern Bloc flying in to pay their respects, and with grim-faced crowds waiting patiently to gaze upon his body lying in state. As we see countless mourners shedding genuine tears or performing their grief, Loznitsa brings the film—and the hero worship—to a sudden and damning halt.

title: Postřižiny (Cutting It Short)
description: Postřižiny (Cutting It Short). 1980. Czechoslovakia. Directed by Jiří Menzel. Screenplay by Menzel, Bohumil Hrabal. With Magdalena Vášáryová, Jiří Schmitzer, Jaromír Hanzlík. 4K digital restoration by Národní filmový archiv; courtesy Národní filmový archiv. In Czech; English subtitles. 98 min. In 1969, Jiří Menzel was banned from directing after adapting Bohumil Hrabal’s short stories as Larks on a String. This “involuntary break” was lifted four years later on condition he make a normalization-approved film about the dignity of manual labor (the underrated Who Looks for Gold?), and it wasn’t until 1980 that he would work with Hrabal again, on this adaptation of his novella. This is Menzel at his most sentimental and sumptuous: a horny, quintessentially Czech comedy set in a brewery manager’s household during the First Czechoslovak Republic. Even in this context, Menzel still found room for a swipe at the authorities—a slaughtered pig is named after the man who would censor and rework scripts at Barrandov Studios. Magda Vášáryová plays the manager’s wife with startling sensuality, radiant even while gutting a pig and swigging beer.

title: Possible Love (가능한 사랑)
description: Possible Love (가능한 사랑). 2026. South Korea. Written and directed by Lee Chang-dong. With Jeon Do-yeon, Sul Kyung-gu, Cho Yeo-jeong, Zo In-sung. DCP courtesy Netflix. In Korean; English subtitles. 164 min. Winner of the Silver Lion Grand Jury Prize at the Venice Film Festival, Possible Love marks the long-awaited return of Lee Chang-dong (Burning, Poetry), whose infrequent releases make each new film a major—and always ravishing—cinematic event. The precarious existence of a laid-off factory worker and his wife is upended when an affluent documentary filmmaker chooses them as the subjects of her latest project. Featuring an extraordinary ensemble led by Jeon Do-yeon, winner of the Cannes Best Actress prize for Secret Sunshine, the film unfolds as a haunting, slow-burning examination of class disparity, lingering trauma, and the elusive quest for human connection. Probing the mysteries of human behavior, Lee exposes the quiet hypocrisies and unspoken desires that shape how we perceive—and exploit—one another. title: ...a pozdravuji vlaštovky (...And Give My Love tothe Swallows)
description: ...a pozdravuji vlaštovky (...And Give My Love to the Swallows). 1972. Czechoslovakia. Directed by Jaromil Jireš. Screenplay by Jireš and Zora Beráková. With Magdalena Vášáryová, Viera Strnisková, Július Vašek. 35mm, courtesy Národní filmový archiv. In Czech; English subtitles. 86 min. This biopic of the last days of Marie Kudeříková, a 22-year-old Czechoslovak antifascist resistance fighter executed by the Nazis, was directed by New Wave filmmaker Jaromil Jireš (The Joke) after the Soviet occupation. As a work of hagiography, it was conceived and released in the first years of normalization to celebrate the bravery of communist antifascists at a time when, in government, party members were disgracing themselves. An aura of mournful defeat hangs over the film, with Jireš’s once-manic style dialed back as he maps out a dreary prison routine. Magda Vášáryová plays Kudeříková less as a martyr than as a girl groping at an adult political reality, goofing around with fellow prisoners between brutal interrogations. As the film shows, even that freedom will eventually be extinguished.

title: GENERAL DELLA ROVERE
description: Based on the true story of Italian cavalry officer Giovanni Bertone during World War II, GENERAL DELLA ROVERE recounts the unexpected moral evolution of Emanuele Bardone (Vittorio de Sica), an ingratiating swindler with a talent for improvising novel solutions to the dilemmas he has sprung on himself. Alas, even when Bardone wins, he feels compelled to double-down and gamble away his momentary advantage. He has a talent for extracting favors from the Nazi officers in Genoa, and when the law catches up to Bardone, he’s offered a bargain: go to prison and imitate the Italian general Della Rovere, in hopes of penetrating his resistance network. De Sica’s big and boisterous performance anchors the film, and renders this somber story of ethical compromise into an improbable crowdpleaser. Rossellini considered GENERAL DELLA ROVERE an embarrassing capitulation, a work-for-hire to demonstrate that he could, under duress, follow a script and a schedule. Shot quickly on studio sets with some undisguised rear projection footage, GENERAL DELLA ROVERE went on to win the Golden Lion at the Venice Film Festival and revitalize Rossellini’s career after a decade of box office setbacks. Like Bardone, Rossellini always had another trick up his sleeve.

title: threeASFOUR: FULL CIRCLE
description: Avant-garde designers and best friends Gabi Asfour, Angela Donhauser, and Adi Gil have spent 25 years working together as the NYC fashion collective threeASFOUR. Although they have built an impressive reputation and a following that includes Björk, Marisa Tomei, and Chloë Sevigny, they find themselves struggling to pay the rent on their Chinatown studio while financing the intricate creations for their next runway collection. Drawing from a captivating trove of archival footage alongside intimate observations of the trio at work, Sean Ono Lennon forges an affectionate portrait of uncompromising artists who have chosen experimentation over commercial success and a moving reflection on artistic collaboration and creative resilience.

title: ONCE UPON A TIME IN HARLEM
description: August 1972: A reunion of Harlem Renaissance luminaries is held at Duke Ellington’s St. Nicholas Ave. townhouse. Though many of these figures haven’t seen each other in 50 years, sharp memories, vigorous debates, and unsettled scores soon flow through this stunner of a cocktail party, which features (among others): artists Romare Bearden, Aaron Douglas, and Richard Bruce Nugent; composer Eubie Blake; poet Arna Bontemps; photographer James Van Der Zee; and activists Richard B. Moore and Louise Patterson. After organizing and shooting this extraordinary gathering, filmmaker William Greaves (SYMBIOPSYCHOTAXIPLASM: TAKE ONE) was unable to complete the film before his death in 2014. One of the cameramen that day was his son David, who expertly reshaped this never-before-seen, newly-restored footage into “a film for the ages…one of the greatest cinematic works of creative nonfiction that I’ve ever seen.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker

title: ALL OF A SUDDEN
description: In the latest film by Oscar®-winning director Ryûsuke Hamaguchi (DRIVE MY CAR), Virginie Efira (BENEDETTA) stars as Marie-Lou, the progressive director of a nursing home in the Parisian suburbs. Her life changes when she meets Mari (Tao Okamoto), Japanese playwright. As the two women reckon with the lives they have lived, they find new ways to make sense of the time that remains. Following caregivers as they navigate the tensions between idealism and pragmatism, Hamaguchi crafts a film that rests fully in the present, attentive to the delicate unfolding of thought, feeling, and human connection.

title: FATHERLAND
description: From the director of IDA and COLD WAR: FATHERLAND follows Nobel Prize-winning author Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler, KINGS OF THE ROAD) and his actress daughter Erika (Sandra Hüller, ANATOMY OF A FALL) as they drive across a war-ravaged 1949 Germany. Returning home after years of exile in the U.S. and exuding a superhuman gravitas, Mann finds the Germany he knew to be gone, replaced by a country with contradictory ideologies. Erika, who acts as his travel coordinator and translator, strives to pierce his detached persona while quietly struggling with a family tragedy.

title: DOV’È LA LIBERTÀ?
description: Incarcerated for twenty-two years after committing a crime of passion, Salvatore Lojacono (Totò) wins parole and returns to a Rome that he scarcely recognizes—and ultimately decides that prison is preferable. Salvatore learns the hard way that business, romance, and family are all elaborate rackets; even the most sympathetic victim he encounters is just on the hunt for a tax swap. His disenchantment is recounted in flashback, as he begs a judge to lock him back up. (The courtroom scenes were, in fact, shot later by Mario Monicelli, after Rossellini abandoned the project in mid-production, and effectively bridged the patchwork of episodes left behind.) The popular Neapolitan comedian Totò gets plenty of opportunities to mug, but also flexes his dramatic muscles as a man who trusts too tenderly. The scenario was inspired by Chaplin’s MODERN TIMES, but the moral vision is closer to MONSIEUR VERDOUX, another comedy born of the recognition that post-war society has been stripped of sentimental illusions and re-organized under principles of ruthless capitalism indistinguishable from the barbarism it displaced. “It stupefied me with its cruelty and bitterness,” wrote Pierre Kast in Cahiers du Cinema, long a bastion of Rossellini apologetics. “It’s a parable of the purest Swiftian type, unpitying and almost intolerable.”

title: RAISE THE RED LANTERN
description: Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father’s death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul. Newly restored, RAISE THE RED LANTERN remains a landmark of Fifth Generation Chinese cinema and 1990s international film. The 4K restoration of RAISE THE RED LANTERN was carried out by the Udine Far East Film Festival on the occasion of its 26th edition. The original image and sound negatives were used under the supervision of Director Zhang Yimou. The vintage positive copy, presented at the 1991 Venice International Film Festival and preserved at the Venice Biennale's Historical Archive of Contemporary Arts, was used for color reference. The restoration was made in 2024 at L'Immagine Ritrovata (Hong Kong – Bologna).

title: THE MAN WITH A CROSS
description: The films that Rossellini made before ROME, OPEN CITY are infrequently revived and rarely discussed. But before he could break the rules and reinvent cinema, he had to hone his filmmaking craft. His early features were commercial works made by a film industry whose growth had been nurtured and supported by Mussolini, even as the films themselves were not, strictly speaking, propaganda made-to-order for the fascist regime. They were nevertheless imbued with enough fascist ethos to make for uncomfortable viewing for post-war audiences. Rossellini’s third feature, THE MAN WITH A CROSS, was conceived by fascist news commentator and editor Asvero Gravelli, and followed the plight of an Italian chaplain on the Russian front. Although the film ends with a dedication to the chaplains who have died in “a crusade against godless barbarians,” Rossellini’s overall approach is more humanist than evangelical. While working unhappily as a screenwriter, Rossellini embarked on his own film, a short about the lives of fish. From the start, Rossellini’s devotion to ‘realism’ was conditional, with this ‘documentary’ about life under the sea actually shot over several months in large aquariums on his rooftop and overlaid with humorous commentary.

title: Dao
description: Dao. 2026. France/Senegal/Guinea-Bissau. Written and directed by Alain Gomis. With Katy Correa, D’Johé Kouadio, Samir Guesmi. DCP courtesy Janus Films. In French, Wolof, Manjak, Portuguese Creole; English subtitles. 192 min. Unfolding across a wedding celebration in France and a traditional funeral rite in Guinea-Bissau, Dao weaves an expansive, deeply personal portrait of a family navigating the bonds between generations, continents, and cultures. At its center is Gloria, a mother preparing to celebrate her daughter’s marriage while mourning the recent loss of her father. Blending fiction, documentary, and improvisation, director Alain Gomis (Félicité, Tey) creates a vibrant, fluid tapestry of ritual, music, dance, and everyday encounters. Featuring a remarkable ensemble of professional and nonprofessional performers, including members of the director’s own family, Dao reflects on ancestry, migration, and the transmission of cultural memory, embracing the complexities of grief and celebration as inseparable parts of the human experience. title: LES CARABINIERS
description: Jean-Luc Godard had long been a champion of Rossellini’s cinema (He famously stated, “All roads lead to Open City.”), even as the younger man’s own filmmaking quickly evolved towards a more modernist and abrasive style. (Upon seeing VIVRE SA VIE, Rossellini admonished Godard that his work was drifting towards “Antonioni-ism.”) Nevertheless, Rossellini gladly accepted a scenario credit and payment from Godard for LES CARABINIERS, a loose adaptation of Benjamin Joppolo’s anti-war play, I carabinieri. Rossellini had directed a stage production in Spoleto, in defiance of a government ban on the play, and his sole contribution to the film was providing an oral summary of Joppolo’s script, which Godard transcribed, cut up, and pasted in his notebook. Godard’s version lets two country bumpkins, Michelangelo and Ulysses, loose upon the world, their only directive from their military recruiter being death, destruction, and any other war crimes they can dream up. The duo’s atrocities are intercut with newsreel footage, postcards of plunder, and other Godardian digressions.

title: threeASFOUR: FULL CIRCLE
description: Avant-garde designers and best friends Gabi Asfour, Angela Donhauser, and Adi Gil have spent 25 years working together as the NYC fashion collective threeASFOUR. Although they have built an impressive reputation and a following that includes Björk, Marisa Tomei, and Chloë Sevigny, they find themselves struggling to pay the rent on their Chinatown studio while financing the intricate creations for their next runway collection. Drawing from a captivating trove of archival footage alongside intimate observations of the trio at work, Sean Ono Lennon forges an affectionate portrait of uncompromising artists who have chosen experimentation over commercial success and a moving reflection on artistic collaboration and creative resilience.

title: ONCE UPON A TIME IN HARLEM

Though many of these figures haven’t seen each other in 50 years, sharp memories, vigorous debates, and unsettled scores soon flow through this stunner of a cocktail party, which features (among others): artists Romare Bearden, Aaron Douglas, and Richard Bruce Nugent; composer Eubie Blake; poet Arna Bontemps; photographer James Van Der Zee; and activists Richard B. Moore and Louise Patterson. After organizing and shooting this extraordinary gathering, filmmaker William Greaves (SYMBIOPSYCHOTAXIPLASM: TAKE ONE) was unable to complete the film before his death in 2014. One of the cameramen that day was his son David, who expertly reshaped this never-before-seen, newly-restored footage into “a film for the ages…one of the greatest cinematic works of creative nonfiction that I’ve ever seen.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker

title: THE ROSSELLINIS
description: “My grandfather left the world his masterpieces, and not a penny to any of us. Instead, he left us an enormous inheritance of family conflicts,” declares Alessandro Rossellini, the son of Renzo Rossellini and grandson of Roberto and his second wife Marcella. Between Roberto’s four wives, numerous mistresses, and descendants stretching from New York to Sweden to Qatar, the Rossellini legacy is nothing if not capacious. In this personal documentary, Alessandro interviews his relatives and tries to diagnose the roots of a genetic ailment: Rossellinitis. Characterized by conviction, outspokenness, and wanderlust (or just plain lust), those suffering from Rossellinitis are encouraged to look deeply into family history and discuss.

title: ALL OF A SUDDEN
description: In the latest film by Oscar®-winning director Ryûsuke Hamaguchi (DRIVE MY CAR), Virginie Efira (BENEDETTA) stars as Marie-Lou, the progressive director of a nursing home in the Parisian suburbs. Her life changes when she meets Mari (Tao Okamoto), Japanese playwright. As the two women reckon with the lives they have lived, they find new ways to make sense of the time that remains. Following caregivers as they navigate the tensions between idealism and pragmatism, Hamaguchi crafts a film that rests fully in the present, attentive to the delicate unfolding of thought, feeling, and human connection.

title: FATHERLAND
description: From the director of IDA and COLD WAR: FATHERLAND follows Nobel Prize-winning author Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler, KINGS OF THE ROAD) and his actress daughter Erika (Sandra Hüller, ANATOMY OF A FALL) as they drive across a war-ravaged 1949 Germany. Returning home after years of exile in the U.S. and exuding a superhuman gravitas, Mann finds the Germany he knew to be gone, replaced by a country with contradictory ideologies. Erika, who acts as his travel coordinator and translator, strives to pierce his detached persona while quietly struggling with a family tragedy.

title: ROME, OPEN CITY
description: Rome, winter 1943: as screeching-tired Gestapo dragnets blanket the “open city,” Resistance leader Marcello Pagliero escapes from his apartment by running across the rooftops (as did co-screenwriter Sergio Amidei in real life), as pregnant widow Anna Magnani prepares for her wedding, parish priest Aldo Fabrizi uses the “frying pan method” to hide the local boys’ bomb brigade’s hardware, and effete Major Harry Feist riffles through his collection of incriminating ID photos—but betrayal, a broad-daylight machine-gunning, a Partisan ambush, blowtorch torture, and death by firing squad loom… Based on actual people and all-too-recent incidents (Magnani’s electrifying final scene was inspired by her enraged pursuit of her boyfriends’s escape by truck); written in a week in Federico Fellini’s kitchen (the only place with heat); shot on a number of the real locations, and cast mainly with non-pros (Fabrizi and second-choice Magnani were already famous, albeit for comedy), OPEN CITY’s documentary look and still hair-raising violence rocked audiences and critics around the world, making Neo-Realism, Rossellini, and Magnani world-famous, sharing the top prize at Cannes, and running twenty-one consecutive months at a single New York cinema. 4K Restoration courtesy Janus Films. 35mm print courtesy Cinecittà.

title: The Kiev Trial (КИЕВСКИЙ ПРОЦЕСС)
description: The Kiev Trial (КИЕВСКИЙ ПРОЦЕСС). 2022. Netherlands/Ukraine. Written and directed by Sergei Loznitsa. DCP courtesy Atoms & Void. In Ukranian, Russian, German; English subtitles. 106 min. Produced by the Baba Yar Holocaust Memorial Center, Sergei Loztnitsa’s The Kiev Trial reconstructs, through previously unseen archival footage, Case No. 1679, the so-called “Kyiv Nuremberg,” the postwar hearings during which 15 Nazis and their collaborators were tried and found guilty of atrocities committed on Ukrainian soil, including the murder of some 3,000 children of mixed ancestry; the execution in mass pits of thousands of Jews from Lvov, Rivne, Kremenchuk, and Novomoskovsk; the assassination of suspected communist partisans; and the liquidation of entire villages “under the Fuhrer’s orders…to create lebensraum [living space] for us.” The unembellished courtroom testimonials of the defendants, corroborated by the witnesses to their crimes, including survivors of Babi Yar and Auschwitz, are a profile in “ordinary” human savagery: murder by lynching, beatings, machine gun, starvation, live burial, fire. The reactions of the masses gathered in Kyiv’s Kalinin Square to witness their death by hanging on January 29, 1946, suggest an uneasy catharsis.

title: RAISE THE RED LANTERN
description: Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father’s death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul. Newly restored, RAISE THE RED LANTERN remains a landmark of Fifth Generation Chinese cinema and 1990s international film. The 4K restoration of RAISE THE RED LANTERN was carried out by the Udine Far East Film Festival on the occasion of its 26th edition. The original image and sound negatives were used under the supervision of Director Zhang Yimou. The vintage positive copy, presented at the 1991 Venice International Film Festival and preserved at the Venice Biennale's Historical Archive of Contemporary Arts, was used for color reference. The restoration was made in 2024 at L'Immagine Ritrovata (Hong Kong – Bologna).

title: Postřižiny (Cutting It Short)
description: Postřižiny (Cutting It Short). 1980. Czechoslovakia. Directed by Jiří Menzel. Screenplay by Menzel, Bohumil Hrabal. With Magdalena Vášáryová, Jiří Schmitzer, Jaromír Hanzlík. 4K digital restoration by Národní filmový archiv; courtesy Národní filmový archiv. In Czech; English subtitles. 98 min. In 1969, Jiří Menzel was banned from directing after adapting Bohumil Hrabal’s short stories as Larks on a String. This “involuntary break” was lifted four years later on condition he make a normalization-approved film about the dignity of manual labor (the underrated Who Looks for Gold?), and it wasn’t until 1980 that he would work with Hrabal again, on this adaptation of his novella. This is Menzel at his most sentimental and sumptuous: a horny, quintessentially Czech comedy set in a brewery manager’s household during the First Czechoslovak Republic. Even in this context, Menzel still found room for a swipe at the authorities—a slaughtered pig is named after the man who would censor and rework scripts at Barrandov Studios. Magda Vášáryová plays the manager’s wife with startling sensuality, radiant even while gutting a pig and swigging beer.

title: THE FLOWERS OF ST. FRANCIS
description: Rossellini’s account of a brief period in the life of Saint Francis is as plainspoken and modest as its subject, an anti-hagiography closer to the mud below than the heavens above. Loosely inspired by Fioretti di San Francesco, a nearly-contemporaneous 14th-century collection of vignettes, the film was shaped into a bare ‘scenario’ by Rossellini and Federico Fellini, but the final result remains bracingly plotless. A series of parables that illustrate the moral quality of its characters rather than any scriptural interpretation, THE FLOWERS OF ST. FRANCIS is built from incidents and yarns: an encounter with a leper, a visit from Saint Clare, the quest for a pig’s foot, and the tale of the brother who keeps giving away his clothes. Francis is played by Brother Nazario Gerardi and the ranks of his disciples are populated by real-life monks that Rossellini featured in PAISAN; the only professional actor in sight is Aldo Fabrizi, with an extended cameo as a preening warlord. Financed by a credulous publisher who believed Rossellini would deliver a devout testament whose debut would coincide with the papally declared ‘Holy Year’ of 1950, THE FLOWERS OF ST. FRANCIS instead premiered in the aftermath of Rossellini’s unsaintly and adulterous dalliance with Ingrid Bergman. The initial critical reaction was indifferent, but Rossellini had the last laugh; in 1995, the Vatican named THE FLOWERS OF ST. FRANCIS among fifteen essential works of religious cinema. 35mm print courtesy Cinecittà. 4K restoration courtesy Janus Films.

title: EUROPA '51
description: Shortly after completing THE FLOWERS OF ST. FRANCIS, Rossellini seized upon a hypothetical: if Francis himself appeared in Europe today and preached his humble doctrine, he would be promptly thrown in an insane asylum. Augmented by ideas derived from Simone Weil and Herbert Marcuse, Rossellini’s thought experiment grew and grew until it became EUROPA ’51, a sweeping state-of-the-continent address aimed at the complacency of post-war society. Luckily, Rossellini retained the services of his wife to put a box office spin on this dense rumination. (It would become, ironically, the only one of their pictures together to do any business in Italy.) Irene Gerard (Ingrid Bergman) is a socialite who’s more focused on throwing a good dinner party than attending to the needs of her young son. When the boy kills himself, Irene’s world is shattered: what could drive a child to so thoroughly reject life, and what can she make of the life that remains? Inspired by her cousin’s commitment to the class struggle, Irene begins devoting her time to Rome’s downtrodden. After all, the sick, the dying, and the poor need her more than her husband (Alexander Knox) ever could, do they not? Is Bergman preaching Communist revolution, Christian neighborliness, or some obscure, hyper-personal fusion of the two? Disarmingly literal and unspeakably sincere in its spiritual crusade, EUROPA ‘51 remains the most mysterious of Bergman and Rossellini’s collaborations.

title: Hadí jed (Serpent’s Poison)
description: Hadí jed (Serpent’s Poison). 1981. Czechoslovakia. Directed by František Vláčil. Screenplay by Vláčil, Irena Charvátová. With Josef Vinklář, Ilona Svobodová, Ferdinand Krůta. 35mm, courtesy Národní filmový archiv. In Czech; English subtitles. 87 min. Best known for his historical epics of the 1960s (Marketa Lazarová, The Valley of the Bees), František Vláčil made this bleak chamber drama about alcoholism nearly two decades later, as the disease had consumed much of his own life. Eighteen-year-old Vladka is told by her dying mother that her father, whom she has never met, is alive; after a search, she finds him drilling geological test wells in the snowy highlands. As played by Josef Vinklář, her father is a charming but pitiful alcoholic she comes to love despite her instincts—and yet, true to Vláčil’s fatalistic worldview, their tentative bond cannot survive the serpent’s poison of addiction. Shot in severe black and white, the film pares Vláčil’s once-elaborate visual language down to plain medium shots in cramped, intimate settings, a spare interrogation into the seeming inability of humans to ever change their habitual behaviors.

description: JOSEPHINE follows the psychological fallout after eight-year-old Josephine (Reeves) witnesses a brutal crime in Golden Gate Park. As she acts out, her parents (Tatum and Chan) struggle with helping their daughter cope, while facing the moral responsibility of demanding justice in a world that’s lost its innocence. Open Fri Nov 20, more showtimes to be announced.

title: The History of Concrete
description: Fri, Sep 18: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Edy Modica (actress, comedian, filmmaker), after 4:40 show! Fri, Sep 18: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Rachel Kaly (comedian, writer, actor), after 7:15 show! Sun, Sep 20: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Sarah Sherman after 2:10 show! Following the finale of his TV show, filmmaker John Wilson searches for a new creative outlet. After attending a workshop on how to write and sell a Hallmark movie, he attempts to apply the same formula to a documentary about concrete.

title: Naza
description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them. We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA ’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence. — Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

title: Fjord
description: An immigrant Romanian family living in Norway is subject to an investigation and faces the scrutiny of the local judicial system.

title: The Devils
description: All screenings on a new 35mm print of the 4K restoration of the film. An enduring, singular masterpiece of cinema starring Academy Award-winner Vanessa Redgrave and Oliver Reed, KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption – and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell. Assembled from the original camera negative, this new 4K restoration presents Ken Russell’s definitive vision of The Devils by referencing the edit he privately constructed in 2004. The film’s sound has been remastered from original English Composite 35mm Mag Film, transferred at 96kHz, plus other original film elements in selected spots as needed. The Picture and Sound restoration was performed by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color, and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: You Can See Everything
description: Thirty-four days before she’s sent to prison, notorious Silicon Valley founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a skeptical film crew to document her every move. What begins as an intimate portrait of an enigmatic felon becomes a mind-bending three-year journey into the abyss.

title: Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut
description: Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, The Devils lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. The restoration many believed would never happen reaffirms Russell’s incendiary masterpiece as among the most overwhelming and uncompromising achievements in British cinema. Assembled from original camera negative, this 4k restoration is Ken Russell’s 2004 preferred edit. Picture and sound restoration by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: La Bola Negra
description: Spain, 1932. A young man seeks admission to the local casino. In 1937, a conscripted nationalist soldier stands guard over a Republican prisoner. In 2017, a former playwright inherits an unexpected document from his grandfather. Through a dazzlingly constructed and performed triptych, La Bola Negra traces the hidden connections between three men separated by time but bound by experience and the way in which queer lives, memories and histories endure across generations.

title: VOYAGE TO ITALY
description: In Naples to sell a late uncle’s villa, London business man George Sanders and wife Ingrid Bergman find that, after eight years of marriage, they have little to say to each other. And as the closing drags on, Bergman remembers a died-too-young poet who loved her, Sanders frets about time away from work, and they split apart—she to stare at the rawness of the statuary in the Museum, the ionization of Vesuvian craters, the skeletons at the cemetery; he to dally with friends on Capri, languidly pursue an estranged wife, and to wave off an attractive prostitute; both to finally view the plaster molds of the dead of Pompeii. Little happens, and yet subtly we see the degeneration of a marriage. Will it take a miracle to save it? Unsuccessful on first release, but over the years steadily climbing the ranks of All-Time Ten Best lists. In this centenary tribute to her father and his cinema of thought, Isabella Rossellini plays herself, her mother Ingrid Bergman, David O. Selznick, Alfred Hitchcock, Federico Fellini, Charlie Chaplin, and others.

title: An Unfinished Film
description: ★★★★★ “An utterly unique and very important movie about Covid, the crisis that affected all of us.” – The Guardian Director Xiaorui convinces his cast and crew to resume the shooting of a film halted ten years earlier. In January 2020, with the shoot almost complete, rumours regarding an illness begin to circulate. A hairdresser from Wuhan is sent home, while the crew follows the news on their phones. The director has to decide whether to halt the filming once again. Some of the crew and actors manage to leave before the hotel is locked down by security guards and everyone left on set is confined to their hotel rooms. As all communication is reduced to phone screens, Wuhan is locked down. The crew continues to communicate via video calls, whilst the quarantined main actor Jiang Cheng struggles to support his wife who is now locked-down with their month-old baby in Beijing.

title: The Host
description: When a terrifying creature rises from the Han River and brings chaos to Seoul, single dad Gang-du (Song Kang-ho, Parasite) will stop at nothing to rescue his daughter from the clutches of the horrifying Host. Equal parts creature-feature thrill ride and poignant human story, Oscar-winning visionary Bong Joon Ho’s first global smash remains an incredible action drama and propulsively entertaining modern classic . “A thing of beauty, the perfect mixture of the silly and the grave.” – The New Yorker

title: Paper Tiger 35mm
description: In James Gray’s deeply felt and intense drama, two brothers become entangled in a scheme that turns out to be too good to be true. As they try to navigate their way through the dangerous world of the Russian mafia, family bonds begin to fray with life-altering consequences.

title: CAMERON WINTER AT CARNEGIE HALL
description: Cameron Winter, in December 2025, after a months-long sold-out tour with his band Geese, returned to New York to play a single show at Carnegie Hall. This is the movie.

description: Previous Events: Sunday, July 5: Q&A with directors Lucy Winer and Paula De Koenigsberg after 2:55 show! Monday, July 6: Q&A with directors Lucy Winer and Paula De Koenigsberg after 7:20 show!

title: Alice's Restaurant/I Love You, Alice B Toklas
Apocalypse Now : Final Cut
description: In Vietnam in 1970, Captain Willard (Martin Sheen) takes a perilous and increasingly hallucinatory journey upriver to find and terminate Colonel Kurtz (Marlon Brando), a once-promising officer who has reportedly gone completely mad. In the company of a Navy patrol boat filled with street-smart kids, a surfing-obsessed Air Cavalry officer (Robert Duvall), and a crazed freelance photographer (Dennis Hopper), Willard travels further and further into the heart of darkness.

title: La Bola Negra
description: Explores what it means to be gay throughout different eras, focusing on "three existences" that are connected through themes of sexuality, desire, pain, and inheritance.

Her life changes when she meets Mari (Tao Okamoto), Japanese playwright. As the two women reckon with the lives they have lived, they find new ways to make sense of the time that remains. Following caregivers as they navigate the tensions between idealism and pragmatism, Hamaguchi crafts a film that rests fully in the present, attentive to the delicate unfolding of thought, feeling, and human connection.

title: Naza
description: Directed by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, two of the co-directors of the 2024 Oscar-winning documentary No Other Land , Naza reveals the systems behind Israel’s bombing of Gaza and its mass killing of Palestinian civilians. Winner of Special Jury Prize at the 2026 Venice Film Festival.

title: Josephine
description: JOSEPHINE follows the psychological fallout after eight-year-old Josephine (Reeves) witnesses a brutal crime in Golden Gate Park. As she acts out, her parents (Tatum and Chan) struggle with helping their daughter cope, while facing the moral responsibility of demanding justice in a world that’s lost its innocence. Open Fri Nov 20, more showtimes to be announced.

title: CAMERON WINTER AT CARNEGIE HALL
description: Cameron Winter, in December 2025, after a months-long sold-out tour with his band Geese, returned to New York to play a single show at Carnegie Hall. This is the movie.

title: You Can See Everything
description: Thirty-four days before she’s sent to prison, notorious Silicon Valley founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a sceptical film crew to document her every move. What begins as an intimate portrait of an enigmatic felon becomes a mind-bending three-year journey into the abyss. From boundary-pushing directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim comes You Can See Everything .

title: Night Moves [1975]
description: Hard-nosed private investigator Harry Moseby (Gene Hackman), to distract himself from a rapidly deteriorating marriage, takes a case from an aging B-movie queen (Janet Ward) to locate her runaway daughter, Delly (Melanie Griffith). His search takes him to the Florida Keys, where the girl has been hiding out with her stepfather, Tom (John Crawford), and Tom's lover, Paula (Jennifer Warren). Harry initiates an affair with Paula and soon learns the case is more complex than he first assessed it.

title: News from Home + Interior NY Subway, 14th Street
The Host
description: When a terrifying creature rises from the Han River and brings chaos to Seoul, single dad Gang-du (Song Kang-ho, Parasite) will stop at nothing to rescue his daughter from the clutches of the horrifying Host. Equal parts creature-feature thrill ride and poignant human story, Oscar-winning visionary Bong Joon Ho’s first global smash remains an incredible action drama and propulsively entertaining modern classic . “A thing of beauty, the perfect mixture of the silly and the grave.” – The New Yorker

title: The Devils
description: All screenings on a new 35mm print of the 4K restoration of the film. An enduring, singular masterpiece of cinema starring Academy Award-winner Vanessa Redgrave and Oliver Reed, KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption – and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell. Assembled from the original camera negative, this new 4K restoration presents Ken Russell’s definitive vision of The Devils by referencing the edit he privately constructed in 2004. The film’s sound has been remastered from original English Composite 35mm Mag Film, transferred at 96kHz, plus other original film elements in selected spots as needed. The Picture and Sound restoration was performed by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color, and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: FATHERLAND
description: From the director of IDA and COLD WAR: FATHERLAND follows Nobel Prize-winning author Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler, KINGS OF THE ROAD) and his actress daughter Erika (Sandra Hüller, ANATOMY OF A FALL) as they drive across a war-ravaged 1949 Germany. Returning home after years of exile in the U.S. and exuding a superhuman gravitas, Mann finds the Germany he knew to be gone, replaced by a country with contradictory ideologies. Erika, who acts as his travel coordinator and translator, strives to pierce his detached persona while quietly struggling with a family tragedy.

title: ...a pozdravuji vlaštovky (...And Give My Love tothe Swallows)
description: ...a pozdravuji vlaštovky (...And Give My Love to the Swallows). 1972. Czechoslovakia. Directed by Jaromil Jireš. Screenplay by Jireš and Zora Beráková. With Magdalena Vášáryová, Viera Strnisková, Július Vašek. 35mm, courtesy Národní filmový archiv. In Czech; English subtitles. 86 min. This biopic of the last days of Marie Kudeříková, a 22-year-old Czechoslovak antifascist resistance fighter executed by the Nazis, was directed by New Wave filmmaker Jaromil Jireš (The Joke) after the Soviet occupation. As a work of hagiography, it was conceived and released in the first years of normalization to celebrate the bravery of communist antifascists at a time when, in government, party members were disgracing themselves. An aura of mournful defeat hangs over the film, with Jireš’s once-manic style dialed back as he maps out a dreary prison routine. Magda Vášáryová plays Kudeříková less as a martyr than as a girl groping at an adult political reality, goofing around with fellow prisoners between brutal interrogations. As the film shows, even that freedom will eventually be extinguished.

title: RAISE THE RED LANTERN
description: Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father’s death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul. Newly restored, RAISE THE RED LANTERN remains a landmark of Fifth Generation Chinese cinema and 1990s international film. The 4K restoration of RAISE THE RED LANTERN was carried out by the Udine Far East Film Festival on the occasion of its 26th edition. The original image and sound negatives were used under the supervision of Director Zhang Yimou. The vintage positive copy, presented at the 1991 Venice International Film Festival and preserved at the Venice Biennale's Historical Archive of Contemporary Arts, was used for color reference. The restoration was made in 2024 at L'Immagine Ritrovata (Hong Kong – Bologna).

title: Filipiñana
description: Isabel, a 17-year-old from the rural north of the Philippines, works at an elite country club outside Manila, lining up golf balls for powerful men. New to the job of tee-girl, she wanders the immaculate grounds sampling the club’s luxuries as its members engage in a complex dance with the doting and subservient staff. But something is rotting beneath the pristine fairways, as Isabel discovers when she tries to return a mislaid golf club to its patriarchal director, Dr. Palanca. The deeper she journeys into its most exclusive corners, the closer she gets to the violent truths of the club, her native Philippines, and her own past. The debut feature from Rafael Manuel, it won the World Cinema Dramatic Special Jury Award for Creative Vision at Sundance 2026 and reveals a major new filmmaking talent.

title: GERMANY, YEAR ZERO
description: Following the international acclaim and box office success of ROME, OPEN CITY and PAISAN, Rossellini took the first of many obstreperous swerves that would come to define his career. His next film would be another dispatch from war-torn Europe, with scenes playing out amidst the rubble with unvarnished immediacy, with unfamiliar and nonprofessional actors populating the cast—but this time, the protagonists would not be resistance fighters liberating Italy, but the defeated Germans muddling through their wasteland reich. Financed largely by the French government, GERMANY, YEAR ZERO became an experiment in radical empathy and its limits, casting about for signs of new life in a nation of crooks, unrepentant Nazis, and pederasts. The only innocent soul is twelve-year-old protagonist Edmund, who cannot qualify for a work permit, but must somehow earn a living to support his household. Even the child recognizes that he has no role models in this world: his brother is a mopey ex-soldier who refuses to register for a ration card, his father is an invalid who muses he’d be better off dead, his neighbors are coarse and severe, his friends are common swindlers, and his former school teacher still preaches that the strong must snuff out the weak. Unsentimental in the extreme and devoid of any comic relief, GERMANY YEAR ZERO plays like a seance for souls who have yet to recognize themselves as the walking dead.

title: FROM DUSK TILL DAWN
description: Two robbers take a man and his kids hostage. Racing to the US-Mexico border, the captors rendezvous at a cantina — not knowing it is a vampire den.

title: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping
description: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping will revisit the world of Panem twenty-four years before the events of The Hunger Games, starting on the morning of the reaping of the Fiftieth Hunger Games, also known as the Second Quarter Quell.

title: Paper Tiger 35mm
description: In James Gray’s deeply felt and intense drama, two brothers become entangled in a scheme that turns out to be too good to be true. As they try to navigate their way through the dangerous world of the Russian mafia, family bonds begin to fray with life-altering consequences.

title: Autumn Sonata
description: Ingmar and Ingrid, Bergman and Bergman, together at last. Sweden’s most popular export before the Volvo, in her final screen role, plays a world-renowned concert pianist who returns home to reunite with her now-married daughter (Liv Ullmann), long a distant second to her mother’s career ambitions, the two women exhuming old resentments and struggling towards reconciliation over the course of an emotionally draining 24 hours. “So unrelenting, so harrowing, that I walked out of the theater on shaking legs. If you’re open to the experience that Bergman means to provide, you may leave the film muttering a wrung-out ‘Whew!’ followed quickly by an appreciative ‘Wow!’” —Richard Corliss, Time Magazine Part of The Leaves Are Falling

title: Wicker
description: On the outskirts of a village by the sea, lives a Fisherwoman; smelly, single and perpetually ridiculed. One day, fed up with her stuffy, small-minded neighbors, she commissions herself a husband to be made from wicker. In an otherwise conservative town, this unconventional romance sparks outrage, jealousy and chaos.

title: Primetime
description: Inspired by true events in 2006, "To Catch a Predator" host Chris Hansen sets out to make television history. But when a high-stakes operation goes fatally wrong, his veneered dream of fame curdles into a nightmare.

title: Naza
description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them. We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA ’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence. — Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

title: Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut
description: Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, The Devils lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. The restoration many believed would never happen reaffirms Russell’s incendiary masterpiece as among the most overwhelming and uncompromising achievements in British cinema. Assembled from original camera negative, this 4k restoration is Ken Russell’s 2004 preferred edit. Picture and sound restoration by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: Wild Horse Nine
description: Set in 1973, during the US’s attempt to overthrow the Chilean government, a hitman for the US government with connections to the JFK assassination suddenly realizes that his own people have put a hit on him to cover up the mess.

title: ONCE UPON A TIME IN HARLEM
description: August 1972: A reunion of Harlem Renaissance luminaries is held at Duke Ellington’s St. Nicholas Ave. townhouse. Though many of these figures haven’t seen each other in 50 years, sharp memories, vigorous debates, and unsettled scores soon flow through this stunner of a cocktail party, which features (among others): artists Romare Bearden, Aaron Douglas, and Richard Bruce Nugent; composer Eubie Blake; poet Arna Bontemps; photographer James Van Der Zee; and activists Richard B. Moore and Louise Patterson. After organizing and shooting this extraordinary gathering, filmmaker William Greaves (SYMBIOPSYCHOTAXIPLASM: TAKE ONE) was unable to complete the film before his death in 2014. One of the cameramen that day was his son David, who expertly reshaped this never-before-seen, newly-restored footage into “a film for the ages…one of the greatest cinematic works of creative nonfiction that I’ve ever seen.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker

title: The Adventures of Prince Achmed
description: This performance will feature a live score performed by Hugo Max . Lotte Reiniger’s The Adventures of Prince Achmed is an enchanting amalgamation of stories from the Arabian Nights animated in cut paper silhouettes, an exquisite artefact of Weimar Cinema and a genre-defying experiment in melding international folk art traditions with the technical possibilities of a new medium. Taken from The Arabian Nights, a wicked sorcerer and the beautiful prince Achmed battle one another in a series of wondrous adventures. Please view this YouTube video for a sample of Hugo's work.

title: Wildwood
description: The Portland-set story follows Prue McKeel, who enters an enchanted wonderland when her baby brother Mac is taken by a murder of crows into the forest’s depths.

title: American Doctor (18)
description: Emmy Award-winning documentarian and journalist Poh Si Teng follow three American medics to Gaza as they volunteer in hospitals facing bombardment, shortages and danger.

title: Wild Horse Nine (15) (AD)
description: Two eccentric CIA agents ( John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell ) await orders on Easter Island, on the cusp of yet another military coup in Martin McDonagh 's latest dark comedy.

title: Ebenezer: A Christmas Carol
description: A thrilling ghost story set in Dickens' London, following one man's supernatural journey to face his past, present and future as he fights for a second chance at redemption.

title: DOV’È LA LIBERTÀ?
description: Incarcerated for twenty-two years after committing a crime of passion, Salvatore Lojacono (Totò) wins parole and returns to a Rome that he scarcely recognizes—and ultimately decides that prison is preferable. Salvatore learns the hard way that business, romance, and family are all elaborate rackets; even the most sympathetic victim he encounters is just on the hunt for a tax swap. His disenchantment is recounted in flashback, as he begs a judge to lock him back up. (The courtroom scenes were, in fact, shot later by Mario Monicelli, after Rossellini abandoned the project in mid-production, and effectively bridged the patchwork of episodes left behind.) The popular Neapolitan comedian Totò gets plenty of opportunities to mug, but also flexes his dramatic muscles as a man who trusts too tenderly. The scenario was inspired by Chaplin’s MODERN TIMES, but the moral vision is closer to MONSIEUR VERDOUX, another comedy born of the recognition that post-war society has been stripped of sentimental illusions and re-organized under principles of ruthless capitalism indistinguishable from the barbarism it displaced. “It stupefied me with its cruelty and bitterness,” wrote Pierre Kast in Cahiers du Cinema, long a bastion of Rossellini apologetics. “It’s a parable of the purest Swiftian type, unpitying and almost intolerable.”

title: NAZA (15)
description: Cloaked in darkness on the rooftops of Tel Aviv, Israeli journalist Yuval Abraham conducts shattering one-on-one interviews with Israeli soldiers and intelligence personnel.

title: AMERICAN DOCTOR
description: Three American physicians share an oath to save lives, and a determination that their responsibility to Gaza will not end when they leave. title: FAMILY PORTRAITS
description: Here the filmmakers create portraits of their parents, children, siblings, or other relatives, with the resultant films – not surprisingly – proving especially lyrical, emotional, and poetic in their contemplation of aging and loss. Edward Owens REMEMBRANCE: A PORTRAIT STUDY (1967, 6 min, 16mm) Edward Owens PRIVATE IMAGININGS AND NARRATIVE FACTS (1968-70, 9 min, 16mm, silent) Robert Beavers PITCHER OF COLORED LIGHT (2000-07, 23 min, 16mm) Gunvor Nelson TIME BEING (1991, 8 min, 16mm, silent) Friedl vom Gröller PARENTS: MOTHER, FATHER / ELTERN: MUTTER, VATER (1997-99, 6 min, 16mm, silent) Friedl vom Gröller NEC SPE, NEC METU (2013, 4 min, 16mm, silent) Guy Sherwin SHORT FILM SERIES: PORTRAIT WITH PARENTS (1974, 3 min, 16mm) Gunvor Nelson MY NAME IS OONA (1969, 10 min, 16mm) Paige Taul 10:28,30 (2019, 4.5 min, 16mm-to-DCP) Viktoria Schmid KATHARINAVIKTORIA (2011, 1 min, 16mm-to-DCP) Viktoria Schmid KATHARINAVIKTORIA 2(021) (2022, 1 min, 16mm) Total running time: 80 min.

title: THE UMBRELLAS OF CHERBOURG
description:
They are young, in love and certain they will wait for each other. Then Guy is sent to Algeria, Geneviève discovers she is pregnant, and the future begins asking questions their romance cannot answer.
Every line is sung, every colour seems to carry a feeling, and Michel Legrand’s music makes ordinary heartbreak soar. Jacques Demy and Catherine Deneuve create a world of ravishing surfaces without protecting their characters from money, time or compromise. A musical of overwhelming beauty whose greatest surprise is how clear-eyed it is about love.

title: Dívka na koštěti (The Girl on the Broomstick)
description: Dívka na koštěti (The Girl on the Broomstick). 1971. Czechoslovakia. Directed by Václav Vorlíček. Screenplay by Vorlíček, Hermína Franková, Miloš Macourek. With Petra Černocká, Jan Hrušínský, Jan Kraus. 4K digitization by Národní filmový archiv; courtesy Národní filmový archiv. In Czech; English subtitles. 76 min. A teenage witch slips out of fairy-tale land into contemporary Czechoslovakia in this deliriously plastic, candy-colored comedic predecessor to Sabrina the Teenage Witch. By 1972, director Václav Vorlíček had already made two classic films from scripts by Miloš Macourek and had proven himself a good fit for the normalization authorities; allegedly he would later be registered as a collaborator with the secret police. For all its wonders, The Girl on the Broomstick does represent a domestication of the energies of the New Wave, which Vorlíček repackages here as politically safe entertainment. And yet it remains a classic, overflowing with odd, off-kilter comedy and delightful performances, not least by the indelible Vladimír Menšík. Its loungey, anarchic rhythms today seem closer to Frank Tashlin and Jerry Lewis than to anything else produced in Czechoslovakia, then or now.

title: ZORN III
description: Mathieu Amalric ZORN III (2018-2022) 2022, 82 min, DCP. With John Zorn and Barbara Hannigan. “Why can’t Mathieu Amalric stop filming John Zorn? It’s because consciously or unconsciously, he understands that he can only get closer to this man if he imitates his restlessness. It’s this Sisyphean tirelessness, the fact that we must imagine Zorn (whose surname translates into German as anger) as a happy man, which is at the core of his art. He makes music in order to be alive. This time, however, Zorn is not the only protagonist, as the Canadian soprano Barbara Hannigan enters the wild world of the composer. Much more straightforward than its previous iterations, the film captures Hannigan’s rehearsals for a performance of Zorn’s song cycle ‘Jumalattaret’ together with pianist Stephen Gosling. The work pushes her vocal capacities to the limit, with the sudden shifts in register, extended high notes and bird-like chirping demanding everything from her.” –Patrick Holzapfel, VIENNALE

Thirty-four days before she is due to begin her prison sentence for fraud, the Theranos founder invites Fielder and fellow filmmaker Lance Oppenheim into the home she shares with her partner, Billy Evans....

title: Queen at Sea
description: Queen at Sea. 2026. UK/USA. Written and directed by Lance Hammer. With Juliette Binoche, Tom Courtenay, Anna Calder-Marshall, Florence Hunt. DCP courtesy Greenwich Entertainment. In English, French; English subtitles. 121 min. Is there anything more pleasurable than watching seasoned actors in a film worthy of their talents and intelligence? In Queen at Sea, Anna Calder-Marshall plays a woman afflicted with dementia, her body and mind slowly and irreversibly deteriorating, whose loss for words and loss of agency causes a bitter rift between her daughter (Juliette Binoche) and her devoted second husband (Tom Courtenay). The impossible moral agony they face—one that lays bare the most sacred intimacies of a marriage—is limned with exquisite candor and subtlety, so much so that we long to have witnessed the mirror images of Calder-Marshall and Courtenay when they were actors in the prime of their youth—she the Ophelia to his Hamlet on the British stage in 1968. We feel grateful, as well, for the return of the American writer-director Lance Hammer, some 18 years after Ballast, who graces us once again with a film of immeasurable compassion and unsettling ambivalence. title: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth
description: Brad Pitt returns to his Academy Award-winning role as Cliff Booth, only this time it’s 1977 and it’s a very different Hollywood. Directed by David Fincher from a screenplay by Quentin Tarantino, the film also stars Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Carla Gugino, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II and Peter Weller. (Netflix)

title: PLANES, TRAINS AND AUTOMOBILES
description: Steve Martin and John Candy star in John Hughes’ classic tale of holiday travel gone awry. Neal Page (Martin) is an uptight advertising executive trying to get home to Chicago for Thanksgiving. When his flight is rerouted to Wichita, he reluctantly partners with Del Griffith (Candy), an obnoxious yet lovable salesman. Together, they embark on a cross-country adventure that includes various modes of transportation, hilarious mishaps and unforgettable rental car shenanigans.

title: GENERAL DELLA ROVERE
description: Based on the true story of Italian cavalry officer Giovanni Bertone during World War II, GENERAL DELLA ROVERE recounts the unexpected moral evolution of Emanuele Bardone (Vittorio de Sica), an ingratiating swindler with a talent for improvising novel solutions to the dilemmas he has sprung on himself. Alas, even when Bardone wins, he feels compelled to double-down and gamble away his momentary advantage. He has a talent for extracting favors from the Nazi officers in Genoa, and when the law catches up to Bardone, he’s offered a bargain: go to prison and imitate the Italian general Della Rovere, in hopes of penetrating his resistance network. De Sica’s big and boisterous performance anchors the film, and renders this somber story of ethical compromise into an improbable crowdpleaser. Rossellini considered GENERAL DELLA ROVERE an embarrassing capitulation, a work-for-hire to demonstrate that he could, under duress, follow a script and a schedule. Shot quickly on studio sets with some undisguised rear projection footage, GENERAL DELLA ROVERE went on to win the Golden Lion at the Venice Film Festival and revitalize Rossellini’s career after a decade of box office setbacks. Like Bardone, Rossellini always had another trick up his sleeve.

Fjord
description: Mihai and Lisbet Gheorghiu, a Romanian-Norwegian Pentecostal couple, move with their five children from Romania to Norway after Mihai’s parents die, seeking closeness to Lisbet’s family, who share their faith. Settling in an isolated coastal village, they form a bond with their neighbors, the Halbergs. When their daughter Elia appears at school with bruises, suspicions arise about the family's strict religious upbringing. Fjord explores clashing worldviews, conformity, tolerance, and the boundaries of freedom and intimacy.

title: Off-Circuit: My Wife Cries
description: A phone call brings Thomas to a hospital, where he finds his wife Carla in tears. As the circumstances of her accident come into focus, so too does a relationship whose familiar terms suddenly seem uncertain. From this deceptively simple premise, Angela Schanelec constructs a relationship drama that resists the conventions of the genre in favour of something decidedly more elliptical. As conversations circle what remains unspoken; gestures and silences come increasingly to the fore with a spellbinding intensity. My Wife Cries is at once formally audacious and acutely attentive to the emotional lives of its characters and how quickly intimacy can give way to estrangement. The screening on Friday 20 November will be followed by an in-person Q&A with Angela Schanelec.

title: Focker-in-Law
description: A young man named Henry, son of Greg and Pam Focker, faces family chaos when he decides to marry a strong-willed woman who appears to be his complete mismatch.

title: The Devils
description: All screenings on a new 35mm print of the 4K restoration of the film. An enduring, singular masterpiece of cinema starring Academy Award-winner Vanessa Redgrave and Oliver Reed, KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption – and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell. Assembled from the original camera negative, this new 4K restoration presents Ken Russell’s definitive vision of The Devils by referencing the edit he privately constructed in 2004. The film’s sound has been remastered from original English Composite 35mm Mag Film, transferred at 96kHz, plus other original film elements in selected spots as needed. The Picture and Sound restoration was performed by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color, and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: WHO ARE YOU, POLLY MAGGOO?
description:
A television crew wants to discover the real Polly Maggoo. The fashion industry wants an image. Admirers want a fantasy. Somewhere inside the competing demands is a young American model who keeps slipping out of the frame.
Photographer William Klein turns his insider’s eye on the absurd theatre of fashion and celebrity. Metallic couture, mock-documentary interviews and surreal interruptions make a wickedly funny pop-art assault on the business of manufacturing personalities. A sixties satire whose question has only become more pointed: who gets to decide what an image means?

title: Josephine
description: Winner of the Grand Jury Prize Dramatic and the Audience Award at the Sundance Film Festival, Josephine is a gripping drama that doesn’t shy away from using aspects of genre filmmaking to tackle a story of deep emotional heft. Writer-director Beth de Araújo’s sophomore feature is a deeply personal story, rooted in the filmmaker's own childhood experience of interrupting a sexual assault in Golden Gate Park with her father. It stars Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan as the parents of eight-year-old Josephine (played by extraordinary newcomer Mason Reeves), whose childhood is marred when she witnesses a violent sexual assault. As she struggles to process what she’s seen, her once-safe world begins to descend into a scary place for a child who does not yet possess the tools to adequately express herself. Desperate and conflicted about how to help their little girl, her parents argue over the moral quandary of having their daughter testify in front of a jury to convict a sexual predator, which demands an extremely high cost, both emotionally and psychologically, especially for Josephine. At the heart of the film is newcomer Mason Reeves, making her striking feature film debut as Josephine. Reeves brings an extraordinary naturalism to the role, subtly illustrating a child who has to grapple with very adult themes far before she needs to. De Araújo's unwavering eye profoundly captures an intimate story of trauma and the ways it reverberates through a family.

title: MUSIC IS MUSIC + BEFORE IT'S TOO LATE
description: Mathieu Amalric MUSIC IS MUSIC 2017, 20 min, DCP “In a poetic composition of song, narration, and images, this film follows Canadian soprano and orchestra conductor Barbara Hannigan, accompanied by the Ludwig Orchestra, as she records her album ‘Crazy Girl Crazy’. Why did she choose these three pieces, in essence so different, but which intimately resonate with her: Berio’s ‘Sequenza III’, Berg’s ‘Lulu Suite’, and Gershwin’s ‘Girl Crazy’?” –INTERNATIONAL FESTIVAL OF FILMS ON ART Mathieu Amalric BEFORE IT’S TOO LATE / AVANT QU’IL NE SOIT TROP TARD 2023, 65 min, DCP “After 47 years together, the Emerson String Quartet records their last album, ‘Infinite Voyage’, in three days. For this farewell, they invited soprano Barbara Hannigan, and a film was born. Their precise work, the moments of enthusiasm and fear, the research and the jokes, the age limit of these men and Hannigan’s flamboyance, the admiring friendship full of irony and rigor, the profession and yet the discovery, humor as a cog towards concentration, the individual and the group…all this composes a portrait of the usually invisible production of music. Before everyone resumes their path.” –DOCLISBOA Total running time: ca. 90 min.

title: Naza
description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them. We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA ’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence. — Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

title: La Bola Negra
description: Explores what it means to be gay throughout different eras, focusing on "three existences" that are connected through themes of sexuality, desire, pain, and inheritance.

title: Raise the Red Lantern
description: Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father's death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul. Zhang Yimou’s masterpiece Raise the Red Lantern has been fully restored in 4K.

title: PAISAN
description: The story of Italy’s liberation, told in six episodes, traveling from the first Allied landing in Sicily to the battle of the Po Delta, PAISAN demonstrated that OPEN CITY had been no fluke. Conceived on a vaster scale, with a considerably higher budget, and international distribution from MGM, PAISAN is a national epic that still startles for its immediacy, its technical mastery, its unpredictable rhythms. Scenes of unbearable suspense on the streets of Florence alternate with lighter fare, such as the doctrinal scuffles between Italian monks and American chaplains in Romagna. Stitched together like a newsreel (and skillfully edited to blend in stock footage and suggest off-screen pyrotechnics with creative sound effects), PAISAN became a worldwide sensation, an intellectual action film that pictured recent history with an unprecedented heft and scope. The film became a lodestar for filmmakers from Gillo Pontecorvo to Martin Scorsese, with the latter remarking, “The result... is still startling: it’s like seeing reality itself unfolding before your eyes.”

title: La Bola Negra
description: Spain, 1932. A young man seeks admission to the local casino. In 1937, a conscripted nationalist soldier stands guard over a Republican prisoner. In 2017, a former playwright inherits an unexpected document from his grandfather. Through a dazzlingly constructed and performed triptych, La Bola Negra traces the hidden connections between three men separated by time but bound by experience and the way in which queer lives, memories and histories endure across generations.

title: Blade Runner : The Final Cut
description: Deckard (Harrison Ford) is forced by the police Boss (M. Emmet Walsh) to continue his old job as Replicant Hunter. His assignment: eliminate four escaped Replicants from the colonies who have returned to Earth. Before starting the job, Deckard goes to the Tyrell Corporation and he meets Rachel (Sean Young), a Replicant girl he falls in love with.

title: Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut
description: Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, The Devils lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. The restoration many believed would never happen reaffirms Russell’s incendiary masterpiece as among the most overwhelming and uncompromising achievements in British cinema. Assembled from original camera negative, this 4k restoration is Ken Russell’s 2004 preferred edit. Picture and sound restoration by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: ONCE UPON A TIME IN HARLEM
description: August 1972: A reunion of Harlem Renaissance luminaries is held at Duke Ellington’s St. Nicholas Ave. townhouse. Though many of these figures haven’t seen each other in 50 years, sharp memories, vigorous debates, and unsettled scores soon flow through this stunner of a cocktail party, which features (among others): artists Romare Bearden, Aaron Douglas, and Richard Bruce Nugent; composer Eubie Blake; poet Arna Bontemps; photographer James Van Der Zee; and activists Richard B. Moore and Louise Patterson. After organizing and shooting this extraordinary gathering, filmmaker William Greaves (SYMBIOPSYCHOTAXIPLASM: TAKE ONE) was unable to complete the film before his death in 2014. One of the cameramen that day was his son David, who expertly reshaped this never-before-seen, newly-restored footage into “a film for the ages…one of the greatest cinematic works of creative nonfiction that I’ve ever seen.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker

title: ALL OF A SUDDEN
description: In the latest film by Oscar®-winning director Ryûsuke Hamaguchi (DRIVE MY CAR), Virginie Efira (BENEDETTA) stars as Marie-Lou, the progressive director of a nursing home in the Parisian suburbs. Her life changes when she meets Mari (Tao Okamoto), Japanese playwright. As the two women reckon with the lives they have lived, they find new ways to make sense of the time that remains. Following caregivers as they navigate the tensions between idealism and pragmatism, Hamaguchi crafts a film that rests fully in the present, attentive to the delicate unfolding of thought, feeling, and human connection.
