description: Isabel, a 17-year-old from the rural north of the Philippines, works at an elite country club outside Manila, lining up golf balls for powerful men. New to the job of tee-girl, she wanders the immaculate grounds sampling the club’s luxuries as its members engage in a complex dance with the doting and subservient staff. But something is rotting beneath the pristine fairways, as Isabel discovers when she tries to return a mislaid golf club to its patriarchal director, Dr. Palanca. The deeper she journeys into its most exclusive corners, the closer she gets to the violent truths of the club, her native Philippines, and her own past. The debut feature from Rafael Manuel, it won the World Cinema Dramatic Special Jury Award for Creative Vision at Sundance 2026 and reveals a major new filmmaking talent.

description: When Sally (Marilyn Burns) hears that her grandfather's grave may have been vandalized, she and her paraplegic brother, Franklin (Paul A. Partain), set out with their friends to investigate. After a detour to their family's old farmhouse, they discover a group of crazed, murderous outcasts living next door. As the group is attacked one by one by the chainsaw-wielding Leatherface (Gunnar Hansen), who wears a mask of human skin, the survivors must do everything they can to escape.

title: The Devils
description: All screenings on a new 35mm print of the 4K restoration of the film. An enduring, singular masterpiece of cinema starring Academy Award-winner Vanessa Redgrave and Oliver Reed, KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption – and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell. Assembled from the original camera negative, this new 4K restoration presents Ken Russell’s definitive vision of The Devils by referencing the edit he privately constructed in 2004. The film’s sound has been remastered from original English Composite 35mm Mag Film, transferred at 96kHz, plus other original film elements in selected spots as needed. The Picture and Sound restoration was performed by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color, and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: Josephine
description: JOSEPHINE follows the psychological fallout after eight-year-old Josephine (Reeves) witnesses a brutal crime in Golden Gate Park. As she acts out, her parents (Tatum and Chan) struggle with helping their daughter cope, while facing the moral responsibility of demanding justice in a world that’s lost its innocence. Open Fri Nov 20, more showtimes to be announced.

title: RAISE THE RED LANTERN
description: Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father’s death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul. Newly restored, RAISE THE RED LANTERN remains a landmark of Fifth Generation Chinese cinema and 1990s international film. The 4K restoration of RAISE THE RED LANTERN was carried out by the Udine Far East Film Festival on the occasion of its 26th edition. The original image and sound negatives were used under the supervision of Director Zhang Yimou. The vintage positive copy, presented at the 1991 Venice International Film Festival and preserved at the Venice Biennale's Historical Archive of Contemporary Arts, was used for color reference. The restoration was made in 2024 at L'Immagine Ritrovata (Hong Kong – Bologna).

What begins as an intimate portrait of an enigmatic felon becomes a mind-bending three-year journey into the abyss. From boundary-pushing directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim comes You Can See Everything .

description: Set in 1973, during the US’s attempt to overthrow the Chilean government, a hitman for the US government with connections to the JFK assassination suddenly realizes that his own people have put a hit on him to cover up the mess.

title: A Talent for Murder
description: A mysterious young man from a New York publisher is sent to Switzerland to persuade the renowned writer Patricia Highsmith to write one final installment of the Ripley anthology.

title: Wicker
description: On the outskirts of a village by the sea, lives a Fisherwoman; smelly, single and perpetually ridiculed. One day, fed up with her stuffy, small-minded neighbors, she commissions herself a husband to be made from wicker. In an otherwise conservative town, this unconventional romance sparks outrage, jealousy and chaos.

title: Naza
description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them. We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA ’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence. — Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

title: ROME, OPEN CITY
description: Rome, winter 1943: as screeching-tired Gestapo dragnets blanket the “open city,” Resistance leader Marcello Pagliero escapes from his apartment by running across the rooftops (as did co-screenwriter Sergio Amidei in real life), as pregnant widow Anna Magnani prepares for her wedding, parish priest Aldo Fabrizi uses the “frying pan method” to hide the local boys’ bomb brigade’s hardware, and effete Major Harry Feist riffles through his collection of incriminating ID photos—but betrayal, a broad-daylight machine-gunning, a Partisan ambush, blowtorch torture, and death by firing squad loom… Based on actual people and all-too-recent incidents (Magnani’s electrifying final scene was inspired by her enraged pursuit of her boyfriends’s escape by truck); written in a week in Federico Fellini’s kitchen (the only place with heat); shot on a number of the real locations, and cast mainly with non-pros (Fabrizi and second-choice Magnani were already famous, albeit for comedy), OPEN CITY’s documentary look and still hair-raising violence rocked audiences and critics around the world, making Neo-Realism, Rossellini, and Magnani world-famous, sharing the top prize at Cannes, and running twenty-one consecutive months at a single New York cinema. 4K Restoration courtesy Janus Films. 35mm print courtesy Cinecittà.

title: The Last Waltz - 50th Anniversary
description: Seventeen years after joining forces as the backing band for rockabilly cult hero Ronnie Hawkins, Canadian roots rockers The Band call it quits with a lavish farewell show at San Francisco's Winterland Ballroom on Nov. 25, 1976. Filmed by Martin Scorsese, this documentary features standout performances by rock legends such as Bob Dylan, Neil Young, Van Morrison, Eric Clapton, Joni Mitchell and Muddy Waters, as well as interviews tracing the group's history and discussing road life.

title: Ebenezer: A Christmas Carol
description: A thrilling ghost story set in Dickens' London, following one man's supernatural journey to face his past, present and future as he fights for a second chance at redemption.

title: Ginger Snaps
description: “I get this ache... And I, I thought it was for sex, but it's to tear everything to fucking pieces.” A wild and bloodthirsty hound has ravaged through the small town of Bailey Downs, attacking the neighbourhood's pet dogs. When the two teenage outcasts, the Fitzgerald sisters, stumble upon the creature one night, their lives change forever as Ginger is bitten, and her body starts to change. A true feast of practical effects, 2000s grunge, and snappy one-liners; Ginger Snaps has been credited in hindsight as a predecessor to the “maneater” supernatural woman most famously seen in Jennifer´s Body (2009). A coming-of-age story told in a fresh perspective; for maybe the true terror lies in growing up, or maybe it lies in the bloodthirsty hound who calls herself your sister. Ginger Snaps is featured as part of MANEATERS, a season exploring the female supernatural on screen. The season is presented with the National Film and Television School’s Film Studies, Programming and Curation MA.

description: When a terrifying creature rises from the Han River and brings chaos to Seoul, single dad Gang-du (Song Kang-ho, Parasite) will stop at nothing to rescue his daughter from the clutches of the horrifying Host. Equal parts creature-feature thrill ride and poignant human story, Oscar-winning visionary Bong Joon Ho’s first global smash remains an incredible action drama and propulsively entertaining modern classic . “A thing of beauty, the perfect mixture of the silly and the grave.” – The New Yorker

title: ALL OF A SUDDEN
description: In the latest film by Oscar®-winning director Ryûsuke Hamaguchi (DRIVE MY CAR), Virginie Efira (BENEDETTA) stars as Marie-Lou, the progressive director of a nursing home in the Parisian suburbs. Her life changes when she meets Mari (Tao Okamoto), Japanese playwright. As the two women reckon with the lives they have lived, they find new ways to make sense of the time that remains. Following caregivers as they navigate the tensions between idealism and pragmatism, Hamaguchi crafts a film that rests fully in the present, attentive to the delicate unfolding of thought, feeling, and human connection.

He builds a movement to protect their land, preserving the ecosystem and centuries of ecological knowledge. Facing threats from global agribusiness, m...

title: OVER THE EDGE
description:
New Granada has houses, roads and a bright suburban future. It has almost nothing for its teenagers. Boredom becomes solidarity, solidarity becomes defiance, and the adults discover that treating young people as a problem can make their fears come true.
Jonathan Kaplan’s cult youth film catches adolescence with unusual sympathy and bite. A young Matt Dillon, a remarkable rock soundtrack and the unruly energy of its cast make rebellion feel exhilarating before the consequences land. A suburban pressure cooker that refuses to dismiss the kids as either innocents or delinquents.

As a child’s train set magically comes to life and the engines race to become the fastest in the world, Rusty the steam train has little hope of winning until he is inspired by the legend of the ‘Starlight Express’. A show seen around the world by over 30 million people, and with music by Andrew Lloyd Webber and lyrics by Richard Stilgoe, ANDREW LLOYD WEBBER'S STARLIGHT EXPRESS - LIVE ON STAGE is an electrifying experience for all ages.

title: EUROPA '51
description: Shortly after completing THE FLOWERS OF ST. FRANCIS, Rossellini seized upon a hypothetical: if Francis himself appeared in Europe today and preached his humble doctrine, he would be promptly thrown in an insane asylum. Augmented by ideas derived from Simone Weil and Herbert Marcuse, Rossellini’s thought experiment grew and grew until it became EUROPA ’51, a sweeping state-of-the-continent address aimed at the complacency of post-war society. Luckily, Rossellini retained the services of his wife to put a box office spin on this dense rumination. (It would become, ironically, the only one of their pictures together to do any business in Italy.) Irene Gerard (Ingrid Bergman) is a socialite who’s more focused on throwing a good dinner party than attending to the needs of her young son. When the boy kills himself, Irene’s world is shattered: what could drive a child to so thoroughly reject life, and what can she make of the life that remains? Inspired by her cousin’s commitment to the class struggle, Irene begins devoting her time to Rome’s downtrodden. After all, the sick, the dying, and the poor need her more than her husband (Alexander Knox) ever could, do they not? Is Bergman preaching Communist revolution, Christian neighborliness, or some obscure, hyper-personal fusion of the two? Disarmingly literal and unspeakably sincere in its spiritual crusade, EUROPA ‘51 remains the most mysterious of Bergman and Rossellini’s collaborations.

title: FATHERLAND
description: From the director of IDA and COLD WAR: FATHERLAND follows Nobel Prize-winning author Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler, KINGS OF THE ROAD) and his actress daughter Erika (Sandra Hüller, ANATOMY OF A FALL) as they drive across a war-ravaged 1949 Germany. Returning home after years of exile in the U.S. and exuding a superhuman gravitas, Mann finds the Germany he knew to be gone, replaced by a country with contradictory ideologies. Erika, who acts as his travel coordinator and translator, strives to pierce his detached persona while quietly struggling with a family tragedy.

description: Mihai and Lisbet Gheorghiu, a Romanian-Norwegian Pentecostal couple, move with their five children from Romania to Norway after Mihai’s parents die, seeking closeness to Lisbet’s family, who share their faith. Settling in an isolated coastal village, they form a bond with their neighbors, the Halbergs. When their daughter Elia appears at school with bruises, suspicions arise about the family's strict religious upbringing. Fjord explores clashing worldviews, conformity, tolerance, and the boundaries of freedom and intimacy.

title: Solve Along A Murder She Wrote
description: Cult hit event Solve-Along-A-Murder-She-Wrote returns to the Prince Charles Cinema with an interactive screening of a classic Murder, She Wrote episode. Watch as Cabot Cove gets caught up in a murder mystery only JB Fletcher (or you!) can solve! Solve-Along-A-Murder-She-Wrote is a unique and hilarious night featuring games, prizes and audience participation, with special permission from NBC Universal Television. See the show Time Out rated one of 2021 and 2019’s 50 Great Nights Out in London that has played to sell-out audiences across the UK and Australia. Hosted by super-fan Tim Benzie, Solve-Along-A-Murder-She-Wrote features: * A race to solve to the crime, via the Fameometer and the Suspiciometer! * A Cabot Cove quiz! * A singalong to the theme tune with new lyrics! * Clips and biogs of the campy guest stars! Tim Benzie is obsessed with Murder, She Wrote, having watched the original series when it was first broadcast, and now relishing the repeats on television everywhere. Tim is the writer/performer of “It’s a Mystery!”, all about our love of whodunnits. An award-winning playwright and co-writer of the Royal Vauxhall Tavern’s 2017-2023 pantos (‘Goosed’, ‘Rubbed’, ‘Slipped’, ‘Pricked’, ‘Cracked’ and ‘Tossed’). He is the co-producer of the camp club night PopHorror. Visit us at www.solvealongamurdershewrote.com , or follow us on Instagram, Twitter and Facebook @solvealonga. 2026 SCHEDULE: Thursday 26th November 2026 New episode TBC Thursday 17th December 2026 Encore screening - "A Christmas Secret" Directed by Anthony Pullen Shaw Starring Angela Lansbury, Larry Wilcox, Amy Brenneman 1992 | 120mins | USA *** The Critics speak! “You’ll be swept away with Jessica Fletcher feels … it has the BEST HOST.” - Time Out London "A cinematic, theatrical and hilarious experience ... title: YOU CAN SEE EVERYTHING
description: Elizabeth Holmes would like to tell her side of the story. Nathan Fielder has a few questions.  Thirty-four days before she is due to begin her prison sentence for fraud, the Theranos founder invites Fielder and fellow filmmaker Lance Oppenheim into the home she shares with her partner, Billy Evans....

title: SMOOTH TALK
description:
For Connie, summer means music, shopping trips and practising the person she wants to become. Then an older stranger pulls up outside her house while she is alone, and ordinary flirtation begins turning into something she cannot easily name—or escape.
Laura Dern and Treat Williams are extraordinary in Joyce Chopra’s adaptation of Joyce Carol Oates. Sunlit teenage restlessness gives way to a confrontation whose menace grows almost imperceptibly. The film understands the thrill of being seen and the terror of being claimed, making its shift from coming-of-age drama to psychological nightmare devastating.

title: Josephine
description: Winner of the Grand Jury Prize Dramatic and the Audience Award at the Sundance Film Festival, Josephine is a gripping drama that doesn’t shy away from using aspects of genre filmmaking to tackle a story of deep emotional heft. Writer-director Beth de Araújo’s sophomore feature is a deeply personal story, rooted in the filmmaker's own childhood experience of interrupting a sexual assault in Golden Gate Park with her father. It stars Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan as the parents of eight-year-old Josephine (played by extraordinary newcomer Mason Reeves), whose childhood is marred when she witnesses a violent sexual assault. As she struggles to process what she’s seen, her once-safe world begins to descend into a scary place for a child who does not yet possess the tools to adequately express herself. Desperate and conflicted about how to help their little girl, her parents argue over the moral quandary of having their daughter testify in front of a jury to convict a sexual predator, which demands an extremely high cost, both emotionally and psychologically, especially for Josephine. At the heart of the film is newcomer Mason Reeves, making her striking feature film debut as Josephine. Reeves brings an extraordinary naturalism to the role, subtly illustrating a child who has to grapple with very adult themes far before she needs to. De Araújo's unwavering eye profoundly captures an intimate story of trauma and the ways it reverberates through a family.

title: Planes, Trains & Automobiles
description: Easily excitable Neal Page (Steve Martin) is somewhat of a control freak. Trying to get home to Chicago to spend Thanksgiving with his wife (Laila Robins) and kids, his flight is rerouted to a distant city in Kansas because of a freak snowstorm, and his sanity begins to fray. Worse yet, he is forced to bunk up with talkative Del Griffith (John Candy), whom he finds extremely annoying. Together they must overcome the insanity of holiday travel to reach their intended destination.

title: Ben'imana
description: In 2012, eighteen years after the genocide against the Tutsi, a Rwandan village is still learning how to live with itself. Vénéranda has spent years helping survivors and the families of those responsible speak the words that were never said between them. However, forgiveness comes easier when it’s someone else’s story. When her own daughter’s future becomes entangled with the past, Vénéranda is forced to find her own words at last. Spanning three generations of women, BEN’IMANA is an intimate portrait of inherited silence — and the fragile question of whether people who have survived the unspeakable together can still build a life side by side.

title: The Devils
description: All screenings on a new 35mm print of the 4K restoration of the film. An enduring, singular masterpiece of cinema starring Academy Award-winner Vanessa Redgrave and Oliver Reed, KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption – and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell. Assembled from the original camera negative, this new 4K restoration presents Ken Russell’s definitive vision of The Devils by referencing the edit he privately constructed in 2004. The film’s sound has been remastered from original English Composite 35mm Mag Film, transferred at 96kHz, plus other original film elements in selected spots as needed. The Picture and Sound restoration was performed by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color, and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: PINOCCHIO
description: Disney’s second animated feature (after SNOW WHITE AND THE SEVEN DWARFS) and his most lavish, PINOCCHIO follows the adventures of animate puppet Pinocchio, in his quest to become a real boy. Featuring a host of memorable characters (Geppetto, Jiminy Cricket, the Blue Fairy, Figaro the Cat, Cleo the Goldfish, and Monstro the Whale, et al.), PINOCCHIO was the first animated feature to win competitive Academy Awards.

title: The Aristocats
description: A big-screen outing for this flight of feline fun from the Disney vaults, the last animated feature to be signed off on by Walt himself is a purr-fect Parisian period piece featuring a family of nose-in-the-air cats who, after being kidnapped away from the accustomed baronial splendor of their home, have to rely on the streetwise wiles of alley cat O’Malley to keep them safe. Featuring animation supremely attentive to the syntax of kitty motion and the vocal talents of Eva Gabor and Scatman Crothers who gets to lead on the boppin' classic “Everybody Wants to Be a Cat.” Part of It Started With A Mouse: Hand-Drawn Classics on 35

title: 14th
description: Please note that there are additional showtimes of 14TH that screen with open captions (on-screen display of dialogue and sounds). For those showtimes, click here. Written in the wreckage of the Civil War, the 14th Amendment was meant to codify the promise of freedom and citizenship. Instead, it has become a permanent argument. Oscar nominee DuVernay’s new documentary pulls this fight out of the footnotes and into the present, chronicling a vicious battle that has raged for more than 150 years. Threading deep archival scholarship with today’s headlines, 14TH brings together legal minds, politicians, historians and cultural voices to explore a question America still hasn’t settled: Who gets to belong?

title: Akira
description: Iconic and game-changing, AKIRA is the definitive anime masterpiece! Katsuhiro Otomo's landmark cyberpunk classic obliterated the boundaries of Japanese animation and forced the world to look into the future. AKIRA's arrival shattered traditional thinking, creating space for future generations of ground-breaking movies. July, 1988 - World War III breaks loose. Then, in 2019, in megalopolis Tokyo...As the leader of a group of young robust delinquents, Kaneda spent his nights tearing through the urban wastes, racing his motorbike against rival groups. One night while riding with his gang, his friend Tetsuo suddenly encounters a strange boy - the product of human experimentation and is injured in the ensuing crash. Shortly thereafter, a military squadron appears on the scene to take the boy and Tetsuo away to an army research facility. Determined to free Tetsuo from capture, Kaneda sneaks into the army research lab. However, a regimen of extreme experimental procedures has awakened a new power in his friend, and now he is consumed by madness..

title: Fjord
description: An immigrant Romanian family living in Norway is subject to an investigation and faces the scrutiny of the local judicial system.

title: Relaxed Screening: You Can See Everything (15) (AD)
description: 34 days before she’s sent to prison, notorious Silicon Valley founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a skeptical film crew led by Nathan Fielder to document her every move.

title: A Confucian Confusion
description: Art versus commerce, friendship versus status, independence versus conformity—values clash and collide in Edward Yang's study of an increasingly Westernized country heading into the twenty-first century without moral guideposts. Moving from breakout hit A Brighter Summer Day's investigation of the past to a critical survey of the present, A Confucian Confusion charts the tangled web of emotional and professional manipulations among a group of young urbanites. At its center is Molly (Ni Shu-chun), director of a floundering public-relations firm. Alienated by the childish fiancé (Bosen Wang) who bankrolls her enterprise—and frustrated by the demands of an assistant, Qiqi (Chen Shiang-chyi), and her own fiancé, Ming (Wang Wei-ming)—Molly lashes out at everyone in her path and threatens to dismantle the company altogether. Meanwhile (amid several other subplots), Molly's talk-show-host sister (Chen Li-mei) attempts to dissuade her separated husband from continuing to write a dark novel about the return of Confucius to a jaded modern society. Injecting comedic elements into his patented brand of earnest soul-searching, Yang finds humor as well as pathos in the desperate behavior of a lost and lonely generation.

title: Filipiñana
description: Isabel, a 17-year-old from the rural north of the Philippines, works at an elite country club outside Manila, lining up golf balls for powerful men. New to the job of tee-girl, she wanders the immaculate grounds sampling the club’s luxuries as its members engage in a complex dance with the doting and subservient staff. But something is rotting beneath the pristine fairways, as Isabel discovers when she tries to return a mislaid golf club to its patriarchal director, Dr. Palanca. The deeper she journeys into its most exclusive corners, the closer she gets to the violent truths of the club, her native Philippines, and her own past. The debut feature from Rafael Manuel, it won the World Cinema Dramatic Special Jury Award for Creative Vision at Sundance 2026 and reveals a major new filmmaking talent.

title: Minotaur
description: Russia, 2022. Corporate executive Gleb finds himself under siege on all fronts: haunted by suspicions that his wife is unfaithful and facing a demand to draft a quota of employees for war. Though desperate to keep his hands clean, his struggle to reassert control accelerates toward violence.

title: The History of Concrete
description: Fri, Sep 18: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Edy Modica (actress, comedian, filmmaker), after 4:40 show! Fri, Sep 18: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Rachel Kaly (comedian, writer, actor), after 7:15 show! Sun, Sep 20: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Sarah Sherman after 2:10 show! Following the finale of his TV show, filmmaker John Wilson searches for a new creative outlet. After attending a workshop on how to write and sell a Hallmark movie, he attempts to apply the same formula to a documentary about concrete.

title: FATHERLAND
description: From the director of IDA and COLD WAR: FATHERLAND follows Nobel Prize-winning author Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler, KINGS OF THE ROAD) and his actress daughter Erika (Sandra Hüller, ANATOMY OF A FALL) as they drive across a war-ravaged 1949 Germany. Returning home after years of exile in the U.S. and exuding a superhuman gravitas, Mann finds the Germany he knew to be gone, replaced by a country with contradictory ideologies. Erika, who acts as his travel coordinator and translator, strives to pierce his detached persona while quietly struggling with a family tragedy.

title: You Can See Everything
description: Thirty-four days before she’s sent to prison, notorious Silicon Valley founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a skeptical film crew to document her every move. What begins as an intimate portrait of an enigmatic felon becomes a mind-bending three-year journey into the abyss.

title: INSIDE JOB
description: A pair of married ex-convicts trying to go straight get jobs at a department store. A gangster who knows about their past threatens to expose it unless they agree to help him rob the department store.

title: ROME, OPEN CITY
description: Rome, winter 1943: as screeching-tired Gestapo dragnets blanket the “open city,” Resistance leader Marcello Pagliero escapes from his apartment by running across the rooftops (as did co-screenwriter Sergio Amidei in real life), as pregnant widow Anna Magnani prepares for her wedding, parish priest Aldo Fabrizi uses the “frying pan method” to hide the local boys’ bomb brigade’s hardware, and effete Major Harry Feist riffles through his collection of incriminating ID photos—but betrayal, a broad-daylight machine-gunning, a Partisan ambush, blowtorch torture, and death by firing squad loom… Based on actual people and all-too-recent incidents (Magnani’s electrifying final scene was inspired by her enraged pursuit of her boyfriends’s escape by truck); written in a week in Federico Fellini’s kitchen (the only place with heat); shot on a number of the real locations, and cast mainly with non-pros (Fabrizi and second-choice Magnani were already famous, albeit for comedy), OPEN CITY’s documentary look and still hair-raising violence rocked audiences and critics around the world, making Neo-Realism, Rossellini, and Magnani world-famous, sharing the top prize at Cannes, and running twenty-one consecutive months at a single New York cinema. 4K Restoration courtesy Janus Films. 35mm print courtesy Cinecittà.

title: It’s Alive! David Ehrlich
description: Self-identified “citizen of the world, animator and educator” David Ehrlich has made over 40 independent, abstract films since 1974. He began his creative life as an artist in New York from 1965 to 1975 before moving to Vermont, where animation became his chosen medium of expression. Rooted in his studies of sculpture and classical music, early works such as Dissipative Dialogues and Precious Metals flirt with representing recognizable objects, while the larger body of his later work, animated on transparent tracing paper and in clay, explores abstract forms of color, line, and shape in a continual process of transformation. Years teaching in China led to rewarding collaborations with composers Fang Xin and Chenguan Tszo that further distinguish his work. Vermont Etude No. 2. 1979. 4 min. DCP. Precious Metal. 1980. 4 min. DCP. Dissipative Dialogues. 1982. 3 min. DCP. BIO. 2015. 3 min. DCP. China Violet. 2014. 3 min. DCP. Color Dance. 2016. 3 min. DCP. Coming and Going. 2020. 3 min. DCP. La Création du Monde. 2021. 4 min. DCP. LIN. 2019. 3 min. DCP. Meditations. 2013. 4 min. DCP. Only the Seas Live Forever. 2020. 4 min. DCP. Pencil Test. 2013. 3 min. DCP. Poznanie. 2012. 3 min. DCP. SHAN. 2017. 3 min. DCP.

title: Josephine
description: JOSEPHINE follows the psychological fallout after eight-year-old Josephine (Reeves) witnesses a brutal crime in Golden Gate Park. As she acts out, her parents (Tatum and Chan) struggle with helping their daughter cope, while facing the moral responsibility of demanding justice in a world that’s lost its innocence. Open Fri Nov 20, more showtimes to be announced.

title: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping
description: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping will revisit the world of Panem twenty-four years before the events of The Hunger Games, starting on the morning of the reaping of the Fiftieth Hunger Games, also known as the Second Quarter Quell.

title: Tangles
description: Mon, Nov 23: Sneak preview + extended intro by Julia Louis-Dreyfus at 8:40! Mon, Nov 23: Sneak preview + extended intro by Julia Louis-Dreyfus at 9:05! Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Sarah Silverman, Abbi Jacobson, Seth Rogen and Bryan Cranston voice a family struggling with their mother’s Alzheimer’s diagnosis in this deeply moving, animated adaptation of Sarah Leavitt’s acclaimed graphic novel. Regular engagement begins January 15th, 2027.

title: ONCE UPON A TIME IN HARLEM
description: August 1972: A reunion of Harlem Renaissance luminaries is held at Duke Ellington’s St. Nicholas Ave. townhouse. Though many of these figures haven’t seen each other in 50 years, sharp memories, vigorous debates, and unsettled scores soon flow through this stunner of a cocktail party, which features (among others): artists Romare Bearden, Aaron Douglas, and Richard Bruce Nugent; composer Eubie Blake; poet Arna Bontemps; photographer James Van Der Zee; and activists Richard B. Moore and Louise Patterson. After organizing and shooting this extraordinary gathering, filmmaker William Greaves (SYMBIOPSYCHOTAXIPLASM: TAKE ONE) was unable to complete the film before his death in 2014. One of the cameramen that day was his son David, who expertly reshaped this never-before-seen, newly-restored footage into “a film for the ages…one of the greatest cinematic works of creative nonfiction that I’ve ever seen.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker

title: You Can See Everything
description: Thirty-four days before she’s sent to prison, notorious Silicon Valley founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a skeptical film crew to document her every move. What begins as an intimate portrait of an enigmatic felon becomes a mind-bending three-year journey into the abyss. From boundary-pushing directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim comes You Can See Everything.

title: Once Upon A Time In… Hollywood
description: Quentin Tarantino’s Once Upon a Time in… Hollywood visits 1969 Los Angeles, where everything is changing, as TV star Rick Dalton (Leonardo DiCaprio) and his longtime stunt double Cliff Booth (Brad Pitt) make their way around an industry they hardly recognize anymore. The ninth film from the writer-director features a large ensemble cast and multiple storylines in a tribute to the final moments of Hollywood’s golden age.

title: Naza
description: Directed by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, two of the co-directors of the 2024 Oscar-winning documentary No Other Land , Naza reveals the systems behind Israel’s bombing of Gaza and its mass killing of Palestinian civilians. Winner of Special Jury Prize at the 2026 Venice Film Festival.

title: Tangles
description: Mon, Nov 23: Sneak preview + extended intro by Julia Louis-Dreyfus at 8:40! Mon, Nov 23: Sneak preview + extended intro by Julia Louis-Dreyfus at 9:05! Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Sarah Silverman, Abbi Jacobson, Seth Rogen and Bryan Cranston voice a family struggling with their mother’s Alzheimer’s diagnosis in this deeply moving, animated adaptation of Sarah Leavitt’s acclaimed graphic novel. Regular engagement begins January 15th, 2027.

title: Eyes Wide Shut
description: Stanley Kubrick's daring last film is many things. It is a compelling psychosexual journey. A haunting dreamscape. A riveting tale of suspense. A major milestone in the careers of stars Tom Cruise and Nicole Kidman. And "a worthy final chapter to a great director's career" (Roger Ebert). Cruise plays Dr William Hartford, who plunges into an erotic foray that threatens his marriage - and may even ensnare him in a lurid murder mystery - after his wife's (Kidman) admission of sexual longings. As the story sweeps from doubt and fear to self-discovery and reconciliation, Kubrick orchestrates it with masterful flourishes. Graceful tracking shots, controlled pacing, rich colours, startling images: bravura traits that make Kubrick a filmmaker for the ages are here to keep everyone's eyes wide shut.

title: You Can See Everything (15) (AD)
description: 34 days before she’s sent to prison, notorious Silicon Valley founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a skeptical film crew led by Nathan Fielder to document her every move.

title: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth 35mm
description: Brad Pitt returns to his Academy Award-winning role as Cliff Booth, only this time it’s 1977 and it’s a very different Hollywood. Directed by David Fincher from a screenplay by Quentin Tarantino, the film also stars Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Carla Gugino, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II and Peter Weller.

title: ALL OF A SUDDEN
description: In the latest film by Oscar®-winning director Ryûsuke Hamaguchi (DRIVE MY CAR), Virginie Efira (BENEDETTA) stars as Marie-Lou, the progressive director of a nursing home in the Parisian suburbs. Her life changes when she meets Mari (Tao Okamoto), Japanese playwright. As the two women reckon with the lives they have lived, they find new ways to make sense of the time that remains. Following caregivers as they navigate the tensions between idealism and pragmatism, Hamaguchi crafts a film that rests fully in the present, attentive to the delicate unfolding of thought, feeling, and human connection.

title: Disney's Hexed
description: An awkward teenage boy and his Type-A mom discover that what makes him unusual might be magical powers that will turn their lives and a secret world of magic upside down.

title: Naza
description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them. We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA ’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence. — Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

title: TO LIVE AND DIE IN L.A.
description: Two cops in Los Angeles try to track down a vicious criminal named Eric Masters. When one of them is killed by Masters, the other swears revenge – no matter what the cost. He becomes obsessed with his target, as the law he once swore to uphold becomes meaningless and a dangerous game of life and death begins. With William Petersen, Willem Dafoe, John Turturro, Dean Stockwell, and more.

title: You Can See Everything
description: Thirty-four days before she’s sent to prison, notorious Silicon Valley founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a sceptical film crew to document her every move. What begins as an intimate portrait of an enigmatic felon becomes a mind-bending three-year journey into the abyss. From boundary-pushing directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim comes You Can See Everything .

title: Amelie - 25th Anniversary
description: 23-year-old Amélie is lonely. After an isolating childhood, she moves to Paris and becomes a waitress at the Café des Deux Moulins, a bar restaurant filled with a colourful cast of diners and employees. One night, Amélie happens across a box of treasures hidden in her apartment, left by a little boy in the Fifties, that changes the course of her life. Henceforth, she dedicates herself to giving back to her community, tracking down the owner of these keepsakes, consoling a widowed neighbour and befriending a reclusive artist. When completing these good deeds, she crosses paths with Nino, a photobooth collagist who shares her oddball sensibilities. She quickly falls in love with him.

title: Josephine
description: After eight-year-old Josephine witnesses a violent assault in San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park, the trauma begins to reshape her world, and her fear and confusion slowly unravel the household around her. Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan star as her parents in Beth de Araújo’s acclaimed drama, winner of both the Grand Jury Prize and the Audience Award at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival.

title: Primetime
description: In 2006, To Catch a Predator host Chris Hansen sets out to make television history.

title: Fatherland
description: Sandra Hüller illuminates the screen in Pawel Pawlikowski’s stunning and existential gem of family, fascism, and Goethe in post-WWII Germany. Fatherland centres on the relationship between the Nobel Prize-winning writer Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler) and his daughter Erika (Sandra Hüller) – actress, writer and rally driver. In the summer of 1949, at the height of the Cold War, father and daughter embark on a challenging and emotional road trip in a black Buick taking them across a Germany in ruins – from US dominated Frankfurt to Soviet controlled Weimar. Returning home after sixteen years of exile in the US, Thomas Mann has to face not only a divided fatherland, but also a deep fracture within his own family.

title: Minotaur (15) (AD)
description: After a nine-year absence having fled his native Russia and gone into exile, Andrey Zvyagintsev makes his long-awaited return; a modern reimagining of Claude Chabrol’s La femme infidèle .

title: North by Northwest
description: The ultimate Hitchcock thrill ride, centered on the Master of Suspense’s favorite theme: an innocent man accused of a crime he didn’t commit. Here, the poor sucker is an effortlessly cool Cary Grant (or is that redundant?), playing an advertising exec who’s mistaken for a spy named George Kaplan — and then mistaken for a murderer! His efforts to clear his own name and unravel a sinister conspiracy will take across the United States, from an epic train ride to an assassination attempt by airplane to a chase across Mount Rushmore. But hey, he does get to romance Eva Marie Saint along the way, so maybe it’s all worth it?

title: WHEN CAESAR WAS KING The comedy genius of Sid Caesar
description: In the early 1950s, 20 million people tuned into see the weekly TV extravaganza Your Show of Shows, starring Sid Caesar, a master of physical comedy, “double talk” and pantomime, supported by “second bananas” Imogene Coca, Carl Reiner, and Howard Morris, and a truly legendary writing staff that included Reiner, Lucille Kallen, Mel Tolkin, Mel Brooks, and Neil Simon (and, later, Woody Allen). This special compilation of some of Caesar’s greatest sketches, from Your Show of Shows and the later Caesar’s Hour, will be followed by an onstage conversation with Bruce Goldstein, Film Forum’s Founding Repertory Artistic Director (and Caesar fanatic), and longtime New York Times and Vanity Fair writer David Margolick, author of the definitive biography When Caesar Was King: How Sid Caesar Reinvented American Comedy (Schocken Books). Book signing in lobby following event. Produced and compiled by Bruce Goldstein. Edited by William Hohauser.

title: Focker-in-Law
description: A young man named Henry, son of Greg and Pam Focker, faces family chaos when he decides to marry a strong-willed woman who appears to be his complete mismatch.

title: Prima Facie
description: A young, ambitious trial lawyer (Cynthia Erivo) brilliantly navigates the ruthless London court system where she is unmatched in her defense of the accused, including men charged with sexual assault. Just as her career is taking off, a life-altering event forces her to reckon with her belief in the judicial system that was once the core of her identity.

title: Josephine
description: JOSEPHINE follows the psychological fallout after eight-year-old Josephine (Reeves) witnesses a brutal crime in Golden Gate Park. As she acts out, her parents (Tatum and Chan) struggle with helping their daughter cope, while facing the moral responsibility of demanding justice in a world that’s lost its innocence. Open Fri Nov 20, more showtimes to be announced.

title: THE HEARTBREAK KID
description:
Lenny is three days into his honeymoon when he spots the woman he thinks he should have married. The bride is upstairs with sunburn. He is downstairs selling himself a completely different future.
Elaine May makes romantic self-delusion almost unbearably funny. Charles Grodin turns every conversation into a sales pitch, while Jeannie Berlin gives the discarded Lila a presence the film refuses to let him wish away. A romantic comedy with surgical instincts, exposing the monstrous entitlement hidden inside one ordinary man’s idea of the perfect match.

title: Tangles
description: Mon, Nov 23: Sneak preview + extended intro by Julia Louis-Dreyfus at 8:40! Mon, Nov 23: Sneak preview + extended intro by Julia Louis-Dreyfus at 9:05! Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Sarah Silverman, Abbi Jacobson, Seth Rogen and Bryan Cranston voice a family struggling with their mother’s Alzheimer’s diagnosis in this deeply moving, animated adaptation of Sarah Leavitt’s acclaimed graphic novel. Regular engagement begins January 15th, 2027.

title: RAISE THE RED LANTERN
description: Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father’s death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul. Newly restored, RAISE THE RED LANTERN remains a landmark of Fifth Generation Chinese cinema and 1990s international film. The 4K restoration of RAISE THE RED LANTERN was carried out by the Udine Far East Film Festival on the occasion of its 26th edition. The original image and sound negatives were used under the supervision of Director Zhang Yimou. The vintage positive copy, presented at the 1991 Venice International Film Festival and preserved at the Venice Biennale's Historical Archive of Contemporary Arts, was used for color reference. The restoration was made in 2024 at L'Immagine Ritrovata (Hong Kong – Bologna).

title: Medea (1988)
description: Based on an unfilmed screenplay by Carl Theodor Dreyer and, of course, Euripides’s tragedy of the same title, von Trier’s made-for-television film—save for two epiphanic eruptions—is uncharacteristically austere, the enfant terrible of Danish cinema making himself a medium for the Old Master’s vision, setting the source material in a pre-Christian Denmark. “An experimental film in the true sense of the word… Taking the greatest limitation of video—the medium’s lack of depth of field—Mr. von Trier turns it into a strength, flattening perspectives in a way that collapses his foreground characters into the tumultuous backgrounds (waves, wind-swept fields) that surround and dominate them.” —Dave Kehr, The New York Times Part of Classical Cinema

title: You Can See Everything
description: Thirty-four days before she’s sent to prison, notorious Silicon Valley founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a sceptical film crew to document her every move. What begins as an intimate portrait of an enigmatic felon becomes a mind-bending three-year journey into the abyss..

title: The Host
description: When a terrifying creature rises from the Han River and brings chaos to Seoul, single dad Gang-du (Song Kang-ho, Parasite) will stop at nothing to rescue his daughter from the clutches of the horrifying Host. Equal parts creature-feature thrill ride and poignant human story, Oscar-winning visionary Bong Joon Ho’s first global smash remains an incredible action drama and propulsively entertaining modern classic . “A thing of beauty, the perfect mixture of the silly and the grave.” – The New Yorker

title: The Devils
description: All screenings on a new 35mm print of the 4K restoration of the film. An enduring, singular masterpiece of cinema starring Academy Award-winner Vanessa Redgrave and Oliver Reed, KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption – and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell. Assembled from the original camera negative, this new 4K restoration presents Ken Russell’s definitive vision of The Devils by referencing the edit he privately constructed in 2004. title: MCCABE & MRS. MILLER
description: Presbyterian Church is a small mining town in the turn-of-the-century Pacific Northwest—and a perfect place where gambler John Q. McCabe and bordello madam Constance Miller can do business. Robert Altman’s dazzlingly original MCCABE & MRS. MILLER, starring Warren Beatty and Julie Christie, stands the mythology of the Old West on its ear. Shot on beautiful Vancouver wilderness locations, this 1971 film captures the essence of a long-ago time, coupled with the edgy modern sensibility Altman brought to his other ’70s masterworks M*A*S*H and NASHVILLE. The spellbinding result, critic Pauline Kael wrote, is “a modern classic.”

title: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping
description: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping will revisit the world of Panem twenty-four years before the events of The Hunger Games, starting on the morning of the reaping of the Fiftieth Hunger Games, also known as the Second Quarter Quell.

title: Bouchra
description: Bouchra. 2026. Italy/Morocco/USA. Directed by Orian Barki, Meriem Bennani. DCP courtesy Film Movement. In Arabic, French, English; English subtitles. 83 min. Much like their beloved pandemic-era series 2 Lizards, Meriem Bennani and Orian Barki’s animated feature Bouchra takes place in a New York City populated by anthropomorphic animals. Bouchra (voiced by Bennani) is a queer, Moroccan jackal in a creative rut, living the thirtysomething life alongside the friends and lovers who make up her chosen kin. Struggling with the aftermath of coming out to her mother years prior, she attempts to develop a script based on these family dynamics. Playfully self-reflexive, Bouchra’s creative and personal journey back to Casablanca and the family home (where matriarch Aïcha is voiced by artist Yto Barrada) draws on real conversations between Bennani and her mother. Brought to life with deep-hitting naturalism—through voice cameos from the directing duo’s family and friends and digital animation rendered in remarkable detail—Bouchra tenderly evokes the experience of negotiating cross-cultural identity. Tickets are available to members at the Explore category and above beginning two weeks before each screening date. Additional tickets will be released to members and the general public one week before each screening date. Please note that space is extremely limited and tickets will be in high demand. Tickets can be reserved at moma.org/contenders beginning at 10:30 a.m. ET. For the Contenders series, due to limited availability, members at the Explore category and above receive two free tickets per membership. If a screening is sold out, a standby line will form one hour before the start time. If you are a ticket holder and arrive after the scheduled start time, we cannot guarantee entry.

title: Fjord
description: Mihai and Lisbet Gheorghiu, a Romanian-Norwegian Pentecostal couple, move with their five children from Romania to Norway after Mihai’s parents die, seeking closeness to Lisbet’s family, who share their faith. Settling in an isolated coastal village, they form a bond with their neighbors, the Halbergs. When their daughter Elia appears at school with bruises, suspicions arise about the family's strict religious upbringing. Fjord explores clashing worldviews, conformity, tolerance, and the boundaries of freedom and intimacy.

title: The Muppet Christmas Carol
description: 'Tis the season for love, laughter, and one of the most cherished stories of all time! Join Kermit the Frog, Miss Piggy, and all the hilarious Muppets in this merry, magical version of Charles Dickens' classic tale. Academy Award® winner Michael Caine (Best Supporting Actor) gives a performance that's anything but "bah, humbug!" as greedy, penny-pinching Ebenezer Scrooge. One fateful Christmas Eve, Scrooge is visited by the Ghosts of Christmas Past, Present, and Future. Together with kind, humble Bob Cratchit (Kermit the Frog) and his family, the Spirits open Scrooge's eyes -- and his heart -- to the true meaning of Christmas. Filled with original music and dazzling special effects, THE MUPPET CHRISTMAS CAROL will become a holiday tradition your family will treasure all the days of the year. Featuring the film’s famous long-lost song ‘When Love is Gone’! ------ As always you can expect SING ALONG performances of this new version of THE MUPPET CHRISTMAS CAROL this Christmas - and now we don't need to pretend that we weren't going to just play the lost scene regardless! Performances will feature a Hosted Pre-Show with our very own Father Christmas, where you will be prepped on what to do throughout the film. Costumes aren't mandatory, but 'Tis the season, and we love seeing you dressed up in your favourite Christmas Jumpers! All this, and a few more surprises up our sleeves, makes this one of the must-see events this Christmas! If you're wanting to Sing Along with The Muppet Christmas Carol, simply book for the performances marked SING ALONG [it's next to the start time]. All other screenings will be regular performances, and nothing will be written next to the start time.

title: You Can See Everything
description: Thirty-four days before she’s sent to prison, notorious Silicon Valley founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a skeptical film crew to document her every move. What begins as an intimate portrait of an enigmatic felon becomes a mind-bending three-year journey into the abyss.

title: Disney's Hexed
description: An awkward teenage boy and his Type-A mom discover that what makes him unusual might be magical powers that will turn their lives and a secret world of magic upside down.

title: Wild Horse Nine
description: Set in 1973, during the US’s attempt to overthrow the Chilean government, a hitman for the US government with connections to the JFK assassination suddenly realizes that his own people have put a hit on him to cover up the mess.

title: PAISAN
description: The story of Italy’s liberation, told in six episodes, traveling from the first Allied landing in Sicily to the battle of the Po Delta, PAISAN demonstrated that OPEN CITY had been no fluke. Conceived on a vaster scale, with a considerably higher budget, and international distribution from MGM, PAISAN is a national epic that still startles for its immediacy, its technical mastery, its unpredictable rhythms. Scenes of unbearable suspense on the streets of Florence alternate with lighter fare, such as the doctrinal scuffles between Italian monks and American chaplains in Romagna. Stitched together like a newsreel (and skillfully edited to blend in stock footage and suggest off-screen pyrotechnics with creative sound effects), PAISAN became a worldwide sensation, an intellectual action film that pictured recent history with an unprecedented heft and scope. The film became a lodestar for filmmakers from Gillo Pontecorvo to Martin Scorsese, with the latter remarking, “The result... is still startling: it’s like seeing reality itself unfolding before your eyes.”

title: Wild Horse Nine (15) (AD)
description: Two eccentric CIA agents ( John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell ) await orders on Easter Island, on the cusp of yet another military coup in Martin McDonagh 's latest dark comedy.

title: Fatherland
description: Sandra Hüller illuminates the screen in Pawel Pawlikowski’s stunning and existential gem of family, fascism, and Goethe in post-WWII Germany. Fatherland centres on the relationship between the Nobel Prize-winning writer Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler) and his daughter Erika (Sandra Hüller) – actress, writer and rally driver. In the summer of 1949, at the height of the Cold War, father and daughter embark on a challenging and emotional road trip in a black Buick taking them across a Germany in ruins – from US dominated Frankfurt to Soviet controlled Weimar. Returning home after sixteen years of exile in the US, Thomas Mann has to face not only a divided fatherland, but also a deep fracture within his own family.

title: Minotaur
description: Russia, 2022. Corporate executive Gleb finds himself under siege on all fronts: haunted by suspicions that his wife is unfaithful and facing a demand to draft a quota of employees for war. Though desperate to keep his hands clean, his struggle to reassert control accelerates toward violence.

title: NAZA (15)
description: Cloaked in darkness on the rooftops of Tel Aviv, Israeli journalist Yuval Abraham conducts shattering one-on-one interviews with Israeli soldiers and intelligence personnel.

title: Unzipped
description: Designer Isaac Mizrahi proved a force of nature on the road to his legendary fall 1994 collection, a career-defining triumph that was documented with an effervescent intimacy by Douglas Keeve, Mizrahi’s then-partner. Both a time capsule of the buoyant, raucous 1990s, when pop culture and high art became interchangeable, and a vérité-style, in-the-trenches report on the daily agonies and ecstasies of the creative process, this seminal artistic portrait—sumptuously shot by Ellen Kuras and Robert Leacock—transcends glitz and glamour to offer an extraordinary view of the charisma and force of will inherent to genius, as well as its personal costs. Digitally restored by the Sundance Institute and UCLA Film & Television Archive. Funding provided by Isaac Mizrahi Entertainment. Laboratory services by Roundabout Entertainment, Inc. and Deluxe Media Audio Services.

title: Focker-in-Law
description: A young man named Henry, son of Greg and Pam Focker, faces family chaos when he decides to marry a strong-willed woman who appears to be his complete mismatch.

title: LIAF: Open Night: Elizabeth Hobbs: History, Heresy & Hyenas (15*)
Ebenezer: A Christmas Carol
description: A thrilling ghost story set in Dickens' London, following one man's supernatural journey to face his past, present and future as he fights for a second chance at redemption.

title: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth 35mm
description: Brad Pitt returns to his Academy Award-winning role as Cliff Booth, only this time it’s 1977 and it’s a very different Hollywood. Directed by David Fincher from a screenplay by Quentin Tarantino, the film also stars Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Carla Gugino, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II and Peter Weller.

title: ALL OF A SUDDEN
description: In the latest film by Oscar®-winning director Ryûsuke Hamaguchi (DRIVE MY CAR), Virginie Efira (BENEDETTA) stars as Marie-Lou, the progressive director of a nursing home in the Parisian suburbs. Her life changes when she meets Mari (Tao Okamoto), Japanese playwright. As the two women reckon with the lives they have lived, they find new ways to make sense of the time that remains. Following caregivers as they navigate the tensions between idealism and pragmatism, Hamaguchi crafts a film that rests fully in the present, attentive to the delicate unfolding of thought, feeling, and human connection.

title: ANDY WARHOL’S 'SCREEN TESTS' + CONRAD VENTUR’S 'SCREEN TESTS REVISITED', PGM 1

For Ventur’s (ongoing) project, he has sought out as many of the surviving SCREEN TESTees as possible, and restaged their portraits, resulting in a poetic tribute to Warhol’s films and to the transformations wrought by time. Conrad Ventur in person on Sat, Nov 21! title: NAKED LUNCH
description:
The bug powder is addictive. The typewriter is alive. And Bill Lee’s latest assignment may be coming from an insect intelligence service. Fleeing into the Interzone, he tries to write a report from a reality that will not stay still.
David Cronenberg fuses William S. Burroughs’s fiction and biography into a wonderfully deadpan nightmare of addiction and authorship. Peter Weller plays the impossible with perfect weary conviction, while grotesque organic machines make language horribly physical. A literary adaptation that succeeds by becoming its own mutant creature.

title: Tangles
description: Mon, Nov 23: Sneak preview + extended intro by Julia Louis-Dreyfus at 8:40! Mon, Nov 23: Sneak preview + extended intro by Julia Louis-Dreyfus at 9:05! Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Sarah Silverman, Abbi Jacobson, Seth Rogen and Bryan Cranston voice a family struggling with their mother’s Alzheimer’s diagnosis in this deeply moving, animated adaptation of Sarah Leavitt’s acclaimed graphic novel. Regular engagement begins January 15th, 2027.

title: Josephine
description: JOSEPHINE follows the psychological fallout after eight-year-old Josephine (Reeves) witnesses a brutal crime in Golden Gate Park. As she acts out, her parents (Tatum and Chan) struggle with helping their daughter cope, while facing the moral responsibility of demanding justice in a world that’s lost its innocence. Open Fri Nov 20, more showtimes to be announced.

title: RAISE THE RED LANTERN
description: Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father’s death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul. Newly restored, RAISE THE RED LANTERN remains a landmark of Fifth Generation Chinese cinema and 1990s international film. The 4K restoration of RAISE THE RED LANTERN was carried out by the Udine Far East Film Festival on the occasion of its 26th edition. The original image and sound negatives were used under the supervision of Director Zhang Yimou. The vintage positive copy, presented at the 1991 Venice International Film Festival and preserved at the Venice Biennale's Historical Archive of Contemporary Arts, was used for color reference. The restoration was made in 2024 at L'Immagine Ritrovata (Hong Kong – Bologna).

title: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth
description: Brad Pitt returns to his Academy Award-winning role as Cliff Booth, only this time it’s 1977 and it’s a very different Hollywood. Directed by David Fincher from a screenplay by Quentin Tarantino, the film also stars Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Carla Gugino, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II and Peter Weller. (Netflix)

title: Desperately Seeking Susan
description: Susan Seidelman’s stylish New York fairy tale features an effervescent young Madonna in her first film role. Rosanna Arquette stars as Roberta, a bored suburban housewife who is fascinated with a mystery woman, Susan, played by Madonna. When she spots an ad meant for Susan in the personals, Roberta goes to the rendezvous too, and in a series of events involving amnesia and mistaken identity, she steps out of her own sterile existence and into the danger and romance of Susan’s life. With incredible 80s style, two iconic leads, and laughs, intrigue, and tons of fun to boot, we’ve got your Black Friday covered!

title: DAWN OF THE DEAD
description: Writer-director George A. Romero ups the ante on his indie landmark NIGHT OF THE LIVING DEAD with a bigger budget, more gore (courtesy of special effects/makeup artist Tom Savini) and a touch of social commentary. Four people take refuge in a Pennsylvania shopping mall as a mysterious plague turns fresh corpses into flesh-hungry zombies and civilization collapses around them. “One of the best horror films ever made.” – Roger Ebert, Chicago Sun-Times.

title: 14th
description: Please note that there are additional showtimes of 14TH that screen with open captions (on-screen display of dialogue and sounds). For those showtimes, click here. Written in the wreckage of the Civil War, the 14th Amendment was meant to codify the promise of freedom and citizenship. Instead, it has become a permanent argument. Oscar nominee DuVernay’s new documentary pulls this fight out of the footnotes and into the present, chronicling a vicious battle that has raged for more than 150 years. Threading deep archival scholarship with today’s headlines, 14TH brings together legal minds, politicians, historians and cultural voices to explore a question America still hasn’t settled: Who gets to belong?

title: YOU CAN SEE EVERYTHING
description: Elizabeth Holmes would like to tell her side of the story. Nathan Fielder has a few questions.  Thirty-four days before she is due to begin her prison sentence for fraud, the Theranos founder invites Fielder and fellow filmmaker Lance Oppenheim into the home she shares with her partner, Billy Evans....

title: The History of Concrete
description: Fri, Sep 18: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Edy Modica (actress, comedian, filmmaker), after 4:40 show! Fri, Sep 18: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Rachel Kaly (comedian, writer, actor), after 7:15 show! Sun, Sep 20: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Sarah Sherman after 2:10 show! Following the finale of his TV show, filmmaker John Wilson searches for a new creative outlet. After attending a workshop on how to write and sell a Hallmark movie, he attempts to apply the same formula to a documentary about concrete.

title: TO DIE FOR
description: Suzanne Stone (Nicole Kidman) has always dreamed of being on TV and she’s dead-set on making that dream come true. But there is just one obstacle: Larry Maretto, her husband (Matt Dillon). So, Suzanne convinces a love-struck teenager (Joaquin Phoenix) to get Larry out of the way for good.

title: BEING THERE / DR. STRANGELOVE
description: Peter Sellers triumphs in his classic performance as an illiterate gardener who is hilariously catapulted into the fast lane of political power. Shirley MacLaine and Academy Award winner Melvyn Douglas co-star. A simple-minded gardener named Chance has spent all his life in the Washington D.C. house of an old man. When the man dies, Chance is put out on the street with no knowledge of the world except what he has learned from television. After a run-in with a limousine, he ends up a guest of a woman (MacLaine) and her husband Ben (Douglas), an influential but sickly businessman. Now called Chauncey Gardner, Chance becomes friend and confidante to Ben, and an unlikely political insider.

title: Naza
description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them. We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA ’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence. — Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

title: LA BOLA NEGRA
description: A genre-defying queer epic, dazzlingly constructed and rooted in the legacy of beloved writer Federico García Lorca, La Bola Negra tells the story of three men whose lives are intimately connected across three different eras.  Spain, 1932. A young man awaits to see if he has secured membership of th...

title: Love Actually
description: Nine intertwined stories examine the complexities of the one emotion that connects us all: love. Among the characters explored are David (Hugh Grant), the handsome newly elected British prime minister who falls for a young junior staffer (Martine McCutcheon), Sarah (Laura Linney), a graphic designer whose devotion to her mentally ill brother complicates her love life, and Harry (Alan Rickman), a married man tempted by his attractive new secretary.

title: You Can See Everything
description: Thirty-four days before she’s sent to prison, notorious Silicon Valley founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a skeptical film crew to document her every move. What begins as an intimate portrait of an enigmatic felon becomes a mind-bending three-year journey into the abyss. From boundary-pushing directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim comes You Can See Everything.

title: FATHERLAND
description: From the director of IDA and COLD WAR: FATHERLAND follows Nobel Prize-winning author Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler, KINGS OF THE ROAD) and his actress daughter Erika (Sandra Hüller, ANATOMY OF A FALL) as they drive across a war-ravaged 1949 Germany. Returning home after years of exile in the U.S. and exuding a superhuman gravitas, Mann finds the Germany he knew to be gone, replaced by a country with contradictory ideologies. Erika, who acts as his travel coordinator and translator, strives to pierce his detached persona while quietly struggling with a family tragedy.

title: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping
description: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping will revisit the world of Panem twenty-four years before the events of The Hunger Games, starting on the morning of the reaping of the Fiftieth Hunger Games, also known as the Second Quarter Quell.

title: Minotaur (15) (AD)
description: After a nine-year absence having fled his native Russia and gone into exile, Andrey Zvyagintsev makes his long-awaited return; a modern reimagining of Claude Chabrol’s La femme infidèle .

title: VOYAGE TO ITALY
description: In Naples to sell a late uncle’s villa, London business man George Sanders and wife Ingrid Bergman find that, after eight years of marriage, they have little to say to each other. And as the closing drags on, Bergman remembers a died-too-young poet who loved her, Sanders frets about time away from work, and they split apart—she to stare at the rawness of the statuary in the Museum, the ionization of Vesuvian craters, the skeletons at the cemetery; he to dally with friends on Capri, languidly pursue an estranged wife, and to wave off an attractive prostitute; both to finally view the plaster molds of the dead of Pompeii. Little happens, and yet subtly we see the degeneration of a marriage. Will it take a miracle to save it? Unsuccessful on first release, but over the years steadily climbing the ranks of All-Time Ten Best lists. In this centenary tribute to her father and his cinema of thought, Isabella Rossellini plays herself, her mother Ingrid Bergman, David O. Selznick, Alfred Hitchcock, Federico Fellini, Charlie Chaplin, and others.

title: Who Killed Alex Odeh?
description: In October 1985, Santa Ana, California was shaken by a brazen act of political violence when a Palestinian American, Alex Odeh, a beloved teacher and community leader, was killed by a tripwire bomb planted in his office. Despite clear evidence and identified suspects, the case was never solved. Who Killed Alex Odeh? reopens the mystery, tracking a renewed investigation in real time as new leads emerge, long-buried records come to light, and the forces behind a political assassination are finally confronted. Unfolding like a detective thriller, the film weaves archival footage, firsthand testimony, and new reporting to expose the violent fundamentalist networks behind the attack and the institutional failures that protected them. As the investigation deepens, the story widens to reveal how the extremist ideology that fueled Odeh’s murder did not disappear - it evolved, gaining traction and legitimacy in the modern political landscape. Directed by Jason Osder and William Lafi Youmans, a Jewish American and a Palestinian American, Who Killed Alex Odeh? is both a gripping cold-case pursuit and a timely examination of political violence, asking what it means when acts of terror go unresolved, and how justice denied continues to shape the world we live in.
director: Jason Osder and William Lafi Youmans

title: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother
description: From writer-director Bassam Tariq, Your Mother, Your Mother, Your Mother stars Mahershala Ali as Latif, a devoutly religious hitman who struggles to balance work, faith and fatherhood. When his wife dies, he embarks on a desperate journey across Houston to protect his children, confronting the forces closing in around him - and the beliefs threatening to unravel within.

title: Josephine
description: After eight-year-old Josephine witnesses a violent assault in San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park, the trauma begins to reshape her world, and her fear and confusion slowly unravel the household around her. Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan star as her parents in Beth de Araújo’s acclaimed drama, winner of both the Grand Jury Prize and the Audience Award at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival.

title: Prima Facie
description: A young, ambitious trial lawyer (Cynthia Erivo) brilliantly navigates the ruthless London court system where she is unmatched in her defense of the accused, including men charged with sexual assault. Just as her career is taking off, a life-altering event forces her to reckon with her belief in the judicial system that was once the core of her identity.

title: MYSTERY MOVIE
description:
Take a seat without knowing what is coming. Our mystery screenings explore the bold, disreputable and gloriously unclassifiable world of psychotronic cinema: discoveries that make you wonder how they were made, who they were made for, and why nobody showed you sooner.
The title stays secret until showtime. Curiosity is essential; good taste is negotiable.
Strictly for adult audiences. Films may contain offensive and upsetting content. Do not attend if you are of a sensitive disposition.

title: The Host
description: When a terrifying creature rises from the Han River and brings chaos to Seoul, single dad Gang-du (Song Kang-ho, Parasite) will stop at nothing to rescue his daughter from the clutches of the horrifying Host. Equal parts creature-feature thrill ride and poignant human story, Oscar-winning visionary Bong Joon Ho’s first global smash remains an incredible action drama and propulsively entertaining modern classic . “A thing of beauty, the perfect mixture of the silly and the grave.” – The New Yorker

title: The Devils
description: All screenings on a new 35mm print of the 4K restoration of the film. An enduring, singular masterpiece of cinema starring Academy Award-winner Vanessa Redgrave and Oliver Reed, KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption – and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell. Assembled from the original camera negative, this new 4K restoration presents Ken Russell’s definitive vision of The Devils by referencing the edit he privately constructed in 2004. The film’s sound has been remastered from original English Composite 35mm Mag Film, transferred at 96kHz, plus other original film elements in selected spots as needed. The Picture and Sound restoration was performed by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color, and Warner Bros. Sound.
