title: 14th
description: Please note that there are additional showtimes of 14TH that screen with open captions (on-screen display of dialogue and sounds). For those showtimes, click here. Written in the wreckage of the Civil War, the 14th Amendment was meant to codify the promise of freedom and citizenship. Instead, it has become a permanent argument. Oscar nominee DuVernay’s new documentary pulls this fight out of the footnotes and into the present, chronicling a vicious battle that has raged for more than 150 years. Threading deep archival scholarship with today’s headlines, 14TH brings together legal minds, politicians, historians and cultural voices to explore a question America still hasn’t settled: Who gets to belong?

title: Thunderbirds Double Bill - Atlantic Inferno / A
description: This cinematic double-bill brings two of Thunderbirds’ best-loved adventures into an electrifying big screen experience – Atlantic Inferno and Attack of the Alligators.

title: In The Mood For Love
description: In 1962 Hong Kong, neighbors Su Li-zhen (Mrs. Chan) and Chow Mo-wan (Mr. Chow) discover their spouses are having an affair. As they spend time together, they develop feelings for each other, but their relationship remains chaste and unspoken, reflecting societal constraints and their own moral compass.

title: The Royal Tenenbaums
description: Royal Tenenbaum and his wife Etheline had three children and then they separated. All three children are extraordinary --- all geniuses. Virtually all memory of the brilliance of the young Tenenbaums was subsequently erased by two decades of betrayal, failure, and disaster. Most of this was generally considered to be their father's fault. "The Royal Tenenbaums" is the story of the family's sudden, unexpected reunion one recent winter.

title: Disney's Hexed
description: An awkward teenage boy and his Type-A mom discover that what makes him unusual might be magical powers that will turn their lives and a secret world of magic upside down.

title: Naza
description: Directed by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, two of the co-directors of the 2024 Oscar-winning documentary No Other Land , Naza reveals the systems behind Israel’s bombing of Gaza and its mass killing of Palestinian civilians. Winner of Special Jury Prize at the 2026 Venice Film Festival.

title: ALL OF A SUDDEN
description: In the latest film by Oscar®-winning director Ryûsuke Hamaguchi (DRIVE MY CAR), Virginie Efira (BENEDETTA) stars as Marie-Lou, the progressive director of a nursing home in the Parisian suburbs. Her life changes when she meets Mari (Tao Okamoto), Japanese playwright. As the two women reckon with the lives they have lived, they find new ways to make sense of the time that remains. Following caregivers as they navigate the tensions between idealism and pragmatism, Hamaguchi crafts a film that rests fully in the present, attentive to the delicate unfolding of thought, feeling, and human connection.

title: THE FLOWERS OF ST. FRANCIS
description: Rossellini’s account of a brief period in the life of Saint Francis is as plainspoken and modest as its subject, an anti-hagiography closer to the mud below than the heavens above. Loosely inspired by Fioretti di San Francesco, a nearly-contemporaneous 14th-century collection of vignettes, the film was shaped into a bare ‘scenario’ by Rossellini and Federico Fellini, but the final result remains bracingly plotless. A series of parables that illustrate the moral quality of its characters rather than any scriptural interpretation, THE FLOWERS OF ST. FRANCIS is built from incidents and yarns: an encounter with a leper, a visit from Saint Clare, the quest for a pig’s foot, and the tale of the brother who keeps giving away his clothes. Francis is played by Brother Nazario Gerardi and the ranks of his disciples are populated by real-life monks that Rossellini featured in PAISAN; the only professional actor in sight is Aldo Fabrizi, with an extended cameo as a preening warlord. Financed by a credulous publisher who believed Rossellini would deliver a devout testament whose debut would coincide with the papally declared ‘Holy Year’ of 1950, THE FLOWERS OF ST. FRANCIS instead premiered in the aftermath of Rossellini’s unsaintly and adulterous dalliance with Ingrid Bergman. The initial critical reaction was indifferent, but Rossellini had the last laugh; in 1995, the Vatican named THE FLOWERS OF ST. FRANCIS among fifteen essential works of religious cinema. 35mm print courtesy Cinecittà. 4K restoration courtesy Janus Films.

title: Focker-in-Law
description: A young man named Henry, son of Greg and Pam Focker, faces family chaos when he decides to marry a strong-willed woman who appears to be his complete mismatch.

title: Filipiñana
description: Isabel, a 17-year-old from the rural north of the Philippines, works at an elite country club outside Manila, lining up golf balls for powerful men. New to the job of tee-girl, she wanders the immaculate grounds sampling the club’s luxuries as its members engage in a complex dance with the doting and subservient staff. But something is rotting beneath the pristine fairways, as Isabel discovers when she tries to return a mislaid golf club to its patriarchal director, Dr. Palanca. The deeper she journeys into its most exclusive corners, the closer she gets to the violent truths of the club, her native Philippines, and her own past. The debut feature from Rafael Manuel, it won the World Cinema Dramatic Special Jury Award for Creative Vision at Sundance 2026 and reveals a major new filmmaking talent.

title: Rate It X
description: Previous Events: Sunday, July 5: Q&A with directors Lucy Winer and Paula De Koenigsberg after 2:55 show! Monday, July 6: Q&A with directors Lucy Winer and Paula De Koenigsberg after 7:20 show!

title: Wildwood
description: The Portland-set story follows Prue McKeel, who enters an enchanted wonderland when her baby brother Mac is taken by a murder of crows into the forest’s depths.

title: Fatherland
description: Sandra Hüller illuminates the screen in Pawel Pawlikowski’s stunning and existential gem of family, fascism, and Goethe in post-WWII Germany. Fatherland centres on the relationship between the Nobel Prize-winning writer Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler) and his daughter Erika (Sandra Hüller) – actress, writer and rally driver. In the summer of 1949, at the height of the Cold War, father and daughter embark on a challenging and emotional road trip in a black Buick taking them across a Germany in ruins – from US dominated Frankfurt to Soviet controlled Weimar. Returning home after sixteen years of exile in the US, Thomas Mann has to face not only a divided fatherland, but also a deep fracture within his own family.

title: DIVORCE ITALIAN STYLE

His solution? Since divorce is illegal, he hatches a plan to lure his spouse into the arms of another and then murder her in a justifiable effort to save his honor.

title: RAISE THE RED LANTERN
description: Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father’s death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul. Newly restored, RAISE THE RED LANTERN remains a landmark of Fifth Generation Chinese cinema and 1990s international film. The 4K restoration of RAISE THE RED LANTERN was carried out by the Udine Far East Film Festival on the occasion of its 26th edition. The original image and sound negatives were used under the supervision of Director Zhang Yimou. The vintage positive copy, presented at the 1991 Venice International Film Festival and preserved at the Venice Biennale's Historical Archive of Contemporary Arts, was used for color reference. The restoration was made in 2024 at L'Immagine Ritrovata (Hong Kong – Bologna).

title: 14th
description: Please note that there are additional showtimes of 14TH that screen with open captions (on-screen display of dialogue and sounds). For those showtimes, click here. Written in the wreckage of the Civil War, the 14th Amendment was meant to codify the promise of freedom and citizenship. Instead, it has become a permanent argument. Oscar nominee DuVernay’s new documentary pulls this fight out of the footnotes and into the present, chronicling a vicious battle that has raged for more than 150 years. Threading deep archival scholarship with today’s headlines, 14TH brings together legal minds, politicians, historians and cultural voices to explore a question America still hasn’t settled: Who gets to belong?

title: L'AMORE
description: Conceived as an homage to the range and artistry of Anna Magnani, L’AMORE is a diptych that drags the actress to the brink and watches, mouth agape, as she leaps into the abyss. The first part—“The Human Voice”—adapts a one-act play by Jean Cocteau, which Magnani had performed on stage in 1942, playing a woman whose only connection to her lover runs through the telephone wire. Shot in a French studio over two weeks with money that Rossellini had procured for GERMANY YEAR ZERO, this intensely claustrophobic showcase for Magnani (and her dog, Micia) renders a break-up as a world-historic event—as it always is for those so spurned. The second episode—“The Miracle”—was based on an original idea by Fellini, who also co-stars as a silent vagabond whom Magnani’s talkative goatherd believes to be the incarnation of Saint Joseph. Throwing herself upon the saint’s blissful body, Magnani wakes in a daze, pregnant and ever closer to the divine. If the monks can report sightings of the Madonna, why cannot Magnani follow her holy path? Although “The Miracle” aroused no complaints from the Vatican, it faced extraordinary hostility in the US, where the lay Catholics of the Legion of Decency launched a successful campaign for the New York Board of Regents to rescind the film’s exhibition license on the basis of alleged sacrilege. Distributor Joseph Burstyn appealed the decision all the way to the Supreme Court, which ultimately ruled in his favor, belatedly bringing cinema under the protection of the First Amendment, and sowing the seeds of censorship’s demise. A miracle indeed.

title: Minotaur
description: Russia, 2022. Corporate executive Gleb finds himself under siege on all fronts: haunted by suspicions that his wife is unfaithful and facing a demand to draft a quota of employees for war. Though desperate to keep his hands clean, his struggle to reassert control accelerates toward violence.

Wong Kar Wai’s loose sequel to In the Mood for Love combines that film’s languorous air of romantic longing with a dizzying time-hopping structure and avant-sci-fi twist. Tony Leung Chiu Wai reprises his role as writer Chow Mo-Wan, whose numerous failed relationships with women who drift in and out of his life (and the one who goes in and out of room 2046, down the hall from his apartment) inspire the delirious futuristic love story he pens. 2046’s dazzling fantasy sequences give Wong and two of his key collaborators—cinematographer Christopher Doyle and editor/costume designer/production designer William Chang Suk Ping—license to let their imaginations run wild, propelling the sumptuous visuals and operatic emotions skyward toward the sublime.

The title remains undisclosed until showtime. It might be a Gothic chill, a creature feature, a psychological trap or something that refuses the usual categories. Come for the surprise; stay for the discovery you could not have chosen from a familiar poster.

title: Naza
description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them. We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA ’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence. — Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

Joined by her hapless but loyal classmate Curtis Mehlberg (Jacob Tremblay), Prue navigates a world of talking animals, bandits, and powerful figures driven by grief and ambition. As the pair is drawn into a conflict threatening the balance of the forest itself, Prue must discover the strength and belief she never knew she possessed. If she hopes to save her brother and protect Wildwood’s fragile future, she will have to risk everything. From Oscar®-nominated and BAFTA®-winning LAIKA, Wildwood is a sweeping adventure about love, sacrifice, and the magic that reveals itself when we dare to look beyond the familiar.

title: The Devils
description: All screenings on a new 35mm print of the 4K restoration of the film. An enduring, singular masterpiece of cinema starring Academy Award-winner Vanessa Redgrave and Oliver Reed, KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption – and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell. Assembled from the original camera negative, this new 4K restoration presents Ken Russell’s definitive vision of The Devils by referencing the edit he privately constructed in 2004. The film’s sound has been remastered from original English Composite 35mm Mag Film, transferred at 96kHz, plus other original film elements in selected spots as needed. The Picture and Sound restoration was performed by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color, and Warner Bros. Sound.

As they scramble to pick up the pieces after the theft, the men let their greed get the best of them while entangling themselves in webs of deceit, treachery and murder. Nominated for four Academy Awards, this classic crime caper is ready to steal you away!

Following caregivers as they navigate the tensions between idealism and pragmatism, Hamaguchi crafts a film that rests fully in the present, attentive to the delicate unfolding of thought, feeling, and human connection.

title: LES CARABINIERS
description: Jean-Luc Godard had long been a champion of Rossellini’s cinema (He famously stated, “All roads lead to Open City.”), even as the younger man’s own filmmaking quickly evolved towards a more modernist and abrasive style. (Upon seeing VIVRE SA VIE, Rossellini admonished Godard that his work was drifting towards “Antonioni-ism.”) Nevertheless, Rossellini gladly accepted a scenario credit and payment from Godard for LES CARABINIERS, a loose adaptation of Benjamin Joppolo’s anti-war play, I carabinieri. Rossellini had directed a stage production in Spoleto, in defiance of a government ban on the play, and his sole contribution to the film was providing an oral summary of Joppolo’s script, which Godard transcribed, cut up, and pasted in his notebook. Godard’s version lets two country bumpkins, Michelangelo and Ulysses, loose upon the world, their only directive from their military recruiter being death, destruction, and any other war crimes they can dream up. The duo’s atrocities are intercut with newsreel footage, postcards of plunder, and other Godardian digressions.

title: EC: RAPT

RAPT employs very little dialogue, and in this respect it is reminiscent of the part-talkie genre…. It is linked to such abstract and hybrid avant-garde works as VAMPYR and L’ÂGE D’OR. The radical nature of RAPT, however, resides in its vision of a cinematic musical score. Off-Circuit: My Wife Cries
description: A phone call brings Thomas to a hospital, where he finds his wife Carla in tears. As the circumstances of her accident come into focus, so too does a relationship whose familiar terms suddenly seem uncertain. From this deceptively simple premise, Angela Schanelec constructs a relationship drama that resists the conventions of the genre in favour of something decidedly more elliptical. As conversations circle what remains unspoken; gestures and silences come increasingly to the fore with a spellbinding intensity. My Wife Cries is at once formally audacious and acutely attentive to the emotional lives of its characters and how quickly intimacy can give way to estrangement. The screening on Friday 20 November will be followed by an in-person Q&A with Angela Schanelec.

When their daughter Elia appears at school with bruises, suspicions arise about the family's strict religious upbringing. Fjord explores clashing worldviews, conformity, tolerance, and the boundaries of freedom and intimacy.

title: SELF-PORTRAITS
description: Just as the realm of two-dimensional portraiture has always encompassed self-portraiture, so too has the corresponding practice within cinema. This program collects instances of filmmakers turning the camera on themselves, or using the techniques of animation to explore their own appearances and identities. title: ABBOTT AND COSTELLO MEET FRANKENSTEIN (16MM)
description:
Dracula needs a brain for Frankenstein’s monster. Unfortunately for baggage handler Wilbur, his is just the right size. With the Wolf Man trying to intervene and Bud Abbott refusing to believe a word, Lou Costello faces the worst delivery job in cinema.
The joke works because the monsters mean business. Bela Lugosi, Lon Chaney Jr. and Glenn Strange bring the genuine Universal Gothic atmosphere; Abbott and Costello supply exquisite double takes, verbal traps and escalating panic. A gloriously unlikely meeting of old Hollywood’s great comic and monstrous bodies.
Presented on 16mm with a reel intermission.

title: Disney's Hexed
description: An awkward teenage boy and his Type-A mom discover that what makes him unusual might be magical powers that will turn their lives and a secret world of magic upside down.

title: No Country For Old Men
description: While out hunting, Llewelyn Moss (Josh Brolin) finds the grisly aftermath of a drug deal. Though he knows better, he cannot resist the cash left behind and takes it with him. The hunter becomes the hunted when a merciless killer named Chigurh (Javier Bardem) picks up his trail. Also looking for Moss is Sheriff Bell (Tommy Lee Jones), an aging lawman who reflects on a changing world and a dark secret of his own, as he tries to find and protect Moss.

title: Wild Horse Nine
description: Set in 1973, during the US’s attempt to overthrow the Chilean government, a hitman for the US government with connections to the JFK assassination suddenly realizes that his own people have put a hit on him to cover up the mess.

title: ONCE UPON A TIME IN HARLEM
description: August 1972: A reunion of Harlem Renaissance luminaries is held at Duke Ellington’s St. Nicholas Ave. townhouse. Though many of these figures haven’t seen each other in 50 years, sharp memories, vigorous debates, and unsettled scores soon flow through this stunner of a cocktail party, which features (among others): artists Romare Bearden, Aaron Douglas, and Richard Bruce Nugent; composer Eubie Blake; poet Arna Bontemps; photographer James Van Der Zee; and activists Richard B. Moore and Louise Patterson. After organizing and shooting this extraordinary gathering, filmmaker William Greaves (SYMBIOPSYCHOTAXIPLASM: TAKE ONE) was unable to complete the film before his death in 2014. One of the cameramen that day was his son David, who expertly reshaped this never-before-seen, newly-restored footage into “a film for the ages…one of the greatest cinematic works of creative nonfiction that I’ve ever seen.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker

title: THE ROSSELLINIS
description: “My grandfather left the world his masterpieces, and not a penny to any of us. Instead, he left us an enormous inheritance of family conflicts,” declares Alessandro Rossellini, the son of Renzo Rossellini and grandson of Roberto and his second wife Marcella. Between Roberto’s four wives, numerous mistresses, and descendants stretching from New York to Sweden to Qatar, the Rossellini legacy is nothing if not capacious. In this personal documentary, Alessandro interviews his relatives and tries to diagnose the roots of a genetic ailment: Rossellinitis. Characterized by conviction, outspokenness, and wanderlust (or just plain lust), those suffering from Rossellinitis are encouraged to look deeply into family history and discuss.

title: Focker-in-Law
description: A young man named Henry, son of Greg and Pam Focker, faces family chaos when he decides to marry a strong-willed woman who appears to be his complete mismatch.

title: Yes
description: Yes. 2026. France/Israel/Cyprus/Germany. Written and directed by Nadav Lapid. With Ariel Bronz, Efrat Dor, Naama Preis, Alexey Serebryakov. DCP courtesy Kino Lorber. In Hebrew, English, Russian; English subtitles. 150 min. Kurt Vonnegut famously observed that “artists are useful to society because they are so sensitive. They are super-sensitive. They keel over like canaries in poison coal mines long before more robust types realize that there is any danger whatsoever.” In life as in art, the Israeli filmmaker Nadav Lapid has become a singular embodiment of this idea, chronicling the uses and abuses of an artist in society in films like The Kindergarten Teacher, Synonyms, Ahed’s Knee, and now in Yes, even as he himself has become a target both of messianic nationalism in Israel and left-wing criticism at festivals abroad. Satirical and splenetic, Yes—the manic portrait of an Israeli jazz musician who sells his soul, bit by inexorable bit, when he’s commissioned to compose a rabidly jingoistic state anthem in the aftermath of the attacks on October 7—strikes at the core of Lapid’s anguished rage and impotence when the hate comes both from without and within. description: In the latest film by Oscar®-winning director Ryûsuke Hamaguchi (DRIVE MY CAR), Virginie Efira (BENEDETTA) stars as Marie-Lou, the progressive director of a nursing home in the Parisian suburbs. Her life changes when she meets Mari (Tao Okamoto), Japanese playwright. As the two women reckon with the lives they have lived, they find new ways to make sense of the time that remains. Following caregivers as they navigate the tensions between idealism and pragmatism, Hamaguchi crafts a film that rests fully in the present, attentive to the delicate unfolding of thought, feeling, and human connection.

description: Please note that there are additional showtimes of 14TH that screen without open captions (on-screen display of dialogue and sounds). For those showtimes, click here. Written in the wreckage of the Civil War, the 14th Amendment was meant to codify the promise of freedom and citizenship. Instead, it has become a permanent argument. Oscar nominee DuVernay’s new documentary pulls this fight out of the footnotes and into the present, chronicling a vicious battle that has raged for more than 150 years. Engulfed by switches, stolen engines, valves, and other mechanical contrivances, the immortal comedian – an engine driver literally on the wrong side of the tracks – solemnly attempts to behave normally in a world which is plainly bewitched.” –CINEMA 16 program notes, 1958 Preceded by: Buster Keaton & Edward F. title: Naza
description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them. We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA ’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence. — Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

title: DIABOLIQUE (16MM)
description:
A cruel headmaster has made enemies of both his wife and his mistress. Together they devise the perfect murder. Then the body disappears—and the most frightening question becomes whether their victim is really dead.
Henri-Georges Clouzot turns damp corridors, a neglected swimming pool and two extraordinary performances into an almost unbearable machine of suspicion. Simone Signoret’s steel meets Véra Clouzot’s mounting terror in a thriller that understands how guilt makes every ordinary sound threatening. Go in knowing as little as possible; leave the secrets in the cinema.
Presented on 16mm with a reel intermission.

title: RAISE THE RED LANTERN
description: Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father’s death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul. Newly restored, RAISE THE RED LANTERN remains a landmark of Fifth Generation Chinese cinema and 1990s international film. The 4K restoration of RAISE THE RED LANTERN was carried out by the Udine Far East Film Festival on the occasion of its 26th edition. The original image and sound negatives were used under the supervision of Director Zhang Yimou. The vintage positive copy, presented at the 1991 Venice International Film Festival and preserved at the Venice Biennale's Historical Archive of Contemporary Arts, was used for color reference. The restoration was made in 2024 at L'Immagine Ritrovata (Hong Kong – Bologna).

title: THE FLOWERS OF ST. FRANCIS
description: Rossellini’s account of a brief period in the life of Saint Francis is as plainspoken and modest as its subject, an anti-hagiography closer to the mud below than the heavens above. Loosely inspired by Fioretti di San Francesco, a nearly-contemporaneous 14th-century collection of vignettes, the film was shaped into a bare ‘scenario’ by Rossellini and Federico Fellini, but the final result remains bracingly plotless. A series of parables that illustrate the moral quality of its characters rather than any scriptural interpretation, THE FLOWERS OF ST. FRANCIS is built from incidents and yarns: an encounter with a leper, a visit from Saint Clare, the quest for a pig’s foot, and the tale of the brother who keeps giving away his clothes. Francis is played by Brother Nazario Gerardi and the ranks of his disciples are populated by real-life monks that Rossellini featured in PAISAN; the only professional actor in sight is Aldo Fabrizi, with an extended cameo as a preening warlord. Financed by a credulous publisher who believed Rossellini would deliver a devout testament whose debut would coincide with the papally declared ‘Holy Year’ of 1950, THE FLOWERS OF ST. FRANCIS instead premiered in the aftermath of Rossellini’s unsaintly and adulterous dalliance with Ingrid Bergman. The initial critical reaction was indifferent, but Rossellini had the last laugh; in 1995, the Vatican named THE FLOWERS OF ST. FRANCIS among fifteen essential works of religious cinema. 35mm print courtesy Cinecittà. 4K restoration courtesy Janus Films.

description: An angelically beautiful Catherine Deneuve was launched to stardom by this dazzling musical heart-tugger from Jacques Demy. She plays an umbrella-shop owner’s delicate daughter, glowing with first love for a handsome garage mechanic, played by Nino Castelnuovo. When the boy is shipped off to fight in Algeria, the two lovers must grow up quickly. Exquisitely designed in a kaleidoscope of colors, and told entirely through the lilting songs of the great composer Michel Legrand, The Umbrellas of Cherbourg is one of the most revered and unorthodox movie musicals of all time.

When his wife dies, he embarks on a desperate journey across Houston to protect his children, confronting the forces closing in around him - and the beliefs threatening to unravel within.

title: Prima Facie
description: A young, ambitious trial lawyer (Cynthia Erivo) brilliantly navigates the ruthless London court system where she is unmatched in her defense of the accused, including men charged with sexual assault. Just as her career is taking off, a life-altering event forces her to reckon with her belief in the judicial system that was once the core of her identity.

title: The Devils
description: All screenings on a new 35mm print of the 4K restoration of the film. An enduring, singular masterpiece of cinema starring Academy Award-winner Vanessa Redgrave and Oliver Reed, KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption – and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell. Assembled from the original camera negative, this new 4K restoration presents Ken Russell’s definitive vision of The Devils by referencing the edit he privately constructed in 2004. The film’s sound has been remastered from original English Composite 35mm Mag Film, transferred at 96kHz, plus other original film elements in selected spots as needed. The Picture and Sound restoration was performed by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color, and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: Fatherland
description: The true story of the relationship between the Nobel Prize-winning writer Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler) and his daughter Erika (Sandra Hüller) - actress, writer and rally driver. In the summer of 1949, at the height of the Cold War, father and daughter embark on a challenging and emotional road trip in a black Buick taking them across a Germany in ruins - from US dominated Frankfurt to Soviet controlled Weimar. Returning home after sixteen years of exile in the US, Thomas Mann has to face not only a divided fatherland, but also a deep fracture within his own family.

title: Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut
description: Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, The Devils lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. The restoration many believed would never happen reaffirms Russell’s incendiary masterpiece as among the most overwhelming and uncompromising achievements in British cinema. Assembled from original camera negative, this 4k restoration is Ken Russell’s 2004 preferred edit. Picture and sound restoration by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: Naza
description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them. We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA ’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence. — Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

title: Unzipped
description: Designer Isaac Mizrahi proved a force of nature on the road to his legendary fall 1994 collection, a career-defining triumph that was documented with an effervescent intimacy by Douglas Keeve, Mizrahi’s then-partner. Both a time capsule of the buoyant, raucous 1990s, when pop culture and high art became interchangeable, and a vérité-style, in-the-trenches report on the daily agonies and ecstasies of the creative process, this seminal artistic portrait—sumptuously shot by Ellen Kuras and Robert Leacock—transcends glitz and glamour to offer an extraordinary view of the charisma and force of will inherent to genius, as well as its personal costs. Digitally restored by the Sundance Institute and UCLA Film & Television Archive. Funding provided by Isaac Mizrahi Entertainment. Laboratory services by Roundabout Entertainment, Inc. and Deluxe Media Audio Services.

title: The Devils
description: All screenings on a new 35mm print of the 4K restoration of the film. An enduring, singular masterpiece of cinema starring Academy Award-winner Vanessa Redgrave and Oliver Reed, KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption – and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell. Assembled from the original camera negative, this new 4K restoration presents Ken Russell’s definitive vision of The Devils by referencing the edit he privately constructed in 2004. The film’s sound has been remastered from original English Composite 35mm Mag Film, transferred at 96kHz, plus other original film elements in selected spots as needed. The Picture and Sound restoration was performed by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color, and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: The Host
description: When a terrifying creature rises from the Han River and brings chaos to Seoul, single dad Gang-du (Song Kang-ho, Parasite) will stop at nothing to rescue his daughter from the clutches of the horrifying Host. Equal parts creature-feature thrill ride and poignant human story, Oscar-winning visionary Bong Joon Ho’s first global smash remains an incredible action drama and propulsively entertaining modern classic . “A thing of beauty, the perfect mixture of the silly and the grave.” – The New Yorker

title: Sans Soleil
description: Marker's voyage through memory, history, and video games is a free-flow of images shot largely in Japan (a cat temple, sacred phalluses, horror movies, sleeping subway riders, an animatronic JFK), with detours to Guinea-Bissau, Iceland, and, for an extended homage to Vertigo, San Francisco. An alien travelog? The world’s most profound home movie? There’s nothing quite like it in the history of cinema. “Some of Sans Soleil’s trains carry dozing commuters, others travel to distant planets. The film itself moves like a ride through an ever-shifting landscape, shuttling between dreams and waking, here and there.” —Series curator Genevieve Yue Part of Trains: Local Routes

title: The Flavor of Green Tea Over Rice
description: Ozu’s satirical—and ultimately quite touching—portrait of a marriage first seen in a state of quiet unraveling stars Kogure Michiyo and Saburi Shin as a well-off, childless middle-aged couple who find discreet outlets to express their disappointments and resentments towards one another: the Westernized wife through habitual practice of harmless deceptions and put-downs of the husband that she likens to a sluggish carp in a koi pond; her husband by supporting a niece (Keiko Tsushima) in her flight from proposed marriage arrangement interviews. “There’s stillness, and then there’s Ozu stillness. After an argument with her husband, Taeko sets off on a train journey. The stops sweep by, but she doesn’t take notice. Defiantly, petulantly, and a bit woefully, she sits.” —Series curator Genevieve Yue Part of Trains: Local Routes

description: Mihai and Lisbet Gheorghiu, a Romanian-Norwegian Pentecostal couple, move with their five children from Romania to Norway after Mihai’s parents die, seeking closeness to Lisbet’s family, who share their faith. Settling in an isolated coastal village, they form a bond with their neighbors, the Halbergs. When their daughter Elia appears at school with bruises, suspicions arise about the family's strict religious upbringing. Fjord explores clashing worldviews, conformity, tolerance, and the boundaries of freedom and intimacy.

description: Based on the beloved children's tale by Dr. Seuss, the reclusive green Grinch (Jim Carrey) decides to ruin Christmas for the cheery citizens of Whoville. Reluctantly joined by his hapless dog, Max, the Grinch comes down from his mountaintop home and sneaks into town to swipe everything holiday-related from the Whos. However, the bitter grump finds a hitch in his plans when he encounters the endearing Cindy Lou Who (Taylor Momsen).

title: Fatherland
description: The true story of the relationship between the Nobel Prize-winning writer Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler) and his daughter Erika (Sandra Hüller) - actress, writer and rally driver. In the summer of 1949, at the height of the Cold War, father and daughter embark on a challenging and emotional road trip in a black Buick taking them across a Germany in ruins - from US dominated Frankfurt to Soviet controlled Weimar. Returning home after sixteen years of exile in the US, Thomas Mann has to face not only a divided fatherland, but also a deep fracture within his own family.

title: Scenes from the Divide
description: In the lead-up to Zohran Mamdani’s election as mayor of New York City, many of the city’s Jewish population found themselves at odds over the candidate’s positions on Palestine and Israel. By inviting viewers into the homes of New Yorkers on both sides of the campaign, DOC NYC alumna Alison Klayman ( Jagged; Ai Weiwei: Never Sorry ) reveals a fierce battle among American Jews over identity, history, and responsibility. SCENES FROM THE DIVIDE explores a community in generational upheaval.

title: Merry Christmas, Mr. Lawrence
description: Set in a POW camp in Japanese-occupied Java circa 1942, the film explores the relationship between British prisoners and their captors. Lt. Col. John Lawrence (Tom Conti), the lone Japanese speaker among the interned British, tries to negotiate an uneasy equilibrium within the camp, which is overseen by the vicious Capt. Yanoi (Ryuichi Sakamoto). An ardent follower of the Bushido moral code, his eye is unexpectedly caught by the arrival Maj. Jack “Strafer” Celliers (David Bowie), an insolent and rabble-rousing new prisoner. Could Yanoi’s fascination with Celliers change everything? Merry Christmas, Mr. Lawrence has endured as a deeply moving anti-war statement, as well as a thoughtful exploration of national and sexual identity.

title: Focker-in-Law

Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan star as her parents in Beth de Araújo’s acclaimed drama, winner of both the Grand Jury Prize and the Audience Award at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival.

title: CINÉMATON, PROGRAM 2
description: Gérard Courant CINÉMATON 1978-85, ca. 80 min selection, Super-8mm-or-video-to-digital “Since the 7th of February, 1978, I have made portraits on film of artistic and cultural personalities that I call CINÉMATON. There are ten rules for the cinematon, ten commandments that must not be deviated from: 1) A camera on a tripod; 2) A camera that does not move; 3) A close-up of a face; 4) No sound; 5) No change in focal length; 6) No change in the framing; 7) Running-time of 3 minutes and 25 seconds; 8) One take only; 9) No cutting during the shooting and no editing; 10) The person that is being filmed can do whatever he/she wants. The aims of the CINÉMATON are multiple: the basic aim is to constitute an archive on art and especially on the film, theater, and entertainment scenes in those moments when the subject that is being filmed proposes a great moment of truth about herself or himself. Each CINÉMATON is preceded by three introductory title cards with the chronological number of the shooting of the portrait, the name of the person that is being filmed, his or her nationality, his profession, the date, hour, and place of the shooting. CINÉMATON has theoretically no end.” –Gérard Courant N°601 TERRY GILLIAM (1985) N°602 SAMUEL FULLER (1985) N°806 NAGISA ŌSHIMA (1986) N°836 MAÏ MASRI (1986) N°844 MICHEL KHLEIFI (1986) N°1068 HARUN FAROCKI (1988) N°1071 NELSON PEREIRA DOS SANTOS (1988) N°1083 SERGUEÏ PARADJANOV (1988) N°1084 ULTRA VIOLET (1988) N°1085 MIKE KUCHAR (1988) N°1256 JEAN ROUCH (1990) N°1519 KEN LOACH (1991) N°1590 JONAS MEKAS (1992) N°1596 JOHN GIORNO (1993) N°1780 MED HONDO (1995) N°1938 MATHIEU AMALRIC (1998) N°2146 PEDRO COSTA (2006) N°2189 HELGA FANDERL (2008) N°2446 MOHAMAD MALAS (2011) N°2929 JACKIE RAYNAL (2015)

title: BAD LIEUTENANT
description:
The badge buys him access to everything he is destroying himself with: drugs, gambling, sex and power. Then a shocking crime forces a corrupt New York cop towards a reckoning he cannot drink, bet or bully his way out of.
Harvey Keitel gives a terrifyingly exposed performance in Abel Ferrara’s bruising journey through addiction, guilt and the possibility of grace. Street-level grime collides with religious anguish; there is no comfortable distance from this man’s collapse. A ferocious New York film that makes redemption feel as dangerous as damnation.

title: Cost Of Living (IFS)
description: Independent Filmmakers Showcase "London, 2017. Robin has a remote, bristly relationship with her mother, Jayne – an inveterate liar and alcoholic with whom everyone is rapidly running out of patience. But when her father, Martyn, files for divorce and Jayne comes to the capital to revitalise her flagging career in journalism, Robin sees in her mother's newly vulnerable state an opportunity to forge the bond they've never previously had. Concerned that Jayne is using their daughter as a pawn in their divorce settlement, Martyn is left meanwhile with a dilemma – how can he protect Robin, without giving into Jayne's manipulations all over again?" https://costoflivingfilm.myportfolio.com/

title: Cinematic Void Presents 3 WOMEN
description: In a dusty, underpopulated California resort town, a naive southern waif, Pinky Rose (Sissy Spacek), idolizes and befriends her fellow nurse, the would-be sophisticate and “thoroughly modern” Millie Lammoreaux (Shelley Duvall). When Millie takes Pinky in as her roommate, Pinky’s hero worship evolves into something far stranger and more sinister than either could have anticipated. Featuring brilliant performances from Spacek and Duvall, this dreamlike masterpiece from Robert Altman careens from the humorous to the chilling to the surreal, resulting in one of the most unusual and compelling films of the 1970s.

title: DAY WITH(OUT) ART 2026: SEEDS IN A DYING COLONY (FREE SCREENING!)
description: For Day With(out) Art 2026, Visual AIDS presents seeds in a dying colony, a program of four newly commissioned videos that move through the afterlives of colonialism and the ongoing HIV epidemic. Across fractured histories and landscapes marked by extraction, the works trace how systems of power shape the body, memory, and experiences of care. The program responds to a moment marked by deepening neocolonialism and mass desensitization to violent, preventable death, including recent spikes in HIV cases and deaths. The title draws from the work of psychiatrist and political philosopher Frantz Fanon, whose writings on colonial violence and the racialized psyche have been taken up by some AIDS historians and theorists to understand how global health systems, formed through colonial rule, ultimately determine the order, quality, and conditions under which people receive healthcare, while also overwriting indigenous knowledge of healthy, embodied living. Rather than isolating HIV as a singular issue, seeds in a dying colony gestures toward the tension between systems of domination that appear enduring and the latent power and ancestral knowledge that remains in their undoing. The artists in this program were selected by a jury of filmmakers who each selected an artist to mentor through their production process. The mentors of the 2026 program include Amil Shivji, Hiura Fernandes, Ésery Mondesir, and J Triangular. Edgar Hudson THERE IS AN ELEPHANT IN THE ROOM (2026, 9.5 min, digital) A young person flees home after a life-altering discovery, carrying the weight of things that cannot be said out loud. He encounters an activist fighting to be heard and a care worker sustaining others through daily acts of survival. Through dance and movement, the film offers a quiet story of survival, exile, and return, asking what it takes to face the elephant that everyone knows is there. Bruna Kury & Matheus Mello TRAVESTY REVENGE / VENGANZA TRAVESTY (2026, 7.5 min, digital) A visual manifesto that transforms the HIV virus into a mirror of empire, where data, propaganda, and flesh collide. Through a frenetic digital collage, the film exposes the biopolitical machinery that controls the body and weaponizes borders against life itself. Sido Lansari ON A BRIGHT DAY / C’ÉTAIT UN JOUR LUMINEUX (2026, 19 min, digital) ON A BRIGHT DAY weaves together archival echoes, poetic fragments, and testimonies of Arab queer lives touched by HIV, spanning generations and geographies. Through the voices of the dead and the living, the film transforms silenced histories into a collective act of remembrance and resistance. Micaela Cyrino HOW TO PROJECT YOUR VOICE WITHOUT CAUSING AN EARTHQUAKE (2026, 16 min, digital) Carolina lives alone in an apartment on the outskirts of São Paulo. Every morning she faces the city’s frenetic pace during the long commute from her home to work. In her thoughts, her grandmother’s wisdom always returns; in her headphones, it’s always the same rap. In her bag, she carries the book of recipes, baths, and blessings she inherited from her grandmother and the desire to end the day well. Total running time: ca. 55 min.

title: Socrates
description: Beginning in the mid-’60s and ending with his death in 1977, Rossellini committed himself to producing a series of films, telefilms, and serial works that would together constitute a narrative of human progress and the history of ideas from aleolithic to present times. Socrates, initiating a tetralogy of works on epoch-defining thinkers, sets its scene in an Athens humbled by Sparta and increasingly irritated by the prickly, prodding philosopher in their midst, finally determined to silence him. Using out-of-vogue in-camera effects to transform an ancient Spanish village into Athens, probing scenes with his customized, remote-controlled Pancinor zoom, and employing a dirge-like electronic score by Mario Nascimbene, Rossellini gives us a singular vision of antiquity, one that’s downright avant-garde. Part of Classical Cinema

title: GALAXIE
description: A pinnacle of the art of filmic portraiture, Gregory Markopoulos’s GALAXIE comprises thirty short portraits of men and women from across the spectrum of the mid-1960s cultural scene in New York City. Its subjects include many of Markopoulos’s fellow experimental filmmakers – Storm De Hirsch, George & Mike Kuchar, Jonas Mekas, Shirley Clarke, Amy Taubin, and Ed Emshwiller – as well as figures from the literary and art worlds, including Parker Tyler, Jasper Johns, W.H. Auden, Allen Ginsberg, Kenneth Kelman, Maurice Sendak, Susan Sontag, and others. In keeping with Markopoulos’s short-form masterpieces MING GREEN, BLISS, and SORROWS, each of the individual portraits in GALAXIE was edited entirely in-camera, a near-miraculous feat given the intricate use of multiple layers of superimposition, all of it achieved by rewinding and making additional passes through the single 100-foot (ca. 3-minute) roll of 16mm film during the shoot. Initially intending to produce only a handful of portraits, Markopoulos ended up filming 40 different chapters, and ultimately incorporated the first 30 into the completed work (presented in the order they were created). Each of the portraits represents an exquisite visual record of the encounter between subject and filmmaker, while the film as a whole provides an extraordinary opportunity to observe the gradual development of Markopoulos’s approach to portraiture and in-camera editing.

title: Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut
description: Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, The Devils lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. The restoration many believed would never happen reaffirms Russell’s incendiary masterpiece as among the most overwhelming and uncompromising achievements in British cinema. Assembled from original camera negative, this 4k restoration is Ken Russell’s 2004 preferred edit. Picture and sound restoration by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother
description: From writer-director Bassam Tariq, Your Mother, Your Mother, Your Mother stars Mahershala Ali as Latif, a devoutly religious hitman who struggles to balance work, faith and fatherhood. When his wife dies, he embarks on a desperate journey across Houston to protect his children, confronting the forces closing in around him - and the beliefs threatening to unravel within.

title: DRILLER KILLER

The rent is due, the painting will not come together and the band next door will not stop. For a downtown artist hanging on by his fingernails, New York’s constant noise starts sounding like a command.
Abel Ferrara stars in his own grimy portrait of creative collapse, where punk rehearsal rooms and cramped apartments matter as much as the notorious violence. This is horror made out of unpaid bills, sleepless nights and a city coming apart. A raw document of late-seventies downtown life with a power tool at its centre.

Winner of the Grand Prix at Cannes and an international pop phenomenon, Oldboy was a revenge thriller unlike any that had come before, featuring passages of pure bravura filmmaking (that one-shot hallway donnybrook!) and surreal sicko humor that’ll put you off of sushi for a while. “Put together with brutally uncompromising style [and] the cold-steel edge of a knife against your throat. Written in the wreckage of the Civil War, the 14th Amendment was meant to codify the promise of freedom and citizenship. Instead, it has become a permanent argument. Oscar nominee DuVernay’s new documentary pulls this fight out of the footnotes and into the present, chronicling a vicious battle that has raged for more than 150 years. Threading deep archival scholarship with today’s headlines, 14TH brings together legal minds, politicians, historians and cultural voices to explore a question America still hasn’t settled: Who gets to belong?

title: Ben'imana
description: In 2012, eighteen years after the genocide against the Tutsi, a Rwandan village is still learning how to live with itself. Vénéranda has spent years helping survivors and the families of those responsible speak the words that were never said between them. However, forgiveness comes easier when it’s someone else’s story. When her own daughter’s future becomes entangled with the past, Vénéranda is forced to find her own words at last. Spanning three generations of women, BEN’IMANA is an intimate portrait of inherited silence — and the fragile question of whether people who have survived the unspeakable together can still build a life side by side.

title: Josephine
description: After eight-year-old Josephine witnesses a violent assault in San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park, the trauma begins to reshape her world, and her fear and confusion slowly unravel the household around her. Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan star as her parents in Beth de Araújo’s acclaimed drama, winner of both the Grand Jury Prize and the Audience Award at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival.

title: Naza
description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them. We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA ’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence. — Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

Returning home after sixteen years of exile in the US, Thomas Mann has to face not only a divided fatherland, but also a deep fracture within his own family.

title: Who Killed Alex Odeh?
description: In October 1985, Santa Ana, California was shaken by a brazen act of political violence when a Palestinian American, Alex Odeh, a beloved teacher and community leader, was killed by a tripwire bomb planted in his office. Despite clear evidence and identified suspects, the case was never solved. Who Killed Alex Odeh? reopens the mystery, tracking a renewed investigation in real time as new leads emerge, long-buried records come to light, and the forces behind a political assassination are finally confronted. Unfolding like a detective thriller, the film weaves archival footage, firsthand testimony, and new reporting to expose the violent fundamentalist networks behind the attack and the institutional failures that protected them. As the investigation deepens, the story widens to reveal how the extremist ideology that fueled Odeh’s murder did not disappear - it evolved, gaining traction and legitimacy in the modern political landscape. Directed by Jason Osder and William Lafi Youmans, a Jewish American and a Palestinian American, Who Killed Alex Odeh? is both a gripping cold-case pursuit and a timely examination of political violence, asking what it means when acts of terror go unresolved, and how justice denied continues to shape the world we live in.
director: Jason Osder and William Lafi Youmans

title: Minotaur
description: Russia, 2022. Corporate executive Gleb finds himself under siege on all fronts: haunted by suspicions that his wife is unfaithful and facing a demand to draft a quota of employees for war. Though desperate to keep his hands clean, his struggle to reassert control accelerates toward violence.

title: Mulholland Dr.
description: A dark-haired woman (Laura Elena Harring) is left amnesiac after a car crash. She wanders the streets of Los Angeles in a daze before taking refuge in an apartment. There she is discovered by Betty (Naomi Watts), a wholesome Midwestern blonde who has come to the City of Angels seeking fame as an actress. Together, the two attempt to solve the mystery of Rita's true identity. The story is set in a dream-like Los Angeles, spoilt neither by traffic jams nor smog.

title: Off-Circuit: My Wife Cries
description: A phone call brings Thomas to a hospital, where he finds his wife Carla in tears. As the circumstances of her accident come into focus, so too does a relationship whose familiar terms suddenly seem uncertain. From this deceptively simple premise, Angela Schanelec constructs a relationship drama that resists the conventions of the genre in favour of something decidedly more elliptical. As conversations circle what remains unspoken; gestures and silences come increasingly to the fore with a spellbinding intensity. My Wife Cries is at once formally audacious and acutely attentive to the emotional lives of its characters and how quickly intimacy can give way to estrangement. The screening on Friday 20 November will be followed by an in-person Q&A with Angela Schanelec.

Settling in an isolated coastal village, they form a bond with their neighbors, the Halbergs. When their daughter Elia appears at school with bruises, suspicions arise about the family's strict religious upbringing. Fjord explores clashing worldviews, conformity, tolerance, and the boundaries of freedom and intimacy.

As Langston hunts down the elusive gift, he runs into mailman Myron (Sinbad), another father on the same quest. With the clock winding down, Langston's moral code is tested as he starts to learn the real meaning of Christmas.

title: Funeral Parade presents "The Long Day Closes"
description: For the festive season, Funeral Parade is proud to present The Long Day Closes, Terence Davies’ bittersweet elegy to cinema-going and queer childhood. Drawn from Davies’ own recollections of the mid-1950s, the film centres on Bud, a lonely boy growing up in working-class Liverpool. Bullied at school and largely friendless, he finds solace in trips to the local cinema and the faraway glamour of Hollywood. His loving family are also a source of comfort but, as he becomes aware of his burgeoning sexuality, Bud must ultimately confront his guilt, shame, and fear alone. Beautifully rendered from a child’s-eye-view, The Long Day Closes is a haunting and tender work of poetic cinema. With intro from curator Sarah Cleary.

title: PRESENCES + DOPPELGANGER
description: Joe Gibbons PRESENCES 1974-90, 45 min, Super 8mm-to-16mm blow-up. Preserved by Anthology Film Archives with support from the Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts and the National Film Preservation Foundation. A long-term project started in the 1970s, PRESENCES compiles a series of portrait films featuring the filmmaker’s colleagues, friends, and family. A stepchild of sorts to Andy Warhol’s SCREEN TESTS, in these silent films Gibbons places each subject in front of a Super 8 camera and then exits the room, leaving his stars to their own devices. Look out for the filmmaker’s parents, filmmakers Peter Kubelka and Tony Conrad, and many other faces from the filmmaker’s past. Preceded by: Peggy Ahwesh DOPPELGANGER 1987, 8 min, Super 8mm-to-16mm. Preserved by Anthology Film Archives with support from New York Women in Film and Television’s (NYWIFT) Women’s Film Preservation Fund. “It’s a portrait of my friend Renate, who was born in Berlin and spent her early childhood playing in the rubble after WW2. She tells stories and recites entries from her diary in both English and German, evoking history, trauma and lost loves. Shot in long verité-like takes, in Super 8 sound, with several color hand processed scenes.” –Peggy Ahwesh Total running time: ca. 55 min.

title: EVEREST: THE OTHER SIDE
description: Elite ski mountaineers Jim Morrison and Hilaree Nelson fell deeply in love while reaching the pinnacle of their sport. Their drive sharpened into a shared dream: to climb and ski the direct North Face of Everest – the most difficult and dangerous climb on the mountain and the most coveted ski line on earth. Thousands have summited the mountain via Nepal’s southeast ridge, but only a handful have ever reached the top by this route — and no one has successfully skied down. Already known for their extraordinary feats in the mountains and no strangers to loss, Morrison and Nelson stake everything on this daunting challenge. From National Geographic Documentary Films and Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi and Jimmy Chin — the Oscar-winning filmmakers behind FREE SOLO and MERU — EVEREST: THE OTHER SIDE is an intimate portrait of two people bound by love, ambition and the pursuit of the impossible.

Threading deep archival scholarship with today’s headlines, 14TH brings together legal minds, politicians, historians and cultural voices to explore a question America still hasn’t settled: Who gets to belong?

description: If you’re nice, you get presents from the Big Guy. If you’re naughty, you get justice. In 2022’s bare-knuckle holiday sensation, VIOLENT NIGHT, an embittered Santa, armed with lethal combat skills, took out a team of mercenaries to rescue a girl and her family. Now, not-so-jolly Saint Nick suits up again to take on a ruthless gangster (Emmy and Golden Globe nominee Jared Harris) terrorizing the merchants of the Silver Bell Mall. But when Santa forgets the true meaning of Christmas, he finds himself in the heart of a lively mall community in desperate need of his help. Sapped of his magic, he’ll need another way to take on the goons threatening the mall, and time is running out. Santa has to rediscover his faith in goodness and call in some last-minute reinforcements from the one person no baddie wants to tangle with: Mrs. Claus (Emmy and Golden Globe nominee Kristen Bell).

title: EAT + BLOW JOB
description: Andy Warhol EAT 1964, 35 min, 16mm, silent “A portrait of artist Robert Indiana, EAT is one of the classics of Warhol’s minimalist cinema. As Indiana slowly eats one mushroom, the action is rendered mysterious by Warhol’s decision to assemble the rolls out of order, so the mushroom appears to magically renew itself from time to time.” –Callie Angell, MoMA Andy Warhol BLOW JOB 1964, 41 min, 16mm-to-DCP, silent. Collection of The Andy Warhol Museum, Pittsburgh; Contribution The Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts, Inc. “Warhol’s unmoving camera remains focused in close-up on the head of a young man, never descending below his shoulders to show the sex act advertised by the film’s title, which is nevertheless legible, in slow motion, in the changing expressions passing across his face. By wittily restricting what his camera sees, Warhol frustrates the expectations of porn fans and film censors alike, while simultaneously implicating both audiences in the same illicit desire.” –Callie Angell, MoMA Total running time: ca. 75 min.

title: Prince Charles Cinema Film Quiz
description: Put your cinematic knowledge to the test with The Prince Charles Cinema Film Quiz! This is a full-blown, no-holds-barred celebration of cinematic chaos, cult classics, and endless movie trivia. Hosted by Chevy Mclaren live in the heart of London cinema - this is your chance to test your film knowledge in this night of movie madness! Expect limited-edition PCC merch, free cinema tickets, exclusive movie prizes, live performances, and bonkers audience games. Bring your cinephile friends (teams up to 5), grab a drink, and prepare to scream, guess, act, and laugh your way through the most chaotic quiz night in London!

description: To mark Worlds AIDS Day and the first anniversary of the passing of the pioneering film maker Rosa von Praunheim, Pink Palace has joined forces with the Goethe Institute London to present this powerful and uncompromising documentary look at the AIDS activism happening in the late 80’s. title: Wild Horse Nine (15) (AD)
description: Two eccentric CIA agents ( John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell ) await orders on Easter Island, on the cusp of yet another military coup in Martin McDonagh 's latest dark comedy.

title: Phantom Thread
description: Renowned dressmaker Reynolds Woodcock and his sister Cyril are at the center of British fashion in 1950s London -- dressing royalty, movie stars, heiresses, socialites and debutantes. Women come and go in Woodcock's life, providing the confirmed bachelor with inspiration and companionship. His carefully tailored existence soon gets disrupted by Alma, a young and strong-willed woman who becomes his muse and lover.

title: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother
description: From writer-director Bassam Tariq, Your Mother, Your Mother, Your Mother stars Mahershala Ali as Latif, a devoutly religious hitman who struggles to balance work, faith and fatherhood. When his wife dies, he embarks on a desperate journey across Houston to protect his children, confronting the forces closing in around him - and the beliefs threatening to unravel within.

title: Josephine
description: After eight-year-old Josephine witnesses a violent assault in San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park, the trauma begins to reshape her world, and her fear and confusion slowly unravel the household around her. Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan star as her parents in Beth de Araújo’s acclaimed drama, winner of both the Grand Jury Prize and the Audience Award at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival.

title: MORGIANA
description:
Two sisters inherit a fortune. One inherits a murderous jealousy. A slow poison and an increasingly unreliable conscience turn their ornate household into a trap from which even the family cat seems unable to look away.
Iva Janžurová plays both women in Juraj Herz’s intoxicating Gothic fairy tale. Distorting lenses, lavish costumes and colour that seems to seep into the characters’ minds make beauty itself feel dangerous. A poisoned jewel of Czech cinema, where sibling rivalry becomes a hallucination and every sumptuous room conceals another reason to be afraid.

title: Prima Facie
description: A young, ambitious trial lawyer (Cynthia Erivo) brilliantly navigates the ruthless London court system where she is unmatched in her defense of the accused, including men charged with sexual assault. Just as her career is taking off, a life-altering event forces her to reckon with her belief in the judicial system that was once the core of her identity.

title: Tangles
description: Mon, Nov 23: Sneak preview + extended intro by Julia Louis-Dreyfus at 8:40! Mon, Nov 23: Sneak preview + extended intro by Julia Louis-Dreyfus at 9:05! Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Sarah Silverman, Abbi Jacobson, Seth Rogen and Bryan Cranston voice a family struggling with their mother’s Alzheimer’s diagnosis in this deeply moving, animated adaptation of Sarah Leavitt’s acclaimed graphic novel. Regular engagement begins January 15th, 2027.

title: The Devils
description: All screenings on a new 35mm print of the 4K restoration of the film. An enduring, singular masterpiece of cinema starring Academy Award-winner Vanessa Redgrave and Oliver Reed, KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption – and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell. Assembled from the original camera negative, this new 4K restoration presents Ken Russell’s definitive vision of The Devils by referencing the edit he privately constructed in 2004. The film’s sound has been remastered from original English Composite 35mm Mag Film, transferred at 96kHz, plus other original film elements in selected spots as needed. The Picture and Sound restoration was performed by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color, and Warner Bros. Sound.

New to the job of tee-girl, she wanders the immaculate grounds sampling the club’s luxuries as its members engage in a complex dance with the doting and subservient staff. But something is rotting beneath the pristine fairways, as Isabel discovers when she tries to return a mislaid golf club to its patriarchal director, Dr. Palanca. The deeper she journeys into its most exclusive corners, the closer she gets to the violent truths of the club, her native Philippines, and her own past. title: Off-Circuit: My Wife Cries
description: A phone call brings Thomas to a hospital, where he finds his wife Carla in tears. As the circumstances of her accident come into focus, so too does a relationship whose familiar terms suddenly seem uncertain. From this deceptively simple premise, Angela Schanelec constructs a relationship drama that resists the conventions of the genre in favour of something decidedly more elliptical. As conversations circle what remains unspoken; gestures and silences come increasingly to the fore with a spellbinding intensity. My Wife Cries is at once formally audacious and acutely attentive to the emotional lives of its characters and how quickly intimacy can give way to estrangement. The screening on Friday 20 November will be followed by an in-person Q&A with Angela Schanelec.

Join Kermit the Frog, Miss Piggy, and all the hilarious Muppets in this merry, magical version of Charles Dickens' classic tale. Academy Award® winner Michael Caine (Best Supporting Actor) gives a performance that's anything but "bah, humbug!" as greedy, penny-pinching Ebenezer Scrooge. One fateful Christmas Eve, Scrooge is visited by the Ghosts of Christmas Past, Present, and Future. Together with kind, humble Bob Cratchit (Kermit the Frog) and his family, the Spirits open Scrooge's eyes -- and his heart -- to the true meaning of Christmas. Filled with original music and dazzling special effects, THE MUPPET CHRISTMAS CAROL will become a holiday tradition your family will treasure all the days of the year. Featuring the film’s famous long-lost song ‘When Love is Gone’! ------ As always you can expect SING ALONG performances of this new version of THE MUPPET CHRISTMAS CAROL this Christmas - and now we don't need to pretend that we weren't going to just play the lost scene regardless! Performances will feature a Hosted Pre-Show with our very own Father Christmas, where you will be prepped on what to do throughout the film. A stranger arrives at the home of a family already doing an impressive job of destroying itself. The father wants a television scoop, the son terrorises his mother, and any remaining boundaries have long since collapsed. Somehow, their visitor seems to know exactly what they need.
Takashi Miike turns the domestic drama into a filthy digital-video experiment, pushing scenes past outrage until they become horribly, absurdly funny. Its cheap-camera intimacy makes every violation feel uncomfortably close, while a perverse tenderness emerges from the wreckage. One of the great acts of sabotage against the respectable family film.

In seventeenth-century France, charismatic priest Urbain Grandier becomes the target of witchcraft accusations after a convent’s supposed demonic possession. As Sister Jeanne’s obsession with him ...

Amid stifling heat and pervasive drought, she lines up golf balls for powerful men to drive into the carefully manicured verdant horizon. Between shifts, she wanders the immaculate grounds, sampling its luxuries and exploring its liminal spaces. The club’s members, including an industrialist and his expatriate niece, the president and his pampered wife and a slew of Chinese tourists, engage in a complex dance with the doting and subservient staff. But something is rotting beneath the pristine fairways of the elite resort, as Isabel discovers when she tries to return a mislaid golf club to its patriarchal director, Dr. Palanca. The deeper she journeys into its most exclusive corners, the closer she gets to the violent truths of the club, her native Philippines and her own past. title: MILLENNIUM FILM JOURNAL NO. 84 LAUNCH SCREENING
description: This program consists of films discussed in Millennium Film Journal No. 84: Circulation. Celebrating 60 years of the Millennium Film Workshop, the issue surveys the landscape of contemporary experimental film distribution, and considers what it means to make experimental images today. The Millennium Film Workshop gratefully acknowledges support for the Millennium Film Journal by the following individuals and organizations: Deborah and Dan Duane; Walter and Karla Goldschmidt Foundation; C. Noll Brinckmann, anonymous donors; and New York State Council on the Arts. To support the publication of the Millennium Film Journal with a tax-deductible gift, please visit: https://millenniumfilmjournal.com/donations/donation-form/. For subscriptions to the bi-annual Millennium Film Journal, visit: https://millenniumfilmjournal.com/individual-subscriptions/ Programmed by Grahame Weinbren, Vince Warne, and MFJ editors. Chantal Akerman PORTRAIT D’UNE PARESSEUSE (SLOTH) (1986, 7 min, digital) “Akerman’s contribution to the anthology film SEVEN WOMEN, SEVEN SINS (which also features shorts by the formidable Helke Sander, Bette Gordon, and Valie Export) is an amusing portrait of the director trying to overcome her own laziness (i.e., to get out of her bed by noon) in order to make her film about sloth, all while her partner Sonia Wieder-Atherton is hard at work. (The scenario produces Akerman’s oft-quoted line, ‘In order to make cinema, one must get out of bed.’” –TIFF Marthe Peters HENRY IS A GIRL WHO LIKES TO SLEEP (2026, 14 min, digital) “One sleeps so as not to have to exist: ‘I do think going to sleep is one of the very best things for people who are unhappy.’ Sleep here is not laziness, it is not carelessness, nor is it linked to sin; it is intimacy and comfort; it is a body that curls up like a cat to overcome vulnerability and everything else. Like a snail that retreats when the outside world is all a threat, the narrator also wants to curl up in her blankets and withdraw into herself. This letter addressed to Henry seems, after all, an attempt to overcome the fear of feeling in the form of a declaration of (self-)love to a cat.” –Margarida Moz, INDIELISBOA INTERNATIONAL FILM FESTIVAL Andrea Luka Zimmerman WHILE THE GODS WERE BUSY WITH ANOTHER CHILD (2026, 25 min, digital) “Once I make a film, I must let it go and allow it to spark conversation, critique, or whatever responses people bring to it. Showing it to my students and to others was incredibly enriching, and I’m aware that public-facing discussions may bring a range of reactions, especially around survivorhood and visibility. For me, though, it’s not about self-presentation but about resisting the individualization that shapes so much of our culture. In my films I create spaces for people who are usually marginalized or spoken about in limiting ways, and I use myself in that same framework. I grew up being told that leaving school at 13 or 16 meant you were destined to become a criminal or a failure. Then, if you become something else, people say, ‘You did so well, you made it.’ It’s like a binary society. But lots of lives are much more enmeshed in each other. We need each other, right?” –Andrea Luka Zimmerman, interviewed by Georgia Korossi for London Short Festival 2026 Charlotte Pryce THE GLOAMING (2026, 14 min, digital) “Pryce’s films are known for being as soft as they are meticulous, made out of both filmed footage and manual manipulation. Given how Pryce is so rooted in nonconformity and imagination, her attention to the surface of the film’s skin stands out. By themselves, her films are all-consuming handcrafted windows into unpeered realms, that may reach the audience in layers. From the presence of a fluid image on a single subject, whether it is an animal, a plant, a book or an obscure unnamed substance, many others follow suit and outwardly open the field of vision. Pryce…looks at the craft as an artisan storyteller. It takes both a lot of control and attentiveness to let go and fully embrace the multi-sensory act of discovery of works best understood as constructed fictions.” –Susana Bessa, “Charlotte Pryce rips through the veil of invisibility,” MFJ 84 Barbara Hammer SAPPHO (1978, 7 min, 16mm-to-digital) “Barbara was so interested in experimenting with form and particularly the materiality of film and of filmmaking. Her last piece – really, her masterpiece – was EVIDENTIARY BODIES (2016). In that work, her body literally dissolves visually into a film strip. The idea is not only BARBARA FOREVER, but Barbara’s legacy – that she would live on in her work. Her work is so personal, it is so much about herself, her body, her sex, the things she’s discovering. But she was also very wide ranging in how she approached the materials.” –Brydie O’Connor, interviewed by S. Topiary Landberg, “Life-affirming art is the point!”, MFJ 84 SAPPHO will be preceded by an excerpt from Brydie O’Connor’s LOVE BARBARA (2026). Total running time: ca. 75 min.
