description: A masterpiece of cunning and suspense… Miles Cullen (Elliott Gould, The Long Goodbye) discovers how interesting life can be when he is transformed from mild-mannered bank teller into daring, ingenious bank robber in a matter of seconds. Held up at the bank by the criminal Reikle (Christopher Plummer, Ordeal by Innocence), Miles manages to stash most of the money in a deposit box first. When Reikle realizes he’s been shortchanged, he plans to take revenge—and a great battle of wits ensues. To keep the money, Miles reaches new heights of courage, seducing the robber’s girlfriend (Céline Lomez, Plague) and his boss’s mistress (Susannah York, The Killing of Sister George). Filled with equal parts intrigue, romance and unexpected twists, this chilling psychological thriller also features comedy legend John Candy (Delirious) in an early film role. The screenplay by future filmmaker extraordinaire Curtis Hanson (L.A. Confidential) was based on the book Think of a Number by Anders Bodelsen. Wonderfully directed by Daryl Duke (Payday).

title: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother
description: From writer-director Bassam Tariq, Your Mother, Your Mother, Your Mother stars Mahershala Ali as Latif, a devoutly religious hitman who struggles to balance work, faith and fatherhood. When his wife dies, he embarks on a desperate journey across Houston to protect his children, confronting the forces closing in around him - and the beliefs threatening to unravel within.

title: Prima Facie
description: A young, ambitious trial lawyer (Cynthia Erivo) brilliantly navigates the ruthless London court system where she is unmatched in her defense of the accused, including men charged with sexual assault. Just as her career is taking off, a life-altering event forces her to reckon with her belief in the judicial system that was once the core of her identity.

title: And Your Bird Can Sing preceded by August 8th
THE VIRGIN SUICIDES
description: A group of male friends become obsessed with five mysterious sisters who are sheltered by their strict, religious parents.

title: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth 35mm
description: Brad Pitt returns to his Academy Award-winning role as Cliff Booth, only this time it’s 1977 and it’s a very different Hollywood. Directed by David Fincher from a screenplay by Quentin Tarantino, the film also stars Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Carla Gugino, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II and Peter Weller.

title: Minotaur
description: Russia, 2022. Corporate executive Gleb finds himself under siege on all fronts: haunted by suspicions that his wife is unfaithful and facing a demand to draft a quota of employees for war. Though desperate to keep his hands clean, his struggle to reassert control accelerates toward violence.

title: Who Killed Alex Odeh?
description: In October 1985, Santa Ana, California was shaken by a brazen act of political violence when a Palestinian American, Alex Odeh, a beloved teacher and community leader, was killed by a tripwire bomb planted in his office. Despite clear evidence and identified suspects, the case was never solved. Who Killed Alex Odeh? reopens the mystery, tracking a renewed investigation in real time as new leads emerge, long-buried records come to light, and the forces behind a political assassination are finally confronted. Unfolding like a detective thriller, the film weaves archival footage, firsthand testimony, and new reporting to expose the violent fundamentalist networks behind the attack and the institutional failures that protected them. As the investigation deepens, the story widens to reveal how the extremist ideology that fueled Odeh’s murder did not disappear - it evolved, gaining traction and legitimacy in the modern political landscape. Directed by Jason Osder and William Lafi Youmans, a Jewish American and a Palestinian American, Who Killed Alex Odeh? is both a gripping cold-case pursuit and a timely examination of political violence, asking what it means when acts of terror go unresolved, and how justice denied continues to shape the world we live in.
director: Jason Osder and William Lafi Youmans

title: La Haine
description: Hatred breeds hatred... 24 hours in the lives of three young men in the French suburbs the day after a violent riot.

title: Big Trouble in Little China
description: Kurt Russell plays hard-boiled truck driver Jack Burton, who gets caught in a bizarre conflict within, and underneath, San Francisco's Chinatown. An ancient Chinese prince and Chinatown crime lord has kidnapped a beautiful green-eyed woman, who is the fiancee to Jack's best friend. Jack must help his friend rescue the girl before the evil Lo Pan uses her to break the ancient curse that keeps him a fleshless and immortal spirit.

title: You Can See Everything (15) (AD)
description: 34 days before she’s sent to prison, notorious Silicon Valley founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a skeptical film crew led by Nathan Fielder to document her every move.

title: Off-Circuit: My Wife Cries
description: A phone call brings Thomas to a hospital, where he finds his wife Carla in tears. As the circumstances of her accident come into focus, so too does a relationship whose familiar terms suddenly seem uncertain. From this deceptively simple premise, Angela Schanelec constructs a relationship drama that resists the conventions of the genre in favour of something decidedly more elliptical. As conversations circle what remains unspoken; gestures and silences come increasingly to the fore with a spellbinding intensity. My Wife Cries is at once formally audacious and acutely attentive to the emotional lives of its characters and how quickly intimacy can give way to estrangement. The screening on Friday 20 November will be followed by an in-person Q&A with Angela Schanelec.

title: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth 35mm
description: Brad Pitt returns to his Academy Award-winning role as Cliff Booth, only this time it’s 1977 and it’s a very different Hollywood. Directed by David Fincher from a screenplay by Quentin Tarantino, the film also stars Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Carla Gugino, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II and Peter Weller.

title: Minotaur (15) (AD)
description: After a nine-year absence having fled his native Russia and gone into exile, Andrey Zvyagintsev makes his long-awaited return; a modern reimagining of Claude Chabrol’s La femme infidèle .

title: You Can See Everything
description: Thirty-four days before she’s sent to prison, notorious Silicon Valley founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a sceptical film crew to document her every move. What begins as an intimate portrait of an enigmatic felon becomes a mind-bending three-year journey into the abyss. From boundary-pushing directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim comes You Can See Everything .

title: Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut
description: Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, The Devils lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. The restoration many believed would never happen reaffirms Russell’s incendiary masterpiece as among the most overwhelming and uncompromising achievements in British cinema. Assembled from original camera negative, this 4k restoration is Ken Russell’s 2004 preferred edit. Picture and sound restoration by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: Three Days of the Condor
description: On a seemingly ordinary day, Joe Turner (Robert Redford), a quiet CIA codebreaker, walks into his workplace and finds that all of his coworkers have been murdered. Horrified, Joe flees the scene and tries to tell his supervisors about the tragedy. Unfortunately, he soon learns that CIA higher-ups were involved in the murders. With no one to trust, and a merciless hit man (Max von Sydow) close on his tail, Joe must somehow survive long enough to figure out why his own agency wants him dead.

title: Once Upon A Time In The West
The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping
description: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping will revisit the world of Panem twenty-four years before the events of The Hunger Games, starting on the morning of the reaping of the Fiftieth Hunger Games, also known as the Second Quarter Quell.

title: Wild Horse Nine
description: Set in 1973, during the US’s attempt to overthrow the Chilean government, a hitman for the US government with connections to the JFK assassination suddenly realizes that his own people have put a hit on him to cover up the mess.

title: Fjord
description: Mihai and Lisbet Gheorghiu, a Romanian-Norwegian Pentecostal couple, move with their five children from Romania to Norway after Mihai’s parents die, seeking closeness to Lisbet’s family, who share their faith. Settling in an isolated coastal village, they form a bond with their neighbors, the Halbergs. When their daughter Elia appears at school with bruises, suspicions arise about the family's strict religious upbringing. Fjord explores clashing worldviews, conformity, tolerance, and the boundaries of freedom and intimacy.

title: Disney's Hexed
description: An awkward teenage boy and his Type-A mom discover that what makes him unusual might be magical powers that will turn their lives and a secret world of magic upside down.

title: Wild Horse Nine
description: Set in 1973, during the US’s attempt to overthrow the Chilean government, a hitman for the US government with connections to the JFK assassination suddenly realizes that his own people have put a hit on him to cover up the mess.

title: Wild Horse Nine (15) (AD)
description: Two eccentric CIA agents ( John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell ) await orders on Easter Island, on the cusp of yet another military coup in Martin McDonagh 's latest dark comedy.

title: NAZA (15)
description: Cloaked in darkness on the rooftops of Tel Aviv, Israeli journalist Yuval Abraham conducts shattering one-on-one interviews with Israeli soldiers and intelligence personnel.

title: Gremlins
description: A gadget salesman is looking for a special gift for his son and finds one at a store in Chinatown. The shopkeeper is reluctant to sell him the `mogwai' but sells it to him with the warning to never expose him to bright light, water, or to feed him after midnight. All of this happens and the result is a gang of gremlins that decide to tear up the town on Christmas Eve.

title: SNAPSHOT + Q&A
description:
In the blood-soaked streets of Victorian London, an amateur inventor turns his primitive moving-image camera on a group of women investigating the Whitechapel murders. Their theory is that Jack the Ripper is something considerably worse than a man. What the camera records offers little reassurance.
Joseph Archer and writer Cathy Wippell drag found-footage horror back to the birth of cinema, using pinhole images, unreliable testimony and newspaper hysteria to make the familiar streets feel dangerously unfamiliar. A resourceful British nightmare in which every damaged frame leaves something dreadful just outside the picture.
Followed by a Q&A with director Joseph Archer and writer Cathy Wippell, hosted by Craig Williams.

title: Focker-in-Law
description: A young man named Henry, son of Greg and Pam Focker, faces family chaos when he decides to marry a strong-willed woman who appears to be his complete mismatch.

title: A Tale of Winter
description: Felicie and Charles have a whirlwind holiday romance. Due to a mix-up on addresses they lose contact, and five years later at Christmas-time Felicie is living with her mother in a cold Paris with a daughter as a reminder of that long-ago summer. For male companionship she oscillates between hairdresser Maxence and the intellectual Loic, but seems unable to commit to either as the memory of Charles and what might have been hangs over everything.

title: "Wuthering Heights" (15) + ScreenTalk
description: The bold and exciting adaptation of the gothic masterpiece returns to our screens with a ScreenTalk from director Emerald Fennell and creative team on how their striking vision was brought to life.

title: Ebenezer: A Christmas Carol
description: A thrilling ghost story set in Dickens' London, following one man's supernatural journey to face his past, present and future as he fights for a second chance at redemption.

title: Armenian FF: From Shadows to Light
Pereda: Perpetual Motion
description: Gabino lives with his mother in Mexico City and makes a precarious living working as a mover with his friend Paco, ferrying other people’s possessions from one home to another. Between jobs, arguments over money and the lingering search for his missing dog, the pair remain constantly occupied while somehow getting nowhere. Pereda turns this modest premise into a dryly funny study of labour, class and frustrated mobility, finding an absurd circularity in the routines of everyday life. Movement is everywhere – furniture changes hands, people come and go, stories are told and retold – yet meaningful change remains tantalisingly out of reach. Featuring Pereda regulars Gabino Rodríguez and Teresa Sánchez, Perpetual Motion brings into focus the repetitions, ambiguities and everyday rituals that would continue to reverberate throughout his cinema.

title: Take Me Home
description: Anna (Anna Sargent making her acting debut), a middle-aged Korean adoptee with a cognitive disability, cares for her aging parents in a fragile balance of meeting one another’s needs. Alongside her sister Emily (Ali Ahn) and her father (Victor Slezak), they must confront challenging questions about the future, but she remains determined to build a life where all of them can thrive.

title: 4 MONTHS, 3 WEEKS AND 2 DAYS
description: Romanian filmmaker Cristian Mungiu shot to international prominence with this rigorously realistic Palme d’Or–winning second feature. In 1987, during the dictatorship of Nicolae Ceaușescu, college roommates Otilia (Anamaria Marinca) and Găbița (Laura Vasiliu) seek an illegal abortion for Găbița. In unflinching but empathetic detail, the film recounts the events of twenty-four perilous hours in their lives, culminating in their encounter with a manipulative and menacing abortionist (Vlad Ivanov). With powerful performances that accentuate the characters’ flawed humanity, 4 MONTHS, 3 WEEKS AND 2 DAYS is a gutting account of the impossible choices women face when taking control of their bodies means breaking the law.

title: MONO NO AWARE XX: EAST FACING WEST
description: An orientation and a window into a Manhattan Chinatown block witnessed over two years, this debut of a cumulative work-in-progress unfolds as a microcosm of a changing immigrant neighborhood. This expanded cinema performance is part of MONO NO AWARE XX, the 20th anniversary bi-annual exhibition of expanded cinema organized by MONO NO AWARE. The event is all ages, free to attend, and open to the public. RSVP strongly encouraged @ www.mononoawarefilm.com Live percussion by Levy Lorenzo.

title: YOU CAN SEE EVERYTHING
description: Elizabeth Holmes would like to tell her side of the story. Nathan Fielder has a few questions.  Thirty-four days before she is due to begin her prison sentence for fraud, the Theranos founder invites Fielder and fellow filmmaker Lance Oppenheim into the home she shares with her partner, Billy Evans....

title: Daisies
description: An audacious and gleeful shock to the system, Věra Chytilová’s Czech New Wave masterpiece is punk as f*&k, but also as sweet, goofy, and girly as the name would imply. A truly absurd and kaleidoscopic endeavor, this film is a raw and riotous middle finger to authoritarianism, the patriarchy, and especially to reason.  Two young women embrace spitting in the face of convention and fall down a rabbit hole of gluttony, destruction, rebellion, and an unabashed pursuit of pleasure. With a visual style as anarchic as the subjects, this visual smorgasbord of varying film stocks, sporadic animation, and hallucinatory editing is essential big screen viewing.

title: Pink Palace: SANTA SANGRE
description: Pink Palace presents a film unlike anything you have seen before, a surrealist psychological horror tale from the master of the bizarre. Visually extraordinary, inventive but also tender and deeply human. Jodorowsky’s exploration of gender roles and androgyny have given this a cult queer following. ...

title: La Raulito
description: A tough and tender telling of the early life of Club Atlético Boca Juniors superfan Maria Esther Duffau who, as a teenager, hustled to survive on the mean streets of Buenos Aires between stints in juvie hall and the psych ward, adopting a male identity (the “Little Raul” of the title) along the way. “I feel like I’m in a perpetual quest to discover new (old) films depicting transmasc, butch, and gender nonconforming characters and stories. I first came across La Raulito in 2022, but it’s taken all these years to finally track it down and be able to show it. Like all of the films in this series, La Raulito has a wonderful quality of melodramatic earnestness. As someone who has always embraced sincerity in my own work as a filmmaker, I think this is one of the most beautiful and brave examples you’ll ever see of telling the story of a hero (a real-life national hero in Argentina) who you absolutely cannot resist falling in love with.” —Series curator Jenni Olson, queer film historian and archivist Introduction and Q&A with guest curator and filmmaker Jenni Olson moderated by filmmaker Julia Solomonoff on Sunday, October 25th Part of Jenni Olson Selects: Mini Masc

title: Sing-A-Long-A Rocky Horror Picture Show
description: THE ROCKY HORROR PICTURE SHOW SING ALONG is getting revamped in 2027 – for all future shows, CLICK HERE ! The Campest Cult Classic of all time gets the Singalonga treatment it’s been SCREAMING for! Featuring the film, starring Tim Curry, Susan Sarandon, Meatloaf and Richard O’Brien, it’s the most outrageous, riotous, kitsch, wonderful romp ever. If you’ve done The Time Warp before, you’ll never have done it quite like this! The evening begins with your host leading a vocal warm-up before they show you how to use your free interactive props bag. Fancy dress is not obligatory but highly recommended! Please Note : The 15 rating we have placed upon this screening is due to the Adult content of the hosted pre-show which may not be suitable for those under 15. Please Note : This is a screening of the movie not a live stage show. Also this screening may contain sudden loud noises and flashing lights.

title: Disney's Hexed
description: An awkward teenage boy and his Type-A mom discover that what makes him unusual might be magical powers that will turn their lives and a secret world of magic upside down.

title: THE WICKER MAN
description:
When a devout Christian police sergeant travels to the remote Scottish island of Summerisle to investigate the disappearance of a young girl, he encounters a close-knit community whose pagan beliefs and seasonal rituals stand in stark contrast to his own. As his investigation deepens, every answer seems only to raise more disturbing questions, leading him towards a revelation he could never have anticipated.
Directed by Robin Hardy from a screenplay by Anthony Shaffer, The Wicker Man overturns the conventions of the traditional horror film, replacing monsters and haunted houses with folklore, religious conflict and mounting psychological unease. Christopher Lee considered Lord Summerisle to be his finest performance, while Paul Giovanni's extraordinary folk-inspired soundtrack became inseparable from the film's haunting atmosphere. Initially released in a heavily truncated version, it has since been restored and is now widely regarded as one of the greatest British horror films ever made.

title: FiFF: Come Into My (Dressing) Room: A Post-Punk Trio
Focker-in-Law
description: A young man named Henry, son of Greg and Pam Focker, faces family chaos when he decides to marry a strong-willed woman who appears to be his complete mismatch.

title: Trading Places
description: Upper-crust executive Louis Winthorpe III (Dan Aykroyd) and down-and-out hustler Billy Ray Valentine (Eddie Murphy) are the subjects of a bet by successful brokers Mortimer (Don Ameche) and Randolph Duke (Ralph Bellamy). An employee of the Dukes, Winthorpe is framed by the brothers for a crime he didn't commit, with the siblings then installing the street-smart Valentine in his position. When Winthorpe and Valentine uncover the scheme, they set out to turn the tables on the Dukes.

When his wife dies, he embarks on a desperate journey across Houston to protect his children, confronting the forces closing in around him - and the beliefs threatening to unravel within.

Just as her career is taking off, a life-altering event forces her to reckon with her belief in the judicial system that was once the core of her identity.

title: Lemonade Blessing
description: Freshly tossed into private Catholic high school by his recently divorced mother, John must go from good boy to heinous sinner when he falls for a girl who requires him to commit sacrilegious acts in order to further their relationship.

title: Tetsuo: The Iron Man
description: That the world of the future was to be increasingly shaped by Asia was a central tenet of cyberpunk, and so it should come as no surprise that one of the greatest of cyberpunk films came from the Land of the Rising Sun. Man and machine feel the urge to merge in Tsukamoto’s utterly indescribable midnight movie staple, an assault-on-the-senses body horror running of the gauntlet which centers on an anonymous salaryman who begins to transform himself into a man of steel, his waking nightmare captured in twitchy camerawork and lurid, gritty black-and-white 16mm. A symphony of sex, steel, and scarification, set to a scraping industrial clangor. Part of A Cyberpunk Canon

title: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth 35mm
description: Brad Pitt returns to his Academy Award-winning role as Cliff Booth, only this time it’s 1977 and it’s a very different Hollywood. Directed by David Fincher from a screenplay by Quentin Tarantino, the film also stars Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Carla Gugino, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II and Peter Weller.

title: Angel's Egg
description: In an underwater city, a young girl takes care of a large egg she holds carefully in her arms. A boy with a gun arrives in search of a bird he saw in his dream. At first, it seems as if feelings of sympathy are developing between the two. Forty years after the film’s original release, Anime Limited is proud to present an all-new 4K restoration of the film, supervised by director Mamoru Oshii, in cinemas nationwide for the very first time. The film is a creative collaboration between acclaimed director Mamoru Oshii (Ghost in the Shell), who wrote and directed the feature, and revered artist Yoshitaka Amano (Final Fantasy, Vampire Hunter D). The film beautifully intertwines Oshii’s thematic reflections on philosophy and theology with Amano’s distinctive ink painting style, culminating in an arrestingly beautiful hand-drawn allegorical fantasy.

title: The Muppet Christmas Carol
description: 'Tis the season for love, laughter, and one of the most cherished stories of all time! Join Kermit the Frog, Miss Piggy, and all the hilarious Muppets in this merry, magical version of Charles Dickens' classic tale. Academy Award® winner Michael Caine (Best Supporting Actor) gives a performance that's anything but "bah, humbug!" as greedy, penny-pinching Ebenezer Scrooge. One fateful Christmas Eve, Scrooge is visited by the Ghosts of Christmas Past, Present, and Future. Together with kind, humble Bob Cratchit (Kermit the Frog) and his family, the Spirits open Scrooge's eyes -- and his heart -- to the true meaning of Christmas. Filled with original music and dazzling special effects, THE MUPPET CHRISTMAS CAROL will become a holiday tradition your family will treasure all the days of the year. Featuring the film’s famous long-lost song ‘When Love is Gone’! ------ As always you can expect SING ALONG performances of this new version of THE MUPPET CHRISTMAS CAROL this Christmas - and now we don't need to pretend that we weren't going to just play the lost scene regardless! Performances will feature a Hosted Pre-Show with our very own Father Christmas, where you will be prepped on what to do throughout the film. Costumes aren't mandatory, but 'Tis the season, and we love seeing you dressed up in your favourite Christmas Jumpers! All this, and a few more surprises up our sleeves, makes this one of the must-see events this Christmas! If you're wanting to Sing Along with The Muppet Christmas Carol, simply book for the performances marked SING ALONG [it's next to the start time]. All other screenings will be regular performances, and nothing will be written next to the start time.

title: THE MATCH FACTORY GIRL
description: Kaurismäki took his penchant for despairing character studies to unspeakably grim depths in the shockingly entertaining THE MATCH FACTORY GIRL. Kati Outinen is memorably impenetrable as Iris, whose grinding days as a cog in a factory wheel, and nights as a neglected daughter living with her parents, ultimately send her over the edge. Yet despite her transgressions, Kaurismäki makes Iris a compelling, even sympathetic figure. Bleak yet suffused with comic irony, THE MATCH FACTORY GIRL closes out the “Proletariat Trilogy” with a bang—and a whimper.

title: Eyes Wide Shut
description: In what would prove to be the coda to Stanley Kubrick’s masterful career, Eyes Wide Shut demanded an immersive level of commitment and trust from the director’s stars – Tom Cruise and Nicole Kidman – during the film’s grueling 15-month shoot in England. The two stars moved beyond their big screen charisma in order to inhabit their characters, peeling away at the psychological layers of trust and loyalty that protects the heart of a marriage. Set in Greenwich Village (recreated at Pinewood Studios in London) and beautifully captured by Larry Smith (Kubrick’s gaffer on Barry Lyndon and The Shining ), Cruise plays Dr. Bill Harford, who feels betrayed after his wife Alice (Nicole Kidman) confesses that she fantasized about having sex with another man, sending Bill into a dream-like excursion of sexual enticement and mystery, including masquerading into a secret society where sex is treated with a cult like indulgence – putting himself and his marriage in danger. A film that Martin Scorsese called “misunderstood,” Eyes Wide Shut creates a slow burn of discomfort that plays foil to the eroticism, sexual tension, and temptation that Kubrick explores.

title: Eyes Wide Shut
description: Stanley Kubrick's daring last film is many things. It is a compelling psychosexual journey. A haunting dreamscape. A riveting tale of suspense. A major milestone in the careers of stars Tom Cruise and Nicole Kidman. And "a worthy final chapter to a great director's career" (Roger Ebert). Cruise plays Dr William Hartford, who plunges into an erotic foray that threatens his marriage - and may even ensnare him in a lurid murder mystery - after his wife's (Kidman) admission of sexual longings. As the story sweeps from doubt and fear to self-discovery and reconciliation, Kubrick orchestrates it with masterful flourishes. Graceful tracking shots, controlled pacing, rich colours, startling images: bravura traits that make Kubrick a filmmaker for the ages are here to keep everyone's eyes wide shut.

title: Boogie Nights
description: In the San Fernando Valley in 1977, teenage busboy Eddie Adams (Mark Wahlberg) gets discovered by porn director Jack Horner (Burt Reynolds), who transforms him into adult-film sensation Dirk Diggler. Brought into a supportive circle of friends, including fellow actors Amber Waves (Julianne Moore), Rollergirl (Heather Graham) and Reed Rothchild (John C. Reilly), Dirk fulfills all his ambitions, but a toxic combination of drugs and egotism threatens to take him back down.

title: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth 35mm
description: Brad Pitt returns to his Academy Award-winning role as Cliff Booth, only this time it’s 1977 and it’s a very different Hollywood. Directed by David Fincher from a screenplay by Quentin Tarantino, the film also stars Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Carla Gugino, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II and Peter Weller.

title: DAYS OF HEAVEN
description: DAYS OF HEAVEN is a moving story about two men who love the same woman. Richard Gere, a fugitive from the slums of Chicago, finds himself pitted against a shy, rich Texan (Sam Shepard) for the love of Abby (Brooke Adams). An extraordinary cinematic achievement of sight and sound by writer/director Terrence Malick.

title: SHOGUN ASSASSIN
description:
After his wife is murdered by agents of a paranoid shogun, former executioner Ogami Ittō takes to the road with his young son Daigoro, pushing him through feudal Japan in a baby cart fitted with an alarming arsenal of hidden weapons. Pursued by ninja assassins and three fearsome Masters of Death, father and son carve a path through ambushes, betrayals and spectacular fountains of blood.
Created for American grindhouse audiences by re-editing and dubbing the first two Lone Wolf and Cub films, SHOGUN ASSASSIN transforms Kenji Misumi’s samurai epics into a lean, hallucinatory barrage of flashing blades, severed limbs and pulsing synthesiser music. Initially notorious in Britain for its extreme violence, the film became a midnight-movie classic whose influence can be felt everywhere from Wu-Tang Clan’s Liquid Swords to Quentin Tarantino’s Kill Bill.

title: The Muppet Christmas Carol
description: 'Tis the season for love, laughter, and one of the most cherished stories of all time! title: Home Alone
description: When bratty 8-year-old Kevin McCallister (Macaulay Culkin) acts out the night before a family trip to Paris, his mother (Catherine O'Hara) makes him sleep in the attic. After the McCallisters mistakenly leave for the airport without Kevin, he awakens to an empty house and assumes his wish to have no family has come true. But his excitement sours when he realizes that two con men (Joe Pesci, Daniel Stern) plan to rob the McCallister residence, and that he alone must protect the family home.

title: I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning
description: Childhood friends Patrick, Shiv, Rian, Oli, and Conor played together, skipped school together, and dreamt of the lives they would have one day. Now they’re thirty, and the future they imagined is slipping quietly out of reach.

title: Esther Anderson Retrospective: TWO GENTLEMAN SHARING + SHORT ENDS
description: For the opening night of The Esther Anderson Retrospective, join us in screen one for the special opportunity to watch her directorial debut Short Ends (1976) followed by the provocative 60s film by director Ted Kotcheff (and starring Esther Anderson) Two Gentlemen Sharing (1969).  Short Ends (1976)...

title: JUST LOOK UP
description: JUST LOOK UP follows Michael Greenberg, a brazen visionary and founder of Climate Defiance, a disruptive youth movement. In the tradition of Gandhi’s Satyagraha, the Civil Rights Movement, and ACT UP, they use radical nonviolent direct action to jolt society awake, calling out Big Oil, corporate CEO...

title: NEW YORKERS + BEFORE THE FIRST WORD
description: This program pairs two films, made a decade apart, that vividly demonstrate the vibrant, distinctive, and sometimes paradoxical nature of New York City’s neighborhoods: at once strikingly diverse and worldly, and yet close knit and self-enclosed. NEW YORKERS (1971), by filmmaker Michael Blackwood (who during his long career made several films about the city, as well as dozens of documentaries about artists, architects, and musicians), sets its sights on the Upper East Side, and in particular on the area in and around East 77th Street. BEFORE THE FIRST WORD (1982) – a co-production between WNET and the educational organization Learning Designs, and ostensibly a film designed as a teaching tool for journalism students – is set seventy-something blocks to the south, in Greenwich Village. Both films capture the degree to which their respective neighborhoods have developed specific cultures, institutions, and local networks to create a kind of shelter from the vertiginous, unceasing forces of change that animate Manhattan – and the degree to which they’re nevertheless unmistakably subject to the evolution that is the fate of all city neighborhoods, and to the more aggressive, inorganic tides of gentrification that have increasingly transformed the city over the past fifty years. Michael Blackwood NEW YORKERS 1971, 29 min, 16mm-to-DCP Tom Simon BEFORE THE FIRST WORD 1982, 29 min, video Total running time: ca. 60 min.

title: Armenian FF: British Armenian Focus shorts
BURST CITY
description:
On an industrial wasteland outside Tokyo, punk bands and their followers square up against the gangsters and authorities pushing a nuclear power development. Rivalries, engines and amplifiers feed the same gathering riot. The city is being sold off, and its unwanted inhabitants intend to make a deafening objection.
Sōgo Ishii throws Japanese underground music straight into dystopian street warfare, with members of The Stalin, The Roosters and The Rockers supplying the noise and attitude. Frantic cutting and a camera seemingly caught in the mosh pit make this feel less like watching a future collapse than being dragged through it. Essential big-screen punk destruction.

title: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth
description: Brad Pitt returns to his Academy Award-winning role as Cliff Booth, only this time it’s 1977 and it’s a very different Hollywood. Directed by David Fincher from a screenplay by Quentin Tarantino, the film also stars Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Carla Gugino, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II and Peter Weller. (Netflix)

title: Opening Night on 35mm
description: Vidiots is thrilled to welcome award-winning actor and director Alden Ehrenreich to introduce this Cassavetes classic!

title: DISNEY'S HEXED
description: An impulsive and unconventional teenage girl named Billie (Hailee Steinfeld) discovers secret magical abilities which, once unleashed, hurtle her out of suburbia and into a spectacle-filled journey through a vast witch realm called Hexe. Forced to team up with her cautious mother, Alice (Rashida Jones), they uncover family mysteries that could change the world of witches forever. ​

title: EVERY CONTACT LEAVES A TRACE

A German woman reckons with history, an artist reflects on government surveillance, a forensic scientist searches the cards for DNA, and when memory reaches its limits, cinema fills in the gaps. Blending documentary, speculation, performance, and personal reflection with remarkable grace, Sachs transforms an ordinary archive into a meditation on memory, history, and the invisible ways we shape one another’s lives.” –Bryan Wendorf, CHICAGO UNDERGROUND FILM FESTIVAL “Sachs reveals her strength: she captures beauty in the mundane, elevates the casual to poetry, and shows that even the most fleeting encounter leaves a lasting legacy.” –Martijn Smit, CINEMAGAZINE “Sachs extends the interpersonal scale of her inquiry into a more expansive awareness. With Sachs, we learn that to be in relation is to come to terms with one’s capacity to do harm and to accept that we might leave imprints that elude our awareness entirely.” –Delaney Holton, SCREEN SLATE “A deeply personal meditation on memory, history, and chance encounters that exemplifies Sachs’s uniquely lyrical approach to nonfiction filmmaking.” –SCREEN MAGAZINE Lynne Sachs will be here in person for all screenings! title: Die Hard [is a Christmas Movie]
description: New York City policeman John McClane (Bruce Willis) is visiting his estranged wife (Bonnie Bedelia) and two daughters on Christmas Eve. He joins her at a holiday party in the headquarters of the Japanese-owned business she works for. But the festivities are interrupted by a group of terrorists who take over the exclusive high-rise, and everyone in it. Very soon McClane realizes that there's no one to save the hostages -- but him.

title: BRIGHTON BEACH
description: At once a charming portrait of the diverse residents of a unique New York City neighborhood, a vibrant time capsule of the city at the very beginning of the 1980s, and a penetrating exploration of the social and political dynamics of a rapidly changing community, BRIGHTON BEACH is a long-lost gem of documentary cinema that has been newly restored by IndieCollect. Directed with great empathy and perceptiveness by Carol Stein & Susan Wittenberg, BRIGHTON BEACH captures the Brooklyn neighborhood known as the poor man’s paradise – a city by the sea down the street from the Coney Island boardwalk. Interspersing interviews with the neighborhood’s residents – including the Soviet Jews who had begun arriving in large numbers at the time – with archival footage of the area fifty years earlier, the film is both a portrait of a very particular time and place as well as a study of the ways in which urban communities function, cohere, and continuously transform themselves.

title: Love Actually
description: Nine intertwined stories examine the complexities of the one emotion that connects us all: love. Among the characters explored are David (Hugh Grant), the handsome newly elected British prime minister who falls for a young junior staffer (Martine McCutcheon), Sarah (Laura Linney), a graphic designer whose devotion to her mentally ill brother complicates her love life, and Harry (Alan Rickman), a married man tempted by his attractive new secretary.

title: MINOTAUR
description: Intrigue, corruption, betrayal: the walls of the maze are closing in. C orporate executive Gleb finds himself under siege on all fronts. At home, he is haunted by suspicions that his wife is unfaithful. At work, he contends with the official demand to draft employees for the war in Ukraine. Desperat...

title: Behemoth!
description: A gifted cellist returns home to Los Angeles after 20 years on the road. Music, which has been the constant, all-consuming river of his life, begins to carry him on an adventure that will change him forever...

title: MYSTERY MOVIE
description:
Take a seat without knowing what is coming. Our mystery screenings explore the bold, disreputable and gloriously unclassifiable world of psychotronic cinema: discoveries that make you wonder how they were made, who they were made for, and why nobody showed you sooner.
The title stays secret until showtime. Curiosity is essential; good taste is negotiable.
Strictly for adult audiences. Films may contain offensive and upsetting content. Do not attend if you are of a sensitive disposition.

title: Belladonna of Sadness
description: Belladonna of Sadness (1973) is a visually striking and wildly experimental work of psychedelic animation that is a haunting tapestry of eroticism, oppression, and rebellion.

title: Christmas Evil
description: For those of you who get your Christmas kicks watching Santa Claus slaughter throngs of people, we’ve got you covered with one of the best holiday horror films of all time! Often referred to as the “Taxi Driver” of Christmas Horror movies, this killer Santa Claus movie is one of the first and still one of the best of the sub-genre! Garbed in his red suit, Harry, a toy factory worker, decides that the only thing he can do to save the spirit of Christmas is to become Santa Claus himself and make all of the naughty townspeople pay… in blood! Originally picketed by angry Christian groups, this banger still puts the SLAY in sleigh bells and no holiday season is complete without a rewatch!

title: 964 PINOCCHIO
description: Shozin Fukui’s 964 PINOCHIO depicts the nightmarish journey of a discarded cybernetic sex android that is expelled from a brothel and left to fend for himself. Aimlessly wandering around the city, Pinocchio meets Kyoto, an amnesiac homeless girl with a horrible secret of her own. Together, they try to piece together their past lives and survive in a cruel, brutal hellscape. At the same time, Pinocchio’s fiendish creators search desperately to find their lost prototype android before the public and authorities discover him! As agents pursue Pinocchio, his frantic escape morphs into a mind-warping hallucinogenic thrill ride!

title: Michael Mann's Manhunter: The Final Cut
Grindhouse
description: Quentin Tarantino and Robert Rodriguez's homage to exploitation double features in the 60s and 70s with two back-to-back cult films that include previews of coming attractions between them.

title: The Hateful Eight (Multiplex Version)
description: During a deadly snowstorm, a bounty hunter (Kurt Russell) rushes to bring his fugitive (Jennifer Jason Leigh) to justice. But losing their lead on the blizzard, they must seek refuge at Minnie’s Haberdashery where the mysterious strangers inside may not be who they seem. Written & directed by Quentin Tarantino and co-starring a stunning ensemble of QT favorites and pitch-perfect additions to his troupe: Samuel L. Jackson, Walton Goggins, Demián Bichir, Tim Roth, Michael Madsen and Bruce Dern round out The Hateful Eight .

title: TENDER LOVING CARE
description: As the demands of work and family begin to converge, a social worker and those closest to her discover the strength found in compassion, community and one another. Set in post-Brexit England, Mike Leigh’s TENDER LOVING CARE is a richly observed portrait of resilience, humor and the enduring power of human connection.

title: Parent & Baby Screening: You Can See Everything (15) (AD)
description: 34 days before she’s sent to prison, notorious Silicon Valley founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a skeptical film crew led by Nathan Fielder to document her every move.

title: Paddington
description: Bringing the beloved children’s novels to life, Paddington tells the story of the comic misadventures of a young Peruvian bear who travels to the city in search of a home. Finding himself lost and alone, he begins to realize that city life is not all he had imagined — until he meets the kindly Brown family who read the label around his neck (‘Please look after this bear. Thank you.’) and offer him a temporary haven. It looks as though his luck has changed until this rarest of bears catches the eye of a museum taxidermist.

title: Tokyo Godfathers
description: Middle-aged alcoholic Gin, teenage runaway Miyuki and former drag queen Hana are a trio of homeless people surviving as a makeshift family on the streets of Tokyo. While rummaging in the trash for food on Christmas Eve, they stumble upon an abandoned newborn baby in a trash bin. With only a handful of clues to the baby's identity, the three misfits search the streets of Tokyo for help in returning the baby to its parents.

title: Paddington 2
description: Paddington 2 has gained something of a cult following, winning over moviegoers of all ages with its charm, impeccable comedy, and genuinely big heart.

title: ONCE UPON A TIME IN HARLEM
description: ONCE UPON A TIME IN HARLEM is the only film this year to screen at the Sundance, Cannes, Telluride, Toronto and New York Film Festivals. The film also won 3 Critics Choice Documentary Awards including Best First Documentary Feature for director David Greaves, as well as the 2026 Library of Congress Lavine / Ken Burns Film Prize and the Maysles Film Center Albie Award in Harlem.

description: Join Vidiots and the Cinema Eye Honors for a full day of incredible documentary shorts – from the mind-blowing and groundbreaking to the heartbreaking and vital, don’t miss your chance to see all the best nonfiction short films of the year in one glorious day! title: WILDWOOD
description: After her baby brother is abducted by a murder of crows, headstrong teenager Prue McKeel (Peyton Elizabeth Lee) launches a desperate rescue mission into the Impassable Wilderness—an enchanted forest hidden just beyond Portland, Oregon. Joined by her hapless but loyal classmate Curtis Mehlberg (Jacob Tremblay), Prue navigates a world of talking animals, bandits and powerful figures driven by grief and ambition. As the pair is drawn into a conflict threatening the balance of the forest itself, Prue must discover the strength and belief she never knew she possessed. If she hopes to save her brother and protect Wildwood’s fragile future, she will have to risk everything. From Oscar-nominated and BAFTA-winning LAIKA, WILDWOOD is a sweeping adventure about love, sacrifice and the magic that reveals itself when we dare to look beyond the familiar.

title: CASSANDRA CAT
description:
A magician living in a small Czech town discovers that his cat possesses a strange power: whenever people look at it while wearing special glasses, their true personalities and hidden desires are revealed in bursts of vivid colour. The cat’s arrival throws the town into chaos, exposing hypocrisy, jealousy, and repression among its respectable citizens.
Blending fantasy, satire, and children’s fable, the film uses playful visual experimentation to critique conformity and social performance. Its shifting colours and whimsical tone mask a sharp commentary on authority, desire, and the fear of emotional honesty.

title: Portrait of Jason on 35mm
description: Interview with Jason Holliday aka Aaron Payne. House-boy, would-be cabaret performer, and self-proclaimed hustler giving one man’s gin-soaked, pill-popped view of what it was like to be black and gay in 1960s United States.

title: The Nightmare Before Christmas
description: The film follows the misadventures of Jack Skellington, Halloweentown's beloved pumpkin king, who has become bored with the same annual routine of frightening people in the "real world." When Jack accidentally stumbles on Christmastown, all bright colors and warm spirits, he gets a new lease on life -- he plots to bring Christmas under his control by kidnapping Santa Claus and taking over the role. But Jack soon discovers even the best-laid plans of mice and skeleton men can go seriously awry.

title: Gone to Earth with The Wild Heart
DAMAGE
description: Stephen Fleming, a conservative MP, is married to Ingrid, with whom he has two children: Martyn, a brilliant political reporter, and Sally, a bright, curious teenager. However, his political career crumbles when he becomes obsessed with his son’s lover, Anna, with whom he begins a passionate affair.

title: MAD LOVE
description:
A brilliant but unstable surgeon becomes obsessed with a beautiful young woman, and when she spurns his advances, he uses his medical skills to manipulate her life in increasingly dangerous and controlling ways. His obsession escalates into a dark and twisted struggle between desire, power, and madness.
Karl Freund directs a tense and atmospheric melodrama, blending expressionist visuals with psychological suspense. The film examines obsession and control with a mixture of style and intensity, making it a compelling early example of Hollywood’s fascination with the darker side of desire.

title: The Holiday
description: Dumped and depressed, English rose Iris agrees to swap homes with similarly unlucky in love Californian Amanda for a much-needed break. Iris finds herself in a palatial Hollywood mansion while Amanda navigates the lanes of a picture-perfect English village. Soon enough, both lovelorn ladies bump into local lads perfect for a romantic pick-me-up.

title: PARADOX ON 72ND STREET
description: Over the course of three years, Gene Searchinger filmed pedestrians, joggers, buskers, bench sitters, stoop sleepers, and countless other types of New Yorker (whom the narration describes as “exaggerated Americans”) at the corner of Broadway and 72nd St. Visually, the film presents an hour-long stream of individuals, each with their own unfathomable inner mindscape, who together comprise “the collective”; the paradox referred to in the title is narrator Lewis Thomas’s assertion that, “It is in our genes to live together and to depend on each other, to be our individual separate selves and at the same time the working parts of others.” Thomas, a biologist and the film’s co-writer, shares narrating duties with the anthropologist Philip Slater, both of whom offer meandering philosophical notes on individualism in American society.

title: IDA
description: From acclaimed director Paweł Pawlikowski comes Ida, a moving and intimate drama about a young novitiate nun in 1960s Poland who, on the verge of taking her vows, makes a shocking discovery about her past. 18-year old Anna (stunning newcomer Agata Trzebuchowska), a sheltered orphan raised in a convent, is preparing to become a nun when the Mother Superior insists she first visit her sole living relative. Naïve, innocent Anna soon finds herself in the presence of her aunt Wanda (Agata Kulesza), a worldly and cynical Communist Party insider, who shocks her with the declaration that her real name is Ida and her Jewish parents were murdered during the Nazi occupation. This revelation triggers a heart-wrenching journey into the countryside, to the family house and into the secrets of the repressed past, evoking the haunting legacy of the Holocaust and the realities of postwar Communism. In this beautifully directed film, Pawlikowski returns to his native Poland for the first time in his career to confront some of the more contentious issues in the history of his birthplace. Powerfully written and eloquently shot, a masterly evocation of a time, a dilemma and a defining historical moment; IDA is also personal, intimate and human. The weight of history is everywhere, but the scale falls within the scope of a young woman learning about the secrets of her own past. This intersection of the personal with momentous historic events makes for what is surely one of the most powerful and affecting films of the year.

title: THE SOCIAL LIFE OF SMALL URBAN SPACES
description: This film emerged from city planner William H. Whyte’s years of research into pedestrian behavior and city dynamics, conducted as part of his Street Life Project. His research resulted both in a film and a book, both of which closely analyzed the functioning of public spaces in various cities, above all in NYC. The book quickly became a classic text within the realm of city planning, and remains beloved not only for the wisdom and elegance of its insights, but for its disarmingly unpretentious, no-nonsense, and often flat-out funny tone. The film version fully embodies all the qualities of the book, and adds one special feature: Whyte’s own voice. Sounding very much like Jimmy Stewart’s city planner cousin, Whyte delivers the narration with an often-self-deprecatory folksiness that’s charmingly at odds with the stentorian tone of most educational films. The film is also effectively a work of street photography. Whyte and his team’s dedication to observing – and recording – the actual behavior of city dwellers, and their sharp eye for the behaviors and gestures that are most revealing of city life, result in a film that is – almost incidentally – a classic city symphony. THE SOCIAL LIFE OF SMALL URBAN SPACES is one of the great films about that strangest of creatures – the city dweller – in its natural habitat.

title: DR CALIGARI
description:
Mrs. Van Houten shows signs of losing touch with reality, and her husband consults Dr. Caligari for treatment. Caligari claims to have a cure, but as his methods unfold, the line between science and madness becomes disturbingly unclear. Strange acts in the town suggest that Cesare, Caligari’s somnambulist, may be carrying out the doctor’s darker intentions, leaving the town gripped by fear and confusion.
Stephen Sayadian (Nightdreams) directs a hallucinatory, over-the-top reimagining of the classic expressionist story. The film combines surreal visuals, black comedy, and grotesque absurdity, turning familiar horror and psychological thriller tropes into something deliberately outrageous, provocative, and unforgettable.

title: The Cinema Eye Shorts List – Program 3 – Buckskin, A Derailment, Water Cooler, They’re Here
description: Join Vidiots and the Cinema Eye Honors for a full day of incredible documentary shorts – from the mind-blowing and groundbreaking to the heartbreaking and vital, don’t miss your chance to see all the best nonfiction short films of the year in one glorious day! The Cinema Eye Shorts List, is a celebration of the top short documentaries of 2026. Each year, Cinema Eye announces ten semi-finalists for their Nonfiction Short Film Honor. From this list of 10, six films will be announced in December as the final nominees for Outstanding Achievement in Nonfiction Short Filmmaking and the winner will be announced at the 20th Annual Cinema Eye Honors in January.

title: PRECIPICE (FILMMAKER IN PERSON!)
description: A profoundly working-class community with an intense connection to its land and water is transformed into a pleasure paradise for the wealthy…all while the ground slips into the sea. The new film by moving-image artist, writer, and poet Abigail Child – a leading figure of the generation of experimental filmmakers that emerged in the late 1970s-early 1980s – PRECIPICE focuses on the intersection between climate change and a changing shore community’s response to this global emergency. It’s been decades since fishing, the engine of Nova Scotia’s last 200 years, collapsed. The result: numerous jobs dried up for independent offshore fishermen. A gold rush on the land fills the vacuum, a double-edged sword of economic activity and environmental deterioration. PRECIPICE documents these challenges and explores how community members work to mitigate the human impact: building back the eroding drumlins, creating oyster farms in local bays, practicing regenerative farming, woodlot conservation and organizing the community to buy land to preserve extant wetlands. “On Nova Scotia’s South Shore, where fishing once shaped the communities, new pressures are shifting the landscape. PRECIPICE points the lens at Rose Bay, and up river, tracing the fragile edge between memory and disappearance, as working-class lives are recast against rising seas and fancy coastal development. Echoes of old home movies, Mi’kmaq tales, and present-day restoration (including oyster farming, wetland preservation, woodlot management) interweave into a portrait of resilience.” –Walter Forsyth, LUNENBURG DOC FEST

title: Love Actually
description: Nine intertwined stories examine the complexities of the one emotion that connects us all: love. Among the characters explored are David (Hugh Grant), the handsome newly elected British prime minister who falls for a young junior staffer (Martine McCutcheon), Sarah (Laura Linney), a graphic designer whose devotion to her mentally ill brother complicates her love life, and Harry (Alan Rickman), a married man tempted by his attractive new secretary.

title: Blue Sky in 35mm with Jessica Lange
The Muppet Christmas Carol
description: 'Tis the season for love, laughter, and one of the most cherished stories of all time! Join Kermit the Frog, Miss Piggy, and all the hilarious Muppets in this merry, magical version of Charles Dickens' classic tale. Academy Award® winner Michael Caine (Best Supporting Actor) gives a performance that's anything but "bah, humbug!" as greedy, penny-pinching Ebenezer Scrooge. title: MINOTAUR
description: Intrigue, corruption, betrayal: the walls of the maze are closing in. C orporate executive Gleb finds himself under siege on all fronts. At home, he is haunted by suspicions that his wife is unfaithful. At work, he contends with the official demand to draft employees for the war in Ukraine. Desperat...

title: WHAT IS THE CITY BUT THE PEOPLE?
description: “In 1969 the Department of City Planning attempted to shore up support for its various [development] projects with a multipronged, multimedia public relations blitz. At its center was the publication of a six-volume book, ‘The Plan for New York City’ (1969), which articulated the commissioner’s vision for the metropolis to stem the flight of the middle classes to the suburbs and revitalize urban space. The plan was presented in synopsis form as a propagandistic documentary produced by the Department and co-directed by John Peer Nugent and Gordon Hyatt. Featuring some flashy cinematography from New York location shooter-extraordinaire Arthur J. Ornitz [THE CONNECTION; MINNIE & MOSKOWITZ; SERPICO], WHAT IS THE CITY is an idiosyncratic document of the city in the late 1960s, offering a wide panorama of places and spaces, narrated by one of the plan’s ghost writers, William H. Whyte [THE SOCIAL LIFE OF SMALL URBAN SPACES]. The film flits between footage of and discussion about ‘urban crisis’ (uprisings, poor housing stock, street violence) and purported city-led remedies. Viewed today, the film is both a curious relic of failed urban policy and an index of just how wedded city authorities were (and remain) to the idea that the manipulation of public perception is key to urban governance.” –FILM AT LINCOLN CENTER The screening on Sat, Dec 5 will be introduced by series curator Lauren Lee White and producer, journalist, and curator Nick Fraccaro!

title: Behemoth!
description: A gifted cellist returns home to Los Angeles after 20 years on the road. Music, which has been the constant, all-consuming river of his life, begins to carry him on an adventure that will change him forever...

title: LA BÊTE
description:
Erotic folklore rendered as aristocratic farce and pastoral hallucination. Walerian Borowczyk’s scandalous period fantasy begins in drawing rooms of inherited wealth and decaying lineage, then slips backward into a fevered 18th-century legend of lust, animality, and transgression. Civilization peels away; appetite remains.
This is costume drama dragged into the mud. Silk gowns and antique furniture give way to rutting in long grass, extended to the point of discomfort and absurdity. Borowczyk stages the encounter between woman and beast as both explicit spectacle and savage satire — a confrontation with repression that’s by turns painterly, grotesque, and deliberately excessive. Sirpa Lane moves from porcelain composure to ecstatic abandon, anchoring a film that refuses good taste as a governing principle.
Banned, cut, and argued over on release, La Bête stands as one of European art-cinema’s most brazen provocations: a heritage romance infected by animal desire, played straight and pushed too far.

title: Scanners
description: Hold onto your skulls for David Cronenberg’s explosive science-fiction horror classic. After a man with extraordinary—and frighteningly destructive—telepathic abilities is nabbed by agents from a mysterious rogue corporation, he discovers he is far from the only possessor of such strange powers, and that some of the other “scanners” have their minds set on world domination, while others are trying to stop them. A terrifying telepathic thriller with one of the most iconic practical effects in horror history, Scanners will work its way into your brain!

title: Cinematic Void Presents SPIRIT TASTING
description: Toasting their late friend at a distillery on New Year’s Eve, three former bandmates stumble into a top-shelf tasting where wishes are required for every bottle. But when their dreams become nightmares, they discover that every pour has its price.

title: Grindhouse
description: Quentin Tarantino and Robert Rodriguez's homage to exploitation double features in the 60s and 70s with two back-to-back cult films that include previews of coming attractions between them.

title: Eyes Wide Shut
description: In what would prove to be the coda to Stanley Kubrick’s masterful career, Eyes Wide Shut demanded an immersive level of commitment and trust from the director’s stars – Tom Cruise and Nicole Kidman – during the film’s grueling 15-month shoot in England. The two stars moved beyond their big screen charisma in order to inhabit their characters, peeling away at the psychological layers of trust and loyalty that protects the heart of a marriage. Set in Greenwich Village (recreated at Pinewood Studios in London) and beautifully captured by Larry Smith (Kubrick’s gaffer on Barry Lyndon and The Shining ), Cruise plays Dr. Bill Harford, who feels betrayed after his wife Alice (Nicole Kidman) confesses that she fantasized about having sex with another man, sending Bill into a dream-like excursion of sexual enticement and mystery, including masquerading into a secret society where sex is treated with a cult like indulgence – putting himself and his marriage in danger. A film that Martin Scorsese called “misunderstood,” Eyes Wide Shut creates a slow burn of discomfort that plays foil to the eroticism, sexual tension, and temptation that Kubrick explores.

title: Members' Screening: Minotaur (15) (AD)
description: After a nine-year absence having fled his native Russia and gone into exile, Andrey Zvyagintsev makes his long-awaited return; a modern reimagining of Claude Chabrol’s La femme infidèle .

title: Home Alone
description: When bratty 8-year-old Kevin McCallister (Macaulay Culkin) acts out the night before a family trip to Paris, his mother (Catherine O'Hara) makes him sleep in the attic. After the McCallisters mistakenly leave for the airport without Kevin, he awakens to an empty house and assumes his wish to have no family has come true. But his excitement sours when he realizes that two con men (Joe Pesci, Daniel Stern) plan to rob the McCallister residence, and that he alone must protect the family home.

title: Relaxed Screening: Godzilla Minus Zero (15)
description: Takashi Yamazaki follows up his Oscar-winning Godzilla Minus One with a sequel that delivers on character-driven storytelling with action-packed monster mayhem.

description: A tapestry spanning nearly a century of Spanish history, LA BOLA NEGRA tells the story of three generations of men whose lives are intimately connected through desire, pain and love.

description: Velcro Flats Presents Sunday 6th December 12.30pm-6pm DAYTIME SHOW £17.50 Waged £12.50 Unwaged Tickets Available On DICE APP  POZI Pozi are a South London trio - Toby Burroughs (drums/vocals), Rosa Brook (violin/vocals) and Frank Lindsay (bass/vocals) - making bittersweet, propulsive weird pop that ...

title: The Jungle Book
description: You know where you are? You’re in the jungle baby! If you could live with the animals, would you want to go back to civilization? Neither would we! Embrace your animal nature with this all-time Disney classic interpretation of Rudyard Kipling’s eternal tale. Abandoned in the jungle, Mowgli is raised by wolves despite being a human boy. With the help of a wise panther, a hypnotic snake, and a bear with endles joie-de-vivre, Mowgli will make his way back to his own species with the help of all his best animal friends. With some of the best songs in the Disney catalogue, top-notch voice talent, and far beyond the “bear necessities” of delight, it’s time to take the fam to the jungle! After all, who hasn’t secretly longed to have been raised by wolves?

title: Gremlins
description: You should know the rules by now: Don’t expose them to bright light. Don’t get them wet. And above all, don’t feed them after midnight. So join Gizmo and all the monstrous Gremlins as they burst off the screen in the greatest small-town holiday adventure since It’s A Wonderful Life ! This bonanza of proliferating pests is the beloved result of the remarkable union between director Joe Dante, writer Chris Columbus, and Steven Spielberg’s Amblin Entertainment. Mixing Norman Rockwell sentimentality and anarchic vandalism, this Christmas-comedy-horror classic both lights up and destroys everything you love (and loathe) about the holidays.

Directed by David Fincher from a screenplay by Quentin Tarantino, the film also stars Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Carla Gugino, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II and Peter Weller.

title: Esther Anderson Retrospective: THE THREE DUMAS
description: The story behind the Count Of Monte Cristo, The Three Dumas is a dramatised documentary championing the revolutionary life and career of novelist Alexandre Dumas. Dumas was a renowned writer, the grandson of an enslaved Haitian heritage who contributed greatly to his perspective as he developed work...

title: Elf
description: Buddy (Will Ferrell) was accidentally transported to the North Pole as a toddler and raised to adulthood among Santa's elves. Unable to shake the feeling that he doesn't fit in, the adult Buddy travels to New York, in full elf uniform, in search of his real father. As it happens, this is Walter Hobbs (James Caan), a cynical businessman. After a DNA test proves this, Walter reluctantly attempts to start a relationship with the childlike Buddy with increasingly chaotic results.

title: Paweł Pawlikowski: Documentaries
description: The film revists Vyenedikt Yerfoeyev’s underground novel ‘Moscow-Petushki’, retracing the narrator’s alcohol-fuelled epic journey from Moscow to the town of Pietushki, 99km away.

title: CINEXPÉRIMENTAUX: A MEETING WITH ABIGAIL CHILD
description: Part of Michel Amarger and Frédérique Devaux’s ongoing series of documentary portraits of those who further the cause of experimental cinema in the 21st century (other subjects have included the filmmakers Nicolas Rey, Rose Lowder, and Stephen Dwoskin, as well as scholars, distributors, and curators such as Vivian Ostrovsky, Pip Chodorov, the Light Cone cooperative, and others), A MEETING WITH ABIGAIL CHILD represents a deep dive into the life and work of Child. Encompassing several in-depth interviews, copious footage from her films past and present, and revealing glimpses of the artist at work, the documentary is an essential supplement to Child’s own filmography.

title: THE UMBRELLAS OF CHERBOURG
description:
They are young, in love and certain they will wait for each other. Then Guy is sent to Algeria, Geneviève discovers she is pregnant, and the future begins asking questions their romance cannot answer.
Every line is sung, every colour seems to carry a feeling, and Michel Legrand’s music makes ordinary heartbreak soar. Jacques Demy and Catherine Deneuve create a world of ravishing surfaces without protecting their characters from money, time or compromise. A musical of overwhelming beauty whose greatest surprise is how clear-eyed it is about love.

title: A Place in the Sun on 35mm
description: We’re excited to welcome back our Founding Member and forever bestie Author/ Film Historian/ Podcaster Karina Longworth for a special screening of George Stevens’ Oscar-winning true crime thriller A Place in the Sun !

title: Castration Movie ⅗ Year of the Hyaena
description: In Chapter iii. Chastity No Exit Virtue Cuck , Michaela (Weard) tries to be a good person.

title: Armenian FF: Inna Sahakyan Special – Aurora's Sunrise + Q&A
THIRD AVENUE: ONLY THE STRONG SURVIVE
description: “This Emmy Award-winning documentary tells the stories of six ‘ordinary’ people who live or work along New York City’s Third Avenue, which runs for sixteen miles through Manhattan, Brooklyn, and the Bronx, cutting through the complex social strata of the city to reveal wildly different economic and ethnic subcultures. The subjects speak for themselves, offering candid glimpses into the disparate worlds of a junkyard dealer who steals cars, a Bowery denizen and the wife he abandoned, a welfare mother living in a condemned building with her five children, a sex worker, a devout Puerto Rican factory worker, and an aging Italian barber and his wife. This unsentimental portrait of the uncommon lives of common people is a subjective sociological study of survival in urban America.” –DCTV

title: The Holdovers
description: From acclaimed director Alexander Payne, THE HOLDOVERS follows a curmudgeonly instructor (Paul Giamatti) at a prestigious American school who is forced to remain on campus during Christmas break to babysit the handful of students with nowhere to go. Eventually he forms an unlikely bond with one of them -- a damaged, brainy troublemaker (newcomer Dominic Sessa) -- and with the school’s head cook, who has just lost a son in Vietnam (Da’Vine Joy Randolph).

title: JUST LOOK UP
description: JUST LOOK UP follows Michael Greenberg, a brazen visionary and founder of Climate Defiance, a disruptive youth movement. In the tradition of Gandhi’s Satyagraha, the Civil Rights Movement, and ACT UP, they use radical nonviolent direct action to jolt society awake, calling out Big Oil, corporate CEO...

title: Cinema Tehran: BASHU THE LITTLE STRANGER
description: Cinema Tehran presents Bashu , acclaimed as the best Iranian film of all time. Fleeing the Iran-Iraq war, a ten year old Afro-Iranian boy finds refuge with a headstrong mother whose language he can’t understand. Bahram Beyzai’s landmark film is a poetic, quietly revolutionary story of displacement, ...

title: DRACULA IN ISTANBUL
description:
A young lawyer travels from Istanbul to Romania to complete a legal transaction with the mysterious Count Dracula, despite warnings about his host's sinister reputation. After returning home, he discovers that Dracula has followed him to Istanbul, where the Count begins preying on those closest to him, prompting a desperate effort to stop the vampire before more lives are lost.
While closely following the broad outline of Bram Stoker's novel, the film relocates the action to contemporary Turkey and adapts the story through Ali Rıza Seyfi's unauthorized 1928 novel Kazıklı Voyvoda. It is notable for introducing several elements that later became closely associated with Dracula on screen, including prominent fangs and the Count scaling the walls of his castle.

description: Vidiots remembers the extraordinary life, talent, style, and humanism of one of the greatest American icons of all time – the eternal Goddess Dolly Parton with a tearjerking screening of Steel Magnolias .

description: In Polish, French, Croatian, German, Russian, Serbian and Italian with English subtitles.

title: MICHAEL
description: MICHAEL explores the making of the artist behind the icon, following Michael Jackson from child prodigy under his father’s relentless direction to the heights of stardom, as he becomes a global cultural force that changes music forever.

title: WHAT IS THE CITY: DEAN + NEWSREEL + DANSKA
description: Josephine Hayes Dean THE REBUILDING OF MASCOT FLATS 1992, 59 min, 16mm “This is a moving story about a group of homeless New Yorkers who set out to renovate an abandoned tenement building. Helped by Habitat for Humanity, including Jimmy Carter, the participants become proficient carpenters and tenant-owners. This group of ethnically diverse people overcomes bureaucracy, skepticism, and lack of money to attain finally a decent affordable place to live.” –ALEXANDER STREET Newsreel THE CASE AGAINST LINCOLN CENTER (Newsreel #17) 1968, 12 min, 16mm-to-DCP More than 20,000 Latino families were displaced to make way for Lincoln Center, home to the Metropolitan Opera and the New York Symphony. This film examines the patrons of the art complex (corporations and wealthy families) and the culture displayed there. Juxtaposing the atmosphere of Lincoln Center with the vibrant street culture of a displaced neighborhood, the film correctly predicts the process by which the West Side was to be turned into a high-rent area for the upper middle class. Herbert Danska UPTOWN: PORTRAIT OF THE SOUTH BRONX 1965, 29 min, 16mm. Print courtesy of the Reserve Film and Video Collection of the New York Public Library for the Performing Arts; preserved with funding from the New York State Library, Division of Library Development. A study of a disadvantaged community within the city, situated in a triangle at the southern tip of the Bronx, UPTOWN includes scenes of tenements, streets, parks, churches, markets, dance halls, and playgrounds, revealing the way of life of its people, their desperation and their hope. Total running time: ca. 105 min.

title: MINOTAUR
description: Intrigue, corruption, betrayal: the walls of the maze are closing in. C orporate executive Gleb finds himself under siege on all fronts. At home, he is haunted by suspicions that his wife is unfaithful. At work, he contends with the official demand to draft employees for the war in Ukraine. Desperat...

title: Take Me Home
description: Anna (Anna Sargent making her acting debut), a middle-aged Korean adoptee with a cognitive disability, cares for her aging parents in a fragile balance of meeting one another’s needs. Alongside her sister Emily (Ali Ahn) and her father (Victor Slezak), they must confront challenging questions about the future, but she remains determined to build a life where all of them can thrive.

title: EVERY CONTACT LEAVES A TRACE
description: “For most of her life, filmmaker Lynne Sachs has saved every business card ever placed into her hand – more than 600 fragments of chance encounters, fleeting conversations, and unexpected connections. Drawing on the forensic principle that every contact leaves a trace, Sachs selects seven cards and follows them back into the lives they represent. A German woman reckons with history, an artist reflects on government surveillance, a forensic scientist searches the cards for DNA, and when memory reaches its limits, cinema fills in the gaps. Blending documentary, speculation, performance, and personal reflection with remarkable grace, Sachs transforms an ordinary archive into a meditation on memory, history, and the invisible ways we shape one another’s lives.” –Bryan Wendorf, CHICAGO UNDERGROUND FILM FESTIVAL “Sachs reveals her strength: she captures beauty in the mundane, elevates the casual to poetry, and shows that even the most fleeting encounter leaves a lasting legacy.” –Martijn Smit, CINEMAGAZINE “Sachs extends the interpersonal scale of her inquiry into a more expansive awareness. Her on-screen interlocutors serve as mirrors into her own wandering mind, a gesture toward entanglement reminiscent of Chris Marker’s reflexive SANS SOLEIL. With Sachs, we learn that to be in relation is to come to terms with one’s capacity to do harm and to accept that we might leave imprints that elude our awareness entirely.” –Delaney Holton, SCREEN SLATE “A deeply personal meditation on memory, history, and chance encounters that exemplifies Sachs’s uniquely lyrical approach to nonfiction filmmaking.” –SCREEN MAGAZINE Lynne Sachs will be here in person for all screenings! She will be joined in conversation by the following guests: Fri, Dec 4 7:00 - David Schwartz Sat, Dec 5 5:30 - Stephen Vitiello with film participants Viva and Felix Torres Sun, Dec 6 8:00 - Jessica Bardsley Mon, Dec 7 6:30 - Brydie O’Conner 8:45 - Su Friedrich Wed, Dec 9 6:30 - Rabbi Ellen Lippmann 8:45 - Lee Ann Brown

title: FEAR HAS 1000 EYES
description:
A priest and his pregnant wife live quietly in a remote Swedish vicarage until her friend Hedvig comes to stay. The visitor brings an interest in the occult and a talent for getting inside other people’s lives. Soon desire, unexplained deaths and the suspicion of something satanic have made the household distinctly less holy.
Torgny Wickman contaminates the Scandinavian sex film with witchcraft and religious dread. Solveig Andersson’s unsettling presence turns pastoral respectability into a trap, while the collision of solemn belief and exploitation excess gives the film its peculiar fever. A rarely encountered corner of Swedish horror where temptation has already let itself in.
Introduced by Harry Thorfinn George.

title: Brazil
description: Low-level bureaucrat Sam Lowry escapes the monotony of his day-to-day life through a recurring daydream of himself as a virtuous hero saving a beautiful damsel. Investigating a case that led to the wrongful arrest and eventual death of an innocent man instead of wanted terrorist Harry Tuttle, he meets the woman from his daydream, and in trying to help her gets caught in a web of mistaken identities, mindless bureaucracy and lies.

title: The Apartment
description: Insurance worker C.C. Baxter (Jack Lemmon) lends his Upper West Side apartment to company bosses to use for extramarital affairs. When his manager Mr. Sheldrake (Fred MacMurray) begins using Baxter's apartment in exchange for promoting him, Baxter is disappointed to learn that Sheldrake's mistress is Fran Kubelik (Shirley MacLaine), the elevator girl at work whom Baxter is interested in himself. Soon Baxter must decide between the girl he loves and the advancement of his career.

title: MY SUMMER OF LOVE
description: Kindred spirits from different worlds become entangled together one volatile summer in this passionate, psychological thriller. Local girl Mona (Natalie Press) is naive, reckless and filled with yearning for something more in life. Tamsin (Emily Blunt) is spoiled and bored and trying to escape the confines of her prep-school existence when she draws Mona into her fantasy world. But what started as a magical friendship soon becomes laced with deception and danger.

title: Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut
description: Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, The Devils lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. The restoration many believed would never happen reaffirms Russell’s incendiary masterpiece as among the most overwhelming and uncompromising achievements in British cinema. Assembled from original camera negative, this 4k restoration is Ken Russell’s 2004 preferred edit. Picture and sound restoration by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: Krampus
description: Frustrated by the constant quarrel between the members of his dysfunctional family, Max loses interest to celebrate Christmas, awakening Krampus, a demon who will punish his entire family.

title: Classic Matinee: LOVE, ACTUALLY
description: Christmas is approaching, and love is making life complicated across London. A new Prime Minister falls for a member of his staff, a writer finds himself lost for words abroad, and a marriage is shaken by an unwelcome discovery. Richard Curtis brings together Hugh Grant, Emma Thompson, Alan Rickman ...

title: Tokyo Godfathers
description: Middle-aged alcoholic Gin, teenage runaway Miyuki and former drag queen Hana are a trio of homeless people surviving as a makeshift family on the streets of Tokyo. While rummaging in the trash for food on Christmas Eve, they stumble upon an abandoned newborn baby in a trash bin. With only a handful of clues to the baby's identity, the three misfits search the streets of Tokyo for help in returning the baby to its parents.
