title: It's A Wonderful Life
description: Beset with personal and professional problems, George Bailey finds his previously happy life falling apart around him on Christmas Eve. Seeing no way out, George considers suicide from the edge of a bridge ­ but Clarence, his guardian angel, intervenes and shows George what his beloved hometown of Bedford Falls would be like without him.

title: MYSTERY DOJO: SURPRISE KUNG FU MATINEES
description:
Enter the 36 Chambers of Grindhouse Cinema, with these Sunday mystery martial-arts matinees that harken back to the glory days of 42nd Street.
Expect deep-cut chopsocky plucked from the 70s and 80s screening on both digital and VHS - with bone-crushing bashers from the genre that mixed Chinese folklore and fantasy, spaghetti westerns, melodrama, Japanese samurai films and American genre cinema into an electrifying combo that inspired both the future of action films - and hip hop.
These Kung Fu flicks became an international sensation in the 1970s, particularly at the Grindhouse cinemas that proliferated in impoverished inner-cities. Here were movies in which working-class heroes stood up to oppression, speaking loud and clear to the marginalised underclasses around the world.
Bring the ruckus!

title: Dolores
description: Join us at Vidiots for a screening of the documentary Dolores in celebration of the life and legacy of Chicana labor activist Dolores Huerta. Co-Presented with our friends at El Cine.

title: First Reformed
description: A pastor of a small church in upstate New York starts to spiral out of control after a soul-shaking encounter with an unstable environmental activist and his pregnant wife.

title: SYMBIOPSYCHOTAXIPLASM: TAKE 2 1/2
description: Following the early-1990s rediscovery of the then-undistributed and unseen SYMBIOPSYCHOTAXIPLASM: TAKE ONE, a sequel to the project was undertaken by William Greaves with support from actor Steve Buscemi and filmmaker Steven Soderbergh, both proponents of the director’s maverick vision. SYMBIOPSYCHOTAXIPLASM: TAKE 2½ incorporates outtakes from the filming of TAKE ONE as well as footage of a Q&A with Greaves and Buscemi following the first film’s screening at the 1999 Hamptons International Film Festival. A third section features TAKE ONE actors Audrey Henningham and Shannon Baker reuniting in 2003 for another multicamera Central Park shoot in which their characters confront each other after more than three decades of estrangement—as do the actors, in a convulsive, psychodramatic break from their on-screen roles. Expanding the parameters of TAKE ONE via new filmmaking technology and an emphasis on the melancholic toll of time, SYMBIOPSYCHOTAXIPLASM: TAKE 2½ enters into a fun-house-mirror dialogue with its ahead-of-the-times predecessor in ways both stylistically ingenious and unexpectedly emotional.

title: Imamura: Warm Water Under a Red Bridge
Esther Anderson Retrospective: A WARM DECEMBER + Q&A
description: A Warm December follows Dr. Matt Younger (Sidney Poitier) on a dirt bike racing trip to London with his daughter Stefanie Younger (Yvette Curtis). During their stay in the city Dr. Younger meets Catherine Oswandu (Esther Anderson), a beautiful young lady who has a cascade of strange men spying on he...

title: DOWN BY LAW
description:
A disc jockey, a small-time pimp and an Italian tourist find themselves sharing a Louisiana prison cell. Two are determined to remain miserable; the third has enough enthusiasm to irritate them both. An escape offers the prospect of freedom and a whole new set of problems.
Tom Waits, John Lurie and Roberto Benigni make an extraordinary comic trio in Jim Jarmusch’s deadpan fugitive tale. Robby Müller’s luminous monochrome photography turns cheap rooms and swamp water into a world suspended somewhere between noir and a ramshackle fairy tale. Losers, awkward silences and immaculate cool, with an unexpected warmth beneath the grime.

title: EYEWORKS SHORT FILM PGM 1
description: Winston Hacking ACTION BOG (Canada, 2025, 2 min, digital) “Time stretches like soft polymer; metamorphoses creep forward frame by frame, suspiciously slow, as if the film were watching me back.” –Winston Hacking Emma Calder SPRINGFIELD (UK, 1986, 7 min, 16mm-to-digital) “Part woman, part vacuum cleaner, what do these effeminate cyborgs have to say about alienation and the gendered hierarchies we inhabit? A witty and offbeat probing of loss, obsession, desperation, and fear.” –Emma Calder Adebukola Bodunrin LEAKS IN THE LINES (France/U.S., 2026, 4 min, digital) “LEAKS IN THE LINES is a hybrid film combining laser etching, phytograms, and 8mm footage of gardens to explore the tension between organic growth and imposed order.” –Adebukola Bodunrin Chihiro Yamanaka VEILS OF LANDSCAPE / / 霞始めてたなびく (Japan, 2025, 5 min, digital) “The east wind begins to blow, carrying warmth into the water. Landscapes merge without boundaries, and in time, the mountains drift into slumber.” –Chihiro Yamanaka JoAnn Gillerman ORCHID (U.S., 1985, 3 min, digital) “Technology meets sensuality as associations of gender are transposed into a yin/yang of unexpected androgyny. Computer graphics, live video and fluid hand drawn frame-by-frame fracturing animations create unique abstracted forms with unlikely pairings of living orchids, human form, nature and technology.” –JoAnn Gillerman Shana Moulton THE UNDISCOVERED DRAWER (U.S., 2013, 9 min, digital) A series of nested drawers opens for Cynthia, leading her on another journey of self-realization. Sara Petty PRELUDES IN MAGICAL TIME (U.S., 1987, 4 min, 16mm-to-digital) “The [film’s] imagery alludes to a window and curtains dancing in a breeze, which creates a structural element throughout the animation, as it drifts and unfolds into completely non-objective forms.” –VCU SCHOLARS COMPASS Emile Cohl ART’S INFANCY / L’ENFANCE DE L’ART (France, 1910, 4 min, 35mm-to-digital. Piano score by Andrew Dorsett.) “Created before cels were used in animation, this film blended techniques of hand-drawn linework, paper cut-outs, trick photography, human pixilation, and mixed-media live-action into a single experimental short film which explores imagined origins of creativity.” –EYEWORKS Çağıl Harmandar VISION (Japan/Turkey, 2023, 7 min, digital) “Eyes are magical spheres that make up dreams and retain memories. In our eyes, the visions of the within and of the beyond overlap. New worlds come to be when our gazes meet.” –Çağıl Harmandar Julian Antonisz WHAT DO WE SEE AFTER CLOSING OUR EYES AND COVERING OUR EARS (Poland, 1978, 5 min, 35mm-to-digital) One of a series of films Antonisz made using his “pantograf-animograf,” an ingenious mechanical device that scales drawings down to the size of a film frame and mechanically animates transformations between drawings. Ruth Peyser GO TO HELL (U.S., 1994, 8 min, 16mm-to-digital) “After a fight with her boyfriend, a woman falls through a hole in the stairs into a hellish fantasy world where she is confronted by a series of terrifying situations. When she emerges, her fear turns to anger, giving her the courage to fight back. Along the way, she discovers the power and exhilaration of finding her voice.” –Ruth Peyser Kevin Eskew ENSMOOTHENING (U.S., 2026, 12 min, digital) “Visualize an Earth of such tranquility and peace in nature that it must be the true marvel of all the ages. A land for forever, smoothened and sterilized. That’s the Dream! Yes! A smooth plastic-coated marble world!” –Kevin Eskew Total running time: ca. 75 min.

title: It's A Wonderful Life
description: Beset with personal and professional problems, George Bailey finds his previously happy life falling apart around him on Christmas Eve. Seeing no way out, George considers suicide from the edge of a bridge ­ but Clarence, his guardian angel, intervenes and shows George what his beloved hometown of Bedford Falls would be like without him.

title: Trainspotting
description: Hilarious but harrowing, the film charts the disintegration of the friendship between Renton, Spud, Sick Boy, Tommy and Begbie as they proceed seemingly towards a psychotic, drug-fuelled self-destruction.

title: THE MAGICIAN
description: Long though lost until its mysterious recovery in the late 20th century, Rex Ingram’s THE MAGICIAN remains one of Hollywood’s most extravagant explorations of the occult. It features Paul Wegener as the hypnotist Oliver Haddo (a character modeled on Aleister Crowley), who seeks out the blood of a virgin for his alchemical experiments in creating life. The film is based on W. Somerset Maugham’s 1908 novel of the same name, which Crowley vituperatively accused of plagiarism. Preceded by: Kenneth Anger INVOCATION OF MY DEMON BROTHER 1969, 12 min, 16mm THE MAGICIAN will be shown alongside Kenneth Anger’s dense and mesmerizing INVOCATION OF MY DEMON BROTHER, which features the Moog drones of Mick Jagger and the Satanic presence of Anton LaVey. Anger held Ingram and his films in great esteem. He claimed that his grandmother, a wardrobe mistress, had worked on a number of his productions; through her stories of the time, the young Anger “became fascinated by this other period when nobody talked on the screen and when there were these magical, mythical images.” Total running time: ca. 100 min.

title: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth
description: Brad Pitt returns to his Academy Award-winning role as Cliff Booth, only this time it’s 1977 and it’s a very different Hollywood. Directed by David Fincher from a screenplay by Quentin Tarantino, the film also stars Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Carla Gugino, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II and Peter Weller. (Netflix)

title: Desert Hearts
description: Vidiots is thrilled to welcome Director/Producer Donna Deitch for a special screening of her seminal sapphic romance Desert Hearts.

title: An Evening with Colman Domingo featuring Sing Sing
WAKE IN FRIGHT
description:
One night in the Yabba should be enough. But a lost bet strands a schoolteacher in an outback town where hospitality means another drink, another dare and another reason he cannot leave.
Ted Kotcheff turns sunshine and friendliness into instruments of terror. Gary Bond’s careful composure is stripped away by a community whose rituals of masculinity are both welcoming and merciless, with Donald Pleasence an unforgettable guide into the abyss. A sun-blasted nightmare of drinking, belonging and the violence that can hide inside the invitation to be one of the boys.

title: EYEWORKS SHORT FILM PGM 2
description: Sandor Reisenbuchler FAREWELL, LITTLE ISLAND / ISTEN VELED, KIS SZIGET (Hungary, 1987, 12 min, 35mm-to-digital) “A short animation depicting the drowning of a village by modern technology.” –NATIONAL FILM INSTITUTE HUNGARY Fanny Sorgo & Eva Pedroza TAKO TSUBO (Austria/Germany, 2024, 6 min, digital) “Mr. Ham decides to have his heart removed in order to be relieved of his complicated feelings. The doctor assures him that this is no longer a problem at all in this day and age. However, Ham keeps his heart for a while after the removal in order to perhaps understand it better after all. TAKO TSUBO is an animated, surrealistic reflection on dealing with feelings in a meritocracy.” –SIXPACKFILM Jeff Carpenter & Mary Lambert RAPID EYE MOVEMENTS (U.S., 1977, 11 min, 16mm-to-digital) “An obscured world of night lives, eavesdropped phone calls, and philosophical romantic musings.” –Jeff Carpenter & Mary Lambert Alexandre Alagôa XYZ (Luxembourg, 2026, 12 min, digital. Contains strobing imagery.) “An obsessive exploration of the three geometric dimensions in hopes of reaching a fourth. Created by shooting with a camera on a tripod throughout the halls of a building where the filmmaker used to work.” –Alexandre Alagôa Lewis Klahr ALTAIR (U.S., 1995, 7 min, 16mm-to-digital) “ALTAIR offers a cutout animation version of color film noir. The images were culled from six, late forties issues of Cosmopolitan magazine and set to an almost 4-minute segment of Stravinsky’s ‘Firebird’ to create a sinister, perfumed world. The viewer is encouraged to speculate on the nature and details of the woman’s battle with large, malevolent societal forces and her descent into an alcoholic swoon.” –Lewis Klahr Caibei Cai SLIVER CAVE / 银幕 (China, 2021, 14 min, digital) “Stepping into a cave, the sight fluctuates by the firelight. Left to right, top to bottom. The same goes for the screen in front of you. It is a borderless tunnel, presenting domestication and desire. –Caibei Cai Ida Lasic MOLLY DANE (U.S., 2020, 6 min, digital) “Experience the ritz and glamour of a death at the Dane’s fundraiser.” –Ida Lasic Amy Kravitz RIVER LETHE (U.S., 1985, 7 min, 16mm-to-digital) A non-narrative and abstract visual poem in five parts. Its title refers to the underworld river of forgetfulness. The drawings are created from non-traditional animation media including rubbed and erased graphite, pigment, and aluminum powders to make an animate surface of unusual richness. Total running time: ca. 80 min.

title: Love Actually
description: Nine intertwined stories examine the complexities of the one emotion that connects us all: love. Among the characters explored are David (Hugh Grant), the handsome newly elected British prime minister who falls for a young junior staffer (Martine McCutcheon), Sarah (Laura Linney), a graphic designer whose devotion to her mentally ill brother complicates her love life, and Harry (Alan Rickman), a married man tempted by his attractive new secretary.

title: Lady Snowblood
description: Yuki’s family is nearly wiped out before she is born due to the machinations of a band of criminals. These criminals kidnap and brutalize her mother but leave her alive. Later her mother ends up in prison with only revenge to keep her alive. She creates an instrument for this revenge by purposefully getting pregnant. Yuki never knows the love of a family but only killing and revenge.

title: Die Hard [is a Christmas Movie]
description: New York City policeman John McClane (Bruce Willis) is visiting his estranged wife (Bonnie Bedelia) and two daughters on Christmas Eve. He joins her at a holiday party in the headquarters of the Japanese-owned business she works for. But the festivities are interrupted by a group of terrorists who take over the exclusive high-rise, and everyone in it. Very soon McClane realizes that there's no one to save the hostages -- but him.

Total running time: ca. 110 min.

title: THE NINTH CONFIGURATION
description: William Peter Blatty’s 1980 film THE NINTH CONFIGURATION — one of his only two directorial efforts — boasts a truly impressive cast of nothing but hardline characters like Scott Wilson, Moses Gunn, Robert Loggia, Alejandro Rey, Neville Brand, Ed Flanders, Tom Atkins(!), Richard Lynch (!!) and Joe Spinell(!!!) and even THE EXORCIST’s Jason Miller alongside Stacy Keach as a military psychiatrist with a taste for unusual therapy programs.

title: In The Mood For Love
description: In 1962 Hong Kong, neighbors Su Li-zhen (Mrs. Chan) and Chow Mo-wan (Mr. Chow) discover their spouses are having an affair. As they spend time together, they develop feelings for each other, but their relationship remains chaste and unspoken, reflecting societal constraints and their own moral compass.

title: It's A Wonderful Life
description: Beset with personal and professional problems, George Bailey finds his previously happy life falling apart around him on Christmas Eve. Seeing no way out, George considers suicide from the edge of a bridge ­ but Clarence, his guardian angel, intervenes and shows George what his beloved hometown of Bedford Falls would be like without him.

title: The Odyssey with John Leguizamo Live Intro
description: On Monday 14th December, trailblazing actor John Leguizamo joins us for a live introduction to THE ODYSSEY in 70mm! Odysseus, the legendary King of Ithaca, embarks on a long and perilous journey home following the Trojan War. Throughout his voyage, he is forced to confront the whims of gods, mythological monsters, and trials that stretch both his cunning and his humanity to the breaking point.

title: Classic Matinee: IT'S A WONDERFUL LIFE
description: Celebrating its 80th anniversary, Frank Capra’s much-loved classic gives one ordinary man an extraordinary Christmas. Facing financial ruin, George Bailey believes his family and neighbours would have been better off without him. An intervention from Clarence, an angel still waiting for his wings, o...

title: Love Actually
description: Nine intertwined stories examine the complexities of the one emotion that connects us all: love. Among the characters explored are David (Hugh Grant), the handsome newly elected British prime minister who falls for a young junior staffer (Martine McCutcheon), Sarah (Laura Linney), a graphic designer whose devotion to her mentally ill brother complicates her love life, and Harry (Alan Rickman), a married man tempted by his attractive new secretary.

title: The Muppet Christmas Carol
description: 'Tis the season for love, laughter, and one of the most cherished stories of all time! Join Kermit the Frog, Miss Piggy, and all the hilarious Muppets in this merry, magical version of Charles Dickens' classic tale. Academy Award® winner Michael Caine (Best Supporting Actor) gives a performance that's anything but "bah, humbug!" as greedy, penny-pinching Ebenezer Scrooge. One fateful Christmas Eve, Scrooge is visited by the Ghosts of Christmas Past, Present, and Future. Together with kind, humble Bob Cratchit (Kermit the Frog) and his family, the Spirits open Scrooge's eyes -- and his heart -- to the true meaning of Christmas. Filled with original music and dazzling special effects, THE MUPPET CHRISTMAS CAROL will become a holiday tradition your family will treasure all the days of the year. Featuring the film’s famous long-lost song ‘When Love is Gone’! ------ As always you can expect SING ALONG performances of this new version of THE MUPPET CHRISTMAS CAROL this Christmas - and now we don't need to pretend that we weren't going to just play the lost scene regardless! Performances will feature a Hosted Pre-Show with our very own Father Christmas, where you will be prepped on what to do throughout the film. Costumes aren't mandatory, but 'Tis the season, and we love seeing you dressed up in your favourite Christmas Jumpers! All this, and a few more surprises up our sleeves, makes this one of the must-see events this Christmas! If you're wanting to Sing Along with The Muppet Christmas Carol, simply book for the performances marked SING ALONG [it's next to the start time]. All other screenings will be regular performances, and nothing will be written next to the start time.

title: The Nightmare Before Christmas
description: The film follows the misadventures of Jack Skellington, Halloweentown's beloved pumpkin king, who has become bored with the same annual routine of frightening people in the "real world." When Jack accidentally stumbles on Christmastown, all bright colors and warm spirits, he gets a new lease on life -- he plots to bring Christmas under his control by kidnapping Santa Claus and taking over the role. But Jack soon discovers even the best-laid plans of mice and skeleton men can go seriously awry.

title: THE SWORD IN THE STONE
description: Disney’s underrated adaptation of the first title in T.H. White’s classic series The Once and Future King relates the coming-of-age of a young King Arthur, here named Wart, and his training by the wizard Merlin. Using the Xerox-transfer technology the studio implemented to great acclaim in its preceding 101 DALMATIANS, THE SWORD IN THE STONE centers on the magical arts of transformation, culminating in an epic battle of Merlin against the evil witch Madam Mim. Preceded by: Georges Méliès LE MAGICIEN (1898, 1 min, 35mm-to-DCP) Like THE SWORD IN THE STONE, George Méliès’s LE MAGICIEN emphasizes mystical metamorphoses. Total running time: ca. 85 min.
director: Wolfgang Reitherman, Clyde Geronimi, and David Hand

title: Relaxed Screening: NAZA (15)
description: Cloaked in darkness on the rooftops of Tel Aviv, Israeli journalist Yuval Abraham conducts shattering one-on-one interviews with Israeli soldiers and intelligence personnel.

title: DONT LOOK BACK
description:
Dylan on stage is only half the story. In hotel rooms, backstage corridors and combative interviews during his 1965 British tour, he is inventing—and resisting—the public figure everyone wants him to become.
D. A. Pennebaker’s camera catches the wit, the cruelty, the boredom and the sudden electricity without a narrator telling us what to think. From the cue cards of “Subterranean Homesick Blues” to performances alive with concentration, this landmark music documentary puts you in the room at the moment a musician becomes an enigma.

title: BRIGHTON BEACH
description: At once a charming portrait of the diverse residents of a unique New York City neighborhood, a vibrant time capsule of the city at the very beginning of the 1980s, and a penetrating exploration of the social and political dynamics of a rapidly changing community, BRIGHTON BEACH is a long-lost gem of documentary cinema that has been newly restored by IndieCollect. Directed with great empathy and perceptiveness by Carol Stein & Susan Wittenberg, BRIGHTON BEACH captures the Brooklyn neighborhood known as the poor man’s paradise – a city by the sea down the street from the Coney Island boardwalk. Interspersing interviews with the neighborhood’s residents – including the Soviet Jews who had begun arriving in large numbers at the time – with archival footage of the area fifty years earlier, the film is both a portrait of a very particular time and place as well as a study of the ways in which urban communities function, cohere, and continuously transform themselves.

title: TheyDream
description: Director William D. Caballero and producer Erin Ploss-Campoamor in person at the December 14th screening!

title: Cinematic Void Presents LOS LEPROSOS Y EL SEXO
description: After a group of violent lepers escape from a sanitarium, robbing several farms, the town’s residents demand that the sheriff take action. Meanwhile, a local criminal joins forces with the lepers to commit even more robberies.

title: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth
description: Brad Pitt returns to his Academy Award-winning role as Cliff Booth, only this time it’s 1977 and it’s a very different Hollywood. Directed by David Fincher from a screenplay by Quentin Tarantino, the film also stars Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Carla Gugino, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II and Peter Weller. (Netflix)

title: McCabe & Mrs. Miller
description: Get lost in this exquisite snowy dream of a western from master filmmaker Robert Altman – an atmospheric treasure centered on the lives, hardships, and triumphs of sex workers in the Wild West. Warren Beatty plays a sly and charismatic gambler who meets brilliant working girl Julie Christie and the two set out to found a modern brothel with protections for the workers and a healthy profit. But success can’t erase the dark realities of life that cling to all the desperate characters of this frontier town. With subtle wit, authentic emotion, stunning cinematography from Vilmos Zsigmund, and an iconic soundtrack from the legendary Leonard Cohen, McCabe & Mrs. Miller is a masterpiece on every level.

title: The Shape of Water
description: An other-worldly story, set against the backdrop of Cold War era America circa 1962, where a mute janitor working at a lab falls in love with an amphibious man being held captive there and devises a plan to help him escape.

title: It's A Wonderful Life
description: Beset with personal and professional problems, George Bailey finds his previously happy life falling apart around him on Christmas Eve. Seeing no way out, George considers suicide from the edge of a bridge ­ but Clarence, his guardian angel, intervenes and shows George what his beloved hometown of Bedford Falls would be like without him.

title: #7 TRAIN + CHINATOWN + TOURIST BUSES GO HOME!
description: Hye Jung Park & J.T. Takagi THE # 7 TRAIN: AN IMMIGRANT JOURNEY 1999, 28 min, DCP Every day 500,000 people from 117 different countries ride a subway that runs from Flushing to Times Square, going through Queens, the most culturally diverse region in the United States. This documentary follows four immigrant passengers: a Korean who works in Harlem, two Otavalen street vendors who work near Chinatown, and a gay Pakistani sari salesman on Fifth Avenue. Their lives and their conflicted relationships with the city and its other residents are juxtaposed with the subway they take each day to Manhattan and their dreams for the future. Jon Alpert & Keiko Tsuno CHINATOWN: IMMIGRANTS IN AMERICA 1980, 27 min, DCP “Produced in response to what DCTV felt were inaccurate media portrayals of New York City’s Chinatown, this award-winning, often startling portrait of an immigrant community probes beneath the tourist’s-eye view to uncover the complexity of an inner-city subculture plagued by poverty and exploitation. ‘This is the story of our neighbors,’ says Alpert. His sympathetic ‘reportage from within’ reveals kitchen workers earning less than $100 for sixty-hour weeks, rents that are among the highest in the city, and garment workers laboring for minimum wages in unsafe conditions. Focusing on individual stories to expose broader issues, this is an unflinching document of Asian immigrants under pressure to assimilate into mainstream culture and struggling to survive in America.” –ELECTRONIC ARTS INTERMIX Tom Tam TOURIST BUSES GO HOME! 1969, 10 min, DCP In this short film – one of the earliest examples of Asian American experimental film – Tom Tam follows the activism and protests against tours of Manhattan’s Chinatown. Total running time: ca. 70 min.

title: THE MAGICIAN
description: Long though lost until its mysterious recovery in the late 20th century, Rex Ingram’s THE MAGICIAN remains one of Hollywood’s most extravagant explorations of the occult. It features Paul Wegener as the hypnotist Oliver Haddo (a character modeled on Aleister Crowley), who seeks out the blood of a virgin for his alchemical experiments in creating life. The film is based on W. Somerset Maugham’s 1908 novel of the same name, which Crowley vituperatively accused of plagiarism. Preceded by: Kenneth Anger INVOCATION OF MY DEMON BROTHER 1969, 12 min, 16mm THE MAGICIAN will be shown alongside Kenneth Anger’s dense and mesmerizing INVOCATION OF MY DEMON BROTHER, which features the Moog drones of Mick Jagger and the Satanic presence of Anton LaVey. Anger held Ingram and his films in great esteem. He claimed that his grandmother, a wardrobe mistress, had worked on a number of his productions; through her stories of the time, the young Anger “became fascinated by this other period when nobody talked on the screen and when there were these magical, mythical images.” Total running time: ca. 100 min.

title: Die Hard [is a Christmas Movie]
description: New York City policeman John McClane (Bruce Willis) is visiting his estranged wife (Bonnie Bedelia) and two daughters on Christmas Eve. He joins her at a holiday party in the headquarters of the Japanese-owned business she works for. But the festivities are interrupted by a group of terrorists who take over the exclusive high-rise, and everyone in it. Very soon McClane realizes that there's no one to save the hostages -- but him.

title: WANDA
description:
Wanda gives up custody of her children and drifts through Pennsylvania’s coal country with no plan that will survive the day. A petty criminal offers her a place beside him, but belonging comes with another set of orders.
Barbara Loden wrote, directed and stars in this extraordinary independent film, finding immense emotional force in pauses, uncertain gestures and shabby rooms. The camera grants attention to a woman other stories would hurry past. Unsentimental and profoundly humane, WANDA asks what freedom can mean when almost every available choice belongs to somebody else.

title: BODY BAGS
description: A horror anthology containing three stories: a female college student is terrorized at work by a serial killer; a hair transplant goes horribly wrong; and a baseball player loses an eye and gets a new one from a recently executed murderer.
director: John Carpenter, Larry Sulkis, Tobe Hooper

title: Eyes Wide Shut
description: Stanley Kubrick's daring last film is many things. It is a compelling psychosexual journey. A haunting dreamscape. A riveting tale of suspense. A major milestone in the careers of stars Tom Cruise and Nicole Kidman. And "a worthy final chapter to a great director's career" (Roger Ebert). Cruise plays Dr William Hartford, who plunges into an erotic foray that threatens his marriage - and may even ensnare him in a lurid murder mystery - after his wife's (Kidman) admission of sexual longings. As the story sweeps from doubt and fear to self-discovery and reconciliation, Kubrick orchestrates it with masterful flourishes. Graceful tracking shots, controlled pacing, rich colours, startling images: bravura traits that make Kubrick a filmmaker for the ages are here to keep everyone's eyes wide shut.

title: Elf
description: Buddy (Will Ferrell) was accidentally transported to the North Pole as a toddler and raised to adulthood among Santa's elves. Unable to shake the feeling that he doesn't fit in, the adult Buddy travels to New York, in full elf uniform, in search of his real father. As it happens, this is Walter Hobbs (James Caan), a cynical businessman. After a DNA test proves this, Walter reluctantly attempts to start a relationship with the childlike Buddy with increasingly chaotic results.

title: It's A Wonderful Life
description: Beset with personal and professional problems, George Bailey finds his previously happy life falling apart around him on Christmas Eve. Seeing no way out, George considers suicide from the edge of a bridge ­ but Clarence, his guardian angel, intervenes and shows George what his beloved hometown of Bedford Falls would be like without him.

title: Phantom Thread
description: Renowned dressmaker Reynolds Woodcock and his sister Cyril are at the center of British fashion in 1950s London -- dressing royalty, movie stars, heiresses, socialites and debutantes. Women come and go in Woodcock's life, providing the confirmed bachelor with inspiration and companionship. His carefully tailored existence soon gets disrupted by Alma, a young and strong-willed woman who becomes his muse and lover.

title: It's A Wonderful Life
description: Beset with personal and professional problems, George Bailey finds his previously happy life falling apart around him on Christmas Eve. Seeing no way out, George considers suicide from the edge of a bridge ­ but Clarence, his guardian angel, intervenes and shows George what his beloved hometown of Bedford Falls would be like without him.

title: Tokyo Godfathers
description: Middle-aged alcoholic Gin, teenage runaway Miyuki and former drag queen Hana are a trio of homeless people surviving as a makeshift family on the streets of Tokyo. While rummaging in the trash for food on Christmas Eve, they stumble upon an abandoned newborn baby in a trash bin. With only a handful of clues to the baby's identity, the three misfits search the streets of Tokyo for help in returning the baby to its parents.

title: THE TEMPEST

title: Ander & Yul (15)
description: Ana Díez’s rarely screened debut explores a turbulent period in Spanish and Basque history through two old friends, one returning to a home he no longer recognises, the other who never left.

title: DIAL CODE: SANTA CLAUSE
description:
Thomas de Frémont, a precocious child obsessed with action films, sets himself up for a terrifying Christmas Eve after he unwittingly makes contact with a deranged psychopath who claims he’s Santa Claus.
Inventive, visually exuberant, and threaded with a dark fairy-tale logic, Dial Code: Santa Claus stands as one of the most striking European holiday thrillers of its era—a precursor to Home Alone with sharper teeth.

title: EC: PETER KUBELKA (THE COMPLETE WORKS): NEW 35MM PRINTS!
description: For this round of the Essential Cinema cycle, we will be showcasing brand new 35mm prints that Anthology has recently acquired of Peter Kubelka’s films. To celebrate these new prints, we will be supplementing the regular EC program with new prints of Kubelka’s POETRY AND TRUTH and ANTIPHON, as well as a vintage print of PAUSE!, which together effectively comprise a complete retrospective of his work! Special thanks to Peter Kubelka and the Austrian Film Museum. MOSAIC IN CONFIDENCE / MOSAIK IM VERTRAUEN (1955, 16 min, 35mm. Made in collaboration with Ferry Radax. Brand new print! ) ADEBAR (1957, 1 min, 35mm. Brand new print! ) SCHWECHATER (1958, 1 min, 16mm. Brand new print! ) ARNULF RAINER (1960, 7 min, 35mm. Brand new print! ) OUR TRIP TO AFRICA / UNSERE AFRIKAREISE (1966, 12 min, 16mm) PAUSE! (1977, 12 min, 16mm) POETRY AND TRUTH / DICHTUNG UND WAHRHEIT (1996-2003, 13 min, 35mm. Brand new print! ) ANTIPHON (2012, 6.5 min, 35mm. Brand new print! ) “Peter Kubelka is the perfectionist of the film medium; and, as I honor that quality above all others at this time finding such a lack of it now elsewhere, I would simply like to say: Peter Kubelka is the world’s greatest filmmaker – which is to say, simply: see his films!…by all means/above all else…etcetera.” –Stan Brakhage Total running time: ca. 75 min.

title: Sundance Short Film Tour
description: The 2026 Sundance Film Festival Short Film Tour, presented by Ketel One Vodka, is a curated collection of six standout short films from this year’s Festival, including three Festival Award–winning titles. This 99-minute program offers a mix of stories that highlight bold perspectives and next-gen storytellers.

title: Dune: Part Three
description: Dune: Part Three is set nearly two decades after Paul Atreides seized control of the Imperium. Now a ruthless Emperor, Paul must face the consequences of his reign as old allies return, terrifying new threats emerge, and betrayal lurks in every shadow. Haunted by visions of Imperial collapse and the reappearance of his long-lost love, Paul is drawn into a sweeping conspiracy, with Chani at the heart of its unfolding mystery. As rebellion brews and enemies close in, Paul must confront the true cost of power and the fate of those he loves the most.

title: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth
description: Brad Pitt returns to his Academy Award-winning role as Cliff Booth, only this time it’s 1977 and it’s a very different Hollywood. Directed by David Fincher from a screenplay by Quentin Tarantino, the film also stars Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Carla Gugino, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II and Peter Weller. (Netflix)

title: Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut
description: Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, The Devils lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. The restoration many believed would never happen reaffirms Russell’s incendiary masterpiece as among the most overwhelming and uncompromising achievements in British cinema. Assembled from original camera negative, this 4k restoration is Ken Russell’s 2004 preferred edit. Picture and sound restoration by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color and Warner Bros. Sound.

title: EC: KUCHAR / LYE
description: George & Mike Kuchar PUSSY ON A HOT TIN ROOF 1961, 14 min, 8mm-to-16mm. Preserved by Anthology Film Archives with support from the National Film Preservation Foundation. “It glows with the embers of desire! It smokes with the revelation of men and women longing for robust temptations that will make them sizzle into maturity with a furnace-blast of unrestrained animalism. A film for young and old to enjoy.” –George Kuchar TOOTSIES IN AUTUMN 1963, 15 min, 8mm-to-16mm. Preserved by Anthology Film Archives with support from the National Film Preservation Foundation. A cautionary tale about past-their-prime thespians caught up in a typically Kucharian vortex of madness. Len Lye TUSALAVA (1929, 10 min, 16mm, silent) TRADE TATTOO (1937, 5 min, 35mm) RHYTHM (1957, 1 min, 16mm) FREE RADICALS (1958/79, 4 min, 16mm) A giant of experimental animation, Len Lye was born in New Zealand in 1901. He moved to England in the 1920s and subsequently to New York in 1944, where he spent the last 40 years of his life. A pioneer of “scratch” or “direct” filmmaking, Lye used various tools to mark patterns, shapes, and images directly onto the film’s surface, and often explored the dynamic energy of abstract images propelled into life by lively jazz scores or Pacific-inspired rhythms. Total running time: ca. 55 min.

title: DEAD MOUNTAINEER'S HOTEL
description:
A police officer is called to a remote hotel in the mountains, where everything seems normal at first. Soon, an avalanche traps the guests and staff inside, and strange, inexplicable events begin to occur. Tensions rise as suspicions deepen and the mystery surrounding the hotel’s unusual visitors slowly unfolds.
Grigori Kromanov directs a surreal and suspenseful adaptation of the Strugatsky brothers’ story. The film mixes science fiction, mystery, and dark humor, creating an eerie, unpredictable atmosphere where the normal rules of reality seem to bend and no one is quite what they appear to be.

title: WIZARDS
description: Ralph Bakshi’s anti-fascist passion project, developed over decades and released prior to his LORD OF THE RINGS, mixes sci-fi and fantasy to tell the story of a far-future Earth where magic and fairies have returned in the wake of nuclear holocaust. These forces of good must battle an evil wizard who attempts to control the world by reviving the forbidden technologies of war. WIZARDS is pure, unrestrained Bakshi, filled with freaky characters, psychedelic backgrounds, and hallucinatory rotoscoping. Preceded by: Tommy Turner THE MAGICIAN 1998, 9 min, 16mm WIZARDS is paired with Tommy Turner’s THE MAGICIAN, a transgressive take on the rituals of ceremonial magic. Total running time: ca. 95 min.

title: American Psycho
description: A wealthy New York investment banking executive hides his alternate psychopathic ego from his co-workers and friends as he escalates deeper into his illogical, gratuitous fantasies.

title: La Haine
description: Hatred breeds hatred... 24 hours in the lives of three young men in the French suburbs the day after a violent riot.

title: A Very Harold & Kumar Christmas
description: Six years after their Guantanamo Bay adventure, stoner buds Harold Lee and Kumar Patel cause a holiday fracas by inadvertently burning down Harold's father-in-law's prize Christmas tree.

title: CURTAINS
description:
Six actresses arrive at a secluded house to compete for the same part. Their director has a taste for manipulation, his former star has reasons to resent him, and someone in a hideous old-woman mask is beginning to thin out the competition. The audition is about to become considerably more demanding.
Samantha Eggar and John Vernon lend venom to this unusually wintry Canadian slasher, where professional jealousy curdles into nightmare. Its notorious ice-skating sequence alone earns a place in horror history, but the film’s warped theatrical atmosphere keeps working long after the mask appears. Elegant cruelty with a very nasty edge.

title: (POSTHUMOUS) + NO TITLE
description: Ghassan Salhab (POSTHUMOUS) / (POSTHUME) 2007, 31 min, DCP. In Arabic with English subtitles. “Not long after the Israeli attack of 2006, Ghassan Salhab directed this filmic essay; its images are both absent and present witnesses to an unexpected war. A cinematographic musing on contemporary Lebanon and a wager on the impossibility of recounting the violence of a bruised country, whose ghosts reappear from the ruins and stare at the screen, before disappearing in cross-fade.” –VISIONS DU RÉEL Ghassan Salhab NO TITLE 2025, 42 min, DCP. In Arabic with English subtitles. “[NO TITLE is] a car-bound survey of utterly devastated sites in South Lebanon following the 2024 Israeli airstrikes. In many respects this film can be viewed as an extension of [Salhab’s CONTRETEMPS (2024)], an afterword necessitated by ongoing escalations beyond the cinema screen. It is not to reveal too much about NO TITLE to cite its closing statement, a gnomic endnote that hints at the unfathomably endless horrors of Israel’s war: ‘still today’.” –ALCHEMY FILM & ARTS Total running time: ca. 75 min.

title: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth
description: Brad Pitt returns to his Academy Award-winning role as Cliff Booth, only this time it’s 1977 and it’s a very different Hollywood. Directed by David Fincher from a screenplay by Quentin Tarantino, the film also stars Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Carla Gugino, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II and Peter Weller. (Netflix)

title: Vidiots Hornyfest – Portrait of a Lady on Fire
description: Passion brews quietly between an artist and her subject, until together they create a space in which it can briefly flourish, in this sumptuous eighteenth-century romance from Céline Sciamma, one of contemporary French cinema’s most acclaimed auteurs. Summoned to an isolated seaside estate on a secret assignment, Marianne (Noémie Merlant) must find a way to paint a wedding portrait of Héloïse (Adèle Haenel), who is resisting chattel marriage, by furtively observing her. What unfolds in exquisite tension is an exchange of sustained gazes in which the two women come to know each other’s gestures, expressions, and bodies with rapturous intimacy, ultimately forging a subversive creative collaboration as well as a delirious romance. Charged with a yearning that almost transcends time and space, Portrait of a Lady on Fire mines the emotional and artistic possibilities that emerge when women can freely live together and see one another in a world without men.

title: Amadeus
description: Disciplined Italian composer Antonio Salieri becomes consumed by jealousy and resentment towards the hedonistic and remarkably talented young Salzburger composer Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart.

title: Avengers: Doomsday
description: In “Avengers: Doomsday,” beloved heroes from three distinct universes will be set on a deadly collision course and face an existential threat unlike anything they’ve ever encountered.

title: Eyes Wide Shut
description: Stanley Kubrick's daring last film is many things. It is a compelling psychosexual journey. A haunting dreamscape. A riveting tale of suspense. A major milestone in the careers of stars Tom Cruise and Nicole Kidman. And "a worthy final chapter to a great director's career" (Roger Ebert). Cruise plays Dr William Hartford, who plunges into an erotic foray that threatens his marriage - and may even ensnare him in a lurid murder mystery - after his wife's (Kidman) admission of sexual longings. As the story sweeps from doubt and fear to self-discovery and reconciliation, Kubrick orchestrates it with masterful flourishes. Graceful tracking shots, controlled pacing, rich colours, startling images: bravura traits that make Kubrick a filmmaker for the ages are here to keep everyone's eyes wide shut.

title: BLOOD BEAT
description:
Christmas in rural Wisconsin becomes awkward when a young woman visits her boyfriend’s family and encounters a hostile mother, psychic disturbances and the spirit of a Japanese samurai. Before long, the seasonal gathering has acquired a body count and abandoned any obligation to explain itself sensibly.
Fabrice Zaphiratos’ regional horror oddity combines woodland slasher business with supernatural combat, electronic noise and a strangely dreamy atmosphere. The homemade effects and abrupt leaps of logic only make its world harder to shake. A Christmas film that seems to have arrived from a parallel video shop where every shelf is the wrong one.

title: The Holdovers
description: From acclaimed director Alexander Payne, THE HOLDOVERS follows a curmudgeonly instructor (Paul Giamatti) at a prestigious American school who is forced to remain on campus during Christmas break to babysit the handful of students with nowhere to go. Eventually he forms an unlikely bond with one of them -- a damaged, brainy troublemaker (newcomer Dominic Sessa) -- and with the school’s head cook, who has just lost a son in Vietnam (Da’Vine Joy Randolph).

title: THE SWORD IN THE STONE
description: Disney’s underrated adaptation of the first title in T.H. White’s classic series The Once and Future King relates the coming-of-age of a young King Arthur, here named Wart, and his training by the wizard Merlin. Using the Xerox-transfer technology the studio implemented to great acclaim in its preceding 101 DALMATIANS, THE SWORD IN THE STONE centers on the magical arts of transformation, culminating in an epic battle of Merlin against the evil witch Madam Mim. Preceded by: Georges Méliès LE MAGICIEN (1898, 1 min, 35mm-to-DCP) Like THE SWORD IN THE STONE, George Méliès’s LE MAGICIEN emphasizes mystical metamorphoses. Total running time: ca. 85 min.
director: Wolfgang Reitherman, Clyde Geronimi, and David Hand

title: Home Alone
description: When bratty 8-year-old Kevin McCallister (Macaulay Culkin) acts out the night before a family trip to Paris, his mother (Catherine O'Hara) makes him sleep in the attic. After the McCallisters mistakenly leave for the airport without Kevin, he awakens to an empty house and assumes his wish to have no family has come true. But his excitement sours when he realizes that two con men (Joe Pesci, Daniel Stern) plan to rob the McCallister residence, and that he alone must protect the family home.

title: The Apartment
description: Insurance worker C.C. Baxter (Jack Lemmon) lends his Upper West Side apartment to company bosses to use for extramarital affairs. When his manager Mr. Sheldrake (Fred MacMurray) begins using Baxter's apartment in exchange for promoting him, Baxter is disappointed to learn that Sheldrake's mistress is Fran Kubelik (Shirley MacLaine), the elevator girl at work whom Baxter is interested in himself. Soon Baxter must decide between the girl he loves and the advancement of his career.

title: It's A Wonderful Life
description: Beset with personal and professional problems, George Bailey finds his previously happy life falling apart around him on Christmas Eve. Seeing no way out, George considers suicide from the edge of a bridge ­ but Clarence, his guardian angel, intervenes and shows George what his beloved hometown of Bedford Falls would be like without him.

title: Angel's Egg
description: In an underwater city, a young girl takes care of a large egg she holds carefully in her arms. A boy with a gun arrives in search of a bird he saw in his dream. At first, it seems as if feelings of sympathy are developing between the two. Forty years after the film’s original release, Anime Limited is proud to present an all-new 4K restoration of the film, supervised by director Mamoru Oshii, in cinemas nationwide for the very first time. The film is a creative collaboration between acclaimed director Mamoru Oshii (Ghost in the Shell), who wrote and directed the feature, and revered artist Yoshitaka Amano (Final Fantasy, Vampire Hunter D). The film beautifully intertwines Oshii’s thematic reflections on philosophy and theology with Amano’s distinctive ink painting style, culminating in an arrestingly beautiful hand-drawn allegorical fantasy.

Join Kermit the Frog, Miss Piggy, and all the hilarious Muppets in this merry, magical version of Charles Dickens' classic tale. Academy Award® winner Michael Caine (Best Supporting Actor) gives a performance that's anything but "bah, humbug!" as greedy, penny-pinching Ebenezer Scrooge. One fateful Christmas Eve, Scrooge is visited by the Ghosts of Christmas Past, Present, and Future. Together with kind, humble Bob Cratchit (Kermit the Frog) and his family, the Spirits open Scrooge's eyes -- and his heart -- to the true meaning of Christmas. Filled with original music and dazzling special effects, THE MUPPET CHRISTMAS CAROL will become a holiday tradition your family will treasure all the days of the year. Featuring the film’s famous long-lost song ‘When Love is Gone’! ------ As always you can expect SING ALONG performances of this new version of THE MUPPET CHRISTMAS CAROL this Christmas - and now we don't need to pretend that we weren't going to just play the lost scene regardless! title: Elf
description: Buddy (Will Ferrell) was accidentally transported to the North Pole as a toddler and raised to adulthood among Santa's elves. Unable to shake the feeling that he doesn't fit in, the adult Buddy travels to New York, in full elf uniform, in search of his real father. As it happens, this is Walter Hobbs (James Caan), a cynical businessman. After a DNA test proves this, Walter reluctantly attempts to start a relationship with the childlike Buddy with increasingly chaotic results.

title: VALERIE AND HER WEEK OF WONDERS
description:
A pair of enchanted earrings offers Valerie protection as her village fills with vampires, corrupt holy men and relatives who will not stay in the same shape. Growing up here means discovering that familiar faces can become the strangest masks.
Jaromil Jireš makes a fairy tale from the collision of innocence, fear and awakening. Jan Curík’s luminous images and Luboš Fišer’s haunting score give the Czech New Wave fantasy the vividness of a half-remembered dream. Beautiful and deeply uncanny, it draws folk horror out of sunlight as readily as shadow.
Presented by Softcore Cinema Club.

title: STUDENT CONFIDENTIAL
description: A millionaire in the midst of a personal crisis becomes a high school guidance counselor and encourages four students to reach their potential… through unorthodox methods.

title: THE VALLEY / AL-WADI
description: “An unknown man survives a car accident in the middle of the Bekaa Valley with just a few scratches and the loss of his memory. Soon after, he meets a group of people who take him to a closely guarded farm. It’s a mysterious place where the inhabitants spend time on more than just farming, a place from which the unnamed protagonist may never be able to leave. This complex, disturbing mystery, conveying a message on the state of civilization, is so far the most ambitious picture by the renowned Lebanese director – a film intellectual who vividly succeeds in transmitting psychological categories into cinematic language.” –Karel Och, KARLOVY VARY INTERNATIONAL FILM FESTIVAL

title: THE GIRL ON A MOTORCYCLE
description:
Rebecca leaves her sleeping husband, climbs onto her motorcycle and sets off across Europe to visit her lover. As the miles disappear, she revisits the affair in a succession of memories and fantasies. The journey offers escape, but her thoughts keep taking more dangerous turns.
Marianne Faithfull and Alain Delon drift through Jack Cardiff’s extravagantly coloured erotic road movie, a strange meeting of literary obsession, leather-clad pop glamour and psychedelic technique. Landscapes dissolve into reverie as the camera gets as intoxicated as its heroine. A swinging-sixties artefact whose beauty keeps tipping into delirium.

title: Solve Along A Murder She Wrote
description: Cult hit event Solve-Along-A-Murder-She-Wrote returns to the Prince Charles Cinema with an interactive screening of a classic Murder, She Wrote episode. Watch as Cabot Cove gets caught up in a murder mystery only JB Fletcher (or you!) can solve! Solve-Along-A-Murder-She-Wrote is a unique and hilarious night featuring games, prizes and audience participation, with special permission from NBC Universal Television. See the show Time Out rated one of 2021 and 2019’s 50 Great Nights Out in London that has played to sell-out audiences across the UK and Australia. Hosted by super-fan Tim Benzie, Solve-Along-A-Murder-She-Wrote features: * A race to solve to the crime, via the Fameometer and the Suspiciometer! * A Cabot Cove quiz! * A singalong to the theme tune with new lyrics! * Clips and biogs of the campy guest stars! Tim Benzie is obsessed with Murder, She Wrote, having watched the original series when it was first broadcast, and now relishing the repeats on television everywhere. Tim is the writer/performer of “It’s a Mystery!”, all about our love of whodunnits. An award-winning playwright and co-writer of the Royal Vauxhall Tavern’s 2017-2023 pantos (‘Goosed’, ‘Rubbed’, ‘Slipped’, ‘Pricked’, ‘Cracked’ and ‘Tossed’). He is the co-producer of the camp club night PopHorror. Before the night I had never seen an episode of Murder, She Wrote before, unlike some dedicated fans who had even dressed up. However, this really was an evening everyone could enjoy.” - Nottingham Post "As soon as I saw it was on at the [Edinburgh] Fringe I elbowed my way through the other BW reviewers, pushed a couple of them over … just so I could get to the front of the queue and see this show again. And it did not disappoint ... I'd go again in a heartbeat.” 5 stars ***** - Broadway World "The self-confessed super-fan and award-winning playwright will lead you into a silly whirlwind of nostalgic giggle, using his wealth of camp trivia and sound logic to solve these killings.” 5 stars ***** - One4Review "Benzie knows how to put on a great show ... I would happily see it again, with all the fervour of the ‘Jessica Fletcher eating popcorn’ meme." 5 stars ***** - Everything Theatre “Whodunnit? Tim dunnit – and he did it so well I can’t wait for the next one!" 5 stars ***** - Fairy-Powered Productions “I’d challenge anyone to sit through this show and not get utterly invested in figuring out whodunit.” 4 stars **** - West End Wilma “This is a highly entertaining production even if you have never seen an episode, filled with outrageous fun." 4 stars **** - British Theatre Guide "For a funny, campy evening, there is little that could beat Solve-Along-A-Murder-She-Wrote’s unique qualities and Benzie’s wit and charm. Personally this reviewer can’t wait to revisit Cabot Cove. Never mind 'whodunnit', more like 'yougottadoit!" 4 stars **** - The Reviews Hub “A lighthearted two hours of entertainment that both die-hard devotees and Cabot Cove novices will enjoy ... A solve-along, sing-along hit." 4 stars **** - Broadway Baby “Benzie's passion and knowledge shines through." 4 stars **** - West End Best Friend "Tim Benzie is the perfect host ... Benzie’s insights help keep the audience engaged with the show and not just passively watching the episode unfold.” 4 stars **** - The Nerd Party “It didn’t take long for Benzie to have the audience in stitches and he had the whole crowd in the palm of his hand the entire evening.” - Bristol 24/7 “A unique and thoroughly enjoyable theatre experience” - Blue Curtains Brisbane *** For links to the full reviews visit www.solvealongamurdershewrote.com

When Jack accidentally stumbles on Christmastown, all bright colors and warm spirits, he gets a new lease on life -- he plots to bring Christmas under his control by kidnapping Santa Claus and taking over the role. But Jack soon discovers even the best-laid plans of mice and skeleton men can go seriously awry.

title: The Shining
description: All work and no play makes Jack a dull boy. Stanley Kubrick’s foreboding masterpiece of psychological terror is an icy Stephen King scare-fest best experienced on screen. Determined to make a new start for his family, Jack Torrance accepts a winter job as caretaker at the remote, snowbound Overlook Hotel to make headway with his frustrated writing career. But as isolation grows and his young son’s disturbing visions intensify, sanity will erode, and the gigantic lodge’s sinister secrets will be revealed. Jack Nicholson, Shelley Duvall, and Danny Lloyd are stellar in one of cinema’s all-time great nightmares, with Scatman Crothers, Joe Turkel, and Philip Stone doing superior work in key supporting roles.

title: Dune: Part Three
description: Dune: Part Three is set nearly two decades after Paul Atreides seized control of the Imperium. Now a ruthless Emperor, Paul must face the consequences of his reign as old allies return, terrifying new threats emerge, and betrayal lurks in every shadow. Haunted by visions of Imperial collapse and the reappearance of his long-lost love, Paul is drawn into a sweeping conspiracy, with Chani at the heart of its unfolding mystery. As rebellion brews and enemies close in, Paul must confront the true cost of power and the fate of those he loves the most.

description:
Agent 00 has a kidnapped scientist to rescue, an evil mastermind to stop and a gadget for almost every occasion. The odds are absurd. Weng Weng treats them as an invitation.
Eddie Nicart’s Filipino spy adventure gives its star a full arsenal of rooftop escapes, martial-arts encounters and Bond-style ingenuity. What makes it irresistible is the commitment: the film plays its impossible mission with an infectious mixture of swagger and invention. A scrappy international cult favourite powered by a performer who makes every entrance his own.

title: BLUE MONDAY PRESENTS: THE PASSIONS OF CAROL
description:
Carol Scrooge runs an adult magazine with little generosity towards the people producing it. On Christmas Eve, a succession of supernatural visitors offers her an unusually intimate education in the errors of her ways. Dickens’ familiar seasonal reckoning takes a substantial detour through the New York adult-film underground.
Shaun Costello brings surprising care and comic invention to this explicit Christmas Carol, with painted sets and performers including Jamie Gillis and Mary Stuart treating the absurd premise with admirable commitment. Its homemade fantasy and grubby office satire make a disarmingly odd festive discovery. Christmas redemption for people who would rather be spending the evening at The Nickel.

title: CIPRÌ & MARESCO PGM 1: CINEMA
description: Erudite and always irreverent cinephiles, Ciprì & Maresco have infused their work with their love for cinema, whether through homages, citations or profanations. Though hyperlocal (their filmmaking never ventured outside their native Palermo), their films have genealogically followed the human and cinematographic trajectories that lead from Sicily to America, and vice versa. They filmed Martin Scorsese recounting the urban articulation of Sicilian villages transplanted to Lower Manhattan and listened to Samuel Fuller chronicling the Allied invasion of Sicily in WWII. (American) Cinema is at the aesthetic center of their work. Their love for John Ford is plastically illustrated in their predilection for long shots, a recurring feature in the films of Ciprì & Maresco. This program gathers sketches from Cinico TV and short films that pay sacrilegious homage to the 7th Art. THE DAWN OF THE MURDERERS / L’ALBA DEL KILLER 1990, 2 min, video[THE FLY] Cinico TV, 1989-96, 38 sec, video STANLEY’S ROOM 1&2 1991, 2.5 min, video MARTIN, A LITTLE… 1992, 10 min, video [HOMAGE TO TWIN PEAKS] Cinico TV, 1989-96, 1 min, video [LE SAMURAI] Cinico TV, 1989-96, 33 sec, video [INTERMISSION 1] Cinico TV, 1989-96, 1 min, video SAMUEL FULLER (EXCERPT 1: ON LANDING IN SICILY IN WWII) 1992, 4.5 min, 16mm-to-digital SAMUEL FULLER (EXCERPT 2: ON HOLLYWOOD) 1992, 6.5 min, 16mm-to-digital SHOCK CORRIDOR aka SAMUEL FULLER ON JOHN FORD / IL CORRIDORE DELLA PAURA 1992, 5 min, 35mm-to-digital [THE TEN COMMANDMENTS aka PAVIGLIANITI AS MOSES] Cinico TV, 1989-96, 35 sec, video CARROT SKIN / PEL DI CAROTA 1991, 2 min, video BLUE MOVIE / MELANCHOLY LESTER 1993, 6 min, video HOMAGE TO E. / OMAGGIO A E. 1990, 12 min, video FARAWAY / LONTANE 1993, 2 min, video [THE HANDEYE] Cinico TV, 1989-96, 9 min, video Total running time: ca. 70 min.

title: The Greg Proops Film Club Presents THE SHOP AROUND THE CORNER
NARROW ROOMS: TERENCE DAVIES TRILOGY
description: Terence Davies did not have a happy childhood, and his early adulthood was plagued by guilt and anguish over his homosexuality. But film became his outlet for self-expression, and in this trilogy of black-and-white short films, Davies brilliantly laid out the anguish of his bleak early years. In CHILDREN, Davies faces homophobic bullies at school and an abusive father at home. In MADONNA AND CHILD, the adult Davies spends his days visiting his aging mother, and his nights pursuing guilt-inducing sadomasochistic sex. DEATH AND TRANSFIGURATION allows Davies to imagine the circumstances of his twilight years and recall slightly fonder moments from his childhood. Though these brilliant films were underappreciated on their release, they announced Davies as a major talent who became one of the greatest gay filmmakers of all time. What better time could there be than the Christmas season to catch this unrelenting exploration of gay Catholic guilt and existential dread? “The trilogy did the rounds of the international festival circuits and was often seen – in the States in particular – as an unnecessarily pessimistic piece, receiving limited arthouse distribution as a result. In a ‘glad to be gay’ climate, the insecurity, guilt and downright loneliness so astutely expressed in these films was an unfashionable stance. Because Terence dared to show the pain of growing up Catholic and homosexual in working-class Liverpool in the ’50s and early ’60s, the films were not celebrated enough. Terence once told me that when he recognized his homosexuality he knelt in prayer for so long that his knees bled – this pain is conveyed in the spirit of his films.” –Jennifer Howarth, SIGHT AND SOUND, 1994 CHILDREN (1976, 43 min, 16mm-to-DCP) MADONNA AND CHILD (1980, 30 min, 16mm-to-DCP) DEATH AND TRANSFIGURATION (1983, 23 min, 16mm-to-DCP) Total running time: ca. 100 min.

title: Die Hard [is a Christmas Movie]
description: New York City policeman John McClane (Bruce Willis) is visiting his estranged wife (Bonnie Bedelia) and two daughters on Christmas Eve. He joins her at a holiday party in the headquarters of the Japanese-owned business she works for. But the festivities are interrupted by a group of terrorists who take over the exclusive high-rise, and everyone in it. Very soon McClane realizes that there's no one to save the hostages -- but him.

title: MYSTERY MOVIE
description:
Take a seat without knowing what is coming. Our mystery screenings explore the bold, disreputable and gloriously unclassifiable world of psychotronic cinema: discoveries that make you wonder how they were made, who they were made for, and why nobody showed you sooner.
The title stays secret until showtime. Curiosity is essential; good taste is negotiable.
Strictly for adult audiences. Films may contain offensive and upsetting content. Do not attend if you are of a sensitive disposition.

title: CIPRÌ & MARESCO PGM 2: (IN)HUMAN URGES
description: The body, in all its abominable candor, is one of the poetic pillars of Ciprì & Maresco’s cinema. Tragically devoid of any female presence, their films frame with sardonic ridicule the violent loneliness of men. Undressed, both literally and metaphorically, the male body is the lone signifier of (in)human urges that are always frustrated, crudely demanded but never fulfilled. The appalling body and its unspeakable impulses are not so much filmed, but structure the vision and cinema of Ciprì & Maresco. The rubble they’re filmed in is not mere background but an unflattering reflection of the human ruins they incarnate. In the cosmically pessimistic universe of Ciprì & Maresco, humanity is doomed, for even life already resembles death. A bitter laughter is the lapidary seal on this dejected, (post-)human landscape. title: Love Actually
description: Nine intertwined stories examine the complexities of the one emotion that connects us all: love. Among the characters explored are David (Hugh Grant), the handsome newly elected British prime minister who falls for a young junior staffer (Martine McCutcheon), Sarah (Laura Linney), a graphic designer whose devotion to her mentally ill brother complicates her love life, and Harry (Alan Rickman), a married man tempted by his attractive new secretary.

title: Rent
description: Embrace your inner theater kid and join us for a big and loud screening of Rent . Anthony Rapp, Adam Pascal, Jesse L. Martin, Wilson Jermaine Heredia, Idina Menzel, and Taye Diggs reprise their Broadway roles — and are joined by Rosario Dawson and Tracie Thoms — as a host of young bohemians trying to realize their creative dreams and support each other through poverty, drug addiction, and AIDS. Talk about a time capsule: Chris Columbus’ 2005 film adaptation of Jonathan Larson’s 1996 musical is technically set in 1989 New York City, although it feels like the most 1990s work of art to ever exist.  While loosely based on the Puccini opera, La Boheme could never!

title: The Hateful Eight (Multiplex Version)
description: During a deadly snowstorm, a bounty hunter (Kurt Russell) rushes to bring his fugitive (Jennifer Jason Leigh) to justice. But losing their lead on the blizzard, they must seek refuge at Minnie’s Haberdashery where the mysterious strangers inside may not be who they seem. Written & directed by Quentin Tarantino and co-starring a stunning ensemble of QT favorites and pitch-perfect additions to his troupe: Samuel L. Jackson, Walton Goggins, Demián Bichir, Tim Roth, Michael Madsen and Bruce Dern round out The Hateful Eight .

title: The Muppet Christmas Carol
description: 'Tis the season for love, laughter, and one of the most cherished stories of all time! Join Kermit the Frog, Miss Piggy, and all the hilarious Muppets in this merry, magical version of Charles Dickens' classic tale. Academy Award® winner Michael Caine (Best Supporting Actor) gives a performance that's anything but "bah, humbug!" as greedy, penny-pinching Ebenezer Scrooge. One fateful Christmas Eve, Scrooge is visited by the Ghosts of Christmas Past, Present, and Future. Together with kind, humble Bob Cratchit (Kermit the Frog) and his family, the Spirits open Scrooge's eyes -- and his heart -- to the true meaning of Christmas. Filled with original music and dazzling special effects, THE MUPPET CHRISTMAS CAROL will become a holiday tradition your family will treasure all the days of the year. Featuring the film’s famous long-lost song ‘When Love is Gone’! ------ As always you can expect SING ALONG performances of this new version of THE MUPPET CHRISTMAS CAROL this Christmas - and now we don't need to pretend that we weren't going to just play the lost scene regardless! Performances will feature a Hosted Pre-Show with our very own Father Christmas, where you will be prepped on what to do throughout the film. Costumes aren't mandatory, but 'Tis the season, and we love seeing you dressed up in your favourite Christmas Jumpers! All this, and a few more surprises up our sleeves, makes this one of the must-see events this Christmas! description: Kermit, Oscar the Grouch, Miss Piggy and the gang get to grips with Charles Dickens’ Christmas favourite in this beloved take on the classic tale. In amongst the Muppet family, Michael Caine steps into the slippers of the miserly Ebenezer Scrooge with great grumpy relish as a trio of ghostly visitations attempt to banish his bah-humbug spirit.

title: It's A Wonderful Life
description: Beset with personal and professional problems, George Bailey finds his previously happy life falling apart around him on Christmas Eve. Seeing no way out, George considers suicide from the edge of a bridge ­ but Clarence, his guardian angel, intervenes and shows George what his beloved hometown of Bedford Falls would be like without him.

description: Bring your little ones, or your adult besties, for a delightful double feature of epic holiday proportions when Vidiots lights up our screen with two of the most enchanting holiday specials of all time!

title: Saturday Afternoon Cartoons: That Frosty Holiday
The Muppet Christmas Carol
description: Revisit the timeless Dickens tale with your prized puppet pals in The Muppet Christmas Carol ! Ebenezer Scrooge (Michael Caine) is the greediest grump in all of London until he’s taken on a mystical journey of self-discovery by the Ghosts of Christmas Past, Present and Yet to Come. Utterly charming and filled with heart, humor, and all your favorite felt-lined friends (plus unforgettable Paul Williams songs!), this beloved family classic is sensational, inspirational, celebrational, and perfectly muppetational, while also surprisingly faithful to the source material.

Now a ruthless Emperor, Paul must face the consequences of his reign as old allies return, terrifying new threats emerge, and betrayal lurks in every shadow. Haunted by visions of Imperial collapse and the reappearance of his long-lost love, Paul is drawn into a sweeping conspiracy, with Chani at the heart of its unfolding mystery. As rebellion brews and enemies close in, Paul must confront the true cost of power and the fate of those he loves the most.

title: Elf
description: A misfit who grows to be three times the size of his elf family, Buddy ultimately heads to his birthplace of New York City to seek out his roots. Unfortunately, they turn out to be a "Scrooge"-like father (James Caan) and a cynical eight-year-old stepbrother who doesn't believe in Santa. Worst of all, everyone seems to have forgotten the true meaning of Christmas. But using his simple elf ways, Buddy sets out to single-handedly win over his family and save Christmas in New York, hoping to at last find his true place in the world.

title: Home Alone
description: When bratty 8-year-old Kevin McCallister (Macaulay Culkin) acts out the night before a family trip to Paris, his mother (Catherine O'Hara) makes him sleep in the attic. After the McCallisters mistakenly leave for the airport without Kevin, he awakens to an empty house and assumes his wish to have no family has come true. But his excitement sours when he realizes that two con men (Joe Pesci, Daniel Stern) plan to rob the McCallister residence, and that he alone must protect the family home.

title: Home Alone
description: Eight-year-old Kevin McCallister makes the most of the situation after his family unwittingly leaves him behind when they go on Christmas vacation. When thieves try to break into his home, he puts up a fight like no other.

title: Art Cinema for Tots: Tales from the Forest
MCCABE & MRS MILLER
description:
A gambler arrives in a muddy mining town and opens a brothel. An experienced madam offers to make the business work, and together they begin building something that almost resembles a future. Then a powerful mining company decides it wants their patch of the frontier.
Robert Altman strips the western of its clean shirts and heroic certainties, leaving Warren Beatty and Julie Christie to negotiate money, desire and survival in the snow. Leonard Cohen’s songs haunt the smoky rooms while Vilmos Zsigmond’s photography makes the whole town feel half remembered. A devastating film about small-time dreamers discovering who really owns the American dream.

title: Tokyo Godfathers
description: Get in the holiday spirit with Satoshi Kon’s breathtaking anime marvel. Based loosely on The 3 Godfathers , this tender tale of three people on the margins of society coming to the aid of a helpless abandoned infant is the inclusive, holiday heartwarmer everyone can rejoice in. When a drunk, a runaway, and a trans woman come across a baby girl at the garbage dump on Christmas Eve, they must band together to solve a mystery, reunite the child with her family, and confront the ghosts from their own pasts. With an astonishing beauty of both animation and spirit, Tokyo Godfathers is easily Satoshi Kon’s most touching film, and an incredible feat of both art and heart.

title: EC: GEORGE LANDOW, AKA OWEN LAND
description: “The unique contribution of Land’s work lies in the fusion of intellectual reason and, significantly, the humor that distances it from the supposedly ‘boring’ world of avant-garde film. Having explored the basic properties of the celluloid strip itself in early works such as FILM IN WHICH THERE APPEAR…, his attention turned to the spectator in a series of ‘literal’ films that question the illusionary nature of cinema through the use of word play and visual ambiguity. His work often parodies experimental film itself by mimicking his contemporaries and mocking the solemn approach of film theorists and scholars.” –Mark Webber, TWO FILMS BY OWEN LAND FLEMING FALOON (1963, 6 min, 16mm) FILM IN WHICH THERE APPEAR EDGE LETTERING, SPROCKET HOLES, DIRT PARTICLES, ETC. title: EC: LAUREL AND HARDY: OUR RELATIONS
description: “Stan Laurel and Oliver Hardy are the movies’ greatest comic duo, the quintessential dumb and dumber odd couple. Though critically overshadowed by Chaplin, Keaton, and Lloyd, they were enormously popular, and proved a major influence on Abbott & Costello, Lucille Ball & Vivian Vance, and Jackie Gleason & Art Carney, not to mention Samuel Beckett (they were an inspiration for WAITING FOR GODOT), Roman Polanski (who paid homage to them in his existentialist short films FAT AND LEAN and TWO MEN AND A WARDROBE), and Ken Jacobs (whose ONTIC ANTICS deconstructs one of their films).” –David Mulkins Special thanks to Ken & Flo Jacobs. Harry Lachman OUR RELATIONS 1936, 73 min, 16mm “Among the finest features ever made by comedy legends Stan Laurel and Oliver Hardy, this delirious 1936 farce casts the duo in dual roles as both respectable family men and their hard-drinking sailor twins. When the brothers converge in the same city during a shore leave, a cascade of mistaken identities, misplaced suspicions, and escalating misunderstandings throws everyone into confusion.” –THE COLONIAL THEATRE

title: CIPRÌ & MARESCO PGM 3: CRIMINAL (DIS)ORGANIZATION
description: In the “Cinico TV” sketches and short films devoted to the Mafia and crime more generally, Ciprì & Maresco radically overturn the conventions of political and anti-Mafia cinema. Cosa Nostra does not appear as a mythical, mysterious, or invincible power, but as an ordinary and grotesque presence, immersed in the marginality of the bodies, landscapes, and characters that inhabit their Palermo. Mafia bosses, affiliates, and rituals are stripped of any aura of (anti-)heroism and returned to a dimension that is at once miserable and surreal, where violence coexists with emptiness, absurdity, and everyday degradation. Through silences, distorted dialogue, and pitch-black humor, Ciprì & Maresco dismantle the mythology surrounding the Mafia and reveal its banality as a form of power and oppression. title: BOB & CAROL & TED & ALICE
description:
After a consciousness-raising weekend retreat, affluent Los Angeles couple Bob and Carol embrace a new gospel of total honesty, emotional openness and sexual freedom. Their more conventional friends Ted and Alice are sceptical - until confessions, affairs and a trip to Las Vegas push all four toward the logical conclusion.
Paul Mazursky’s wickedly sharp debut catches the sexual revolution halfway between liberation and nervous breakdown, with Natalie Wood, Robert Culp, Elliott Gould and Dyan Cannon exposing every absurdity beneath the era’s enlightened smiles.

title: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth
description: Brad Pitt returns to his Academy Award-winning role as Cliff Booth, only this time it’s 1977 and it’s a very different Hollywood. Directed by David Fincher from a screenplay by Quentin Tarantino, the film also stars Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Carla Gugino, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II and Peter Weller. (Netflix)

title: Married to the Mob
description: Michelle Pfeiffer is at her absolutely most charming in this magnificent mash up of comedy and crime story from the great Jonathan Demme. Angela de Marco is fed up with her gangster husband’s line of work and wants no part of the crime world. When her husband is killed for having an affair with the mistress of mob boss Tony “The Tiger” Russo, Angela and her son depart for New York City to make a fresh start. Unfortunately, Tony has set his sights upon Angela — and so has an undercover FBI agent looking to use her to bust Tony. With a dynamite cast, iconic 80s fashion, and Demme’s delightful direction, you will never have more fun with the mafia than in this utter blast on the big screen!

title: Hail Mary preceded by The Book of Mary
Scott Pilgrim vs. the World
description: As bass guitarist for a garage-rock band, Scott Pilgrim has never had trouble getting a girlfriend; usually, the problem is getting rid of them. But when Ramona Flowers skates into his heart, he finds she has the most troublesome baggage of all: an army of ex-boyfriends who will stop at nothing to eliminate him from her list of suitors.

title: EC: LÉGER & MURPHY / PICABIA & CLAIR / MAN RAY & DUCHAMP
description: Fernand Léger & Dudley Murphy BALLET MÉCANIQUE (1924, 19 min, 35mm, silent. Preserved by Anthology Film Archives.) “The two fundamental works of the graphic cinema from the 1920s made without animation were Fernand Léger’s BALLET MÉCANIQUE and Marcel Duchamp’s ANEMIC CINEMA. By extending a metaphor from several of his paintings into film, Léger compared a universe of human actions and everyday objects to the functions of a machine.” –P. Adams Sitney, VISIONARY FILM René Clair & Francis Picabia ENTR’ACTE (1924, 22 min, 35mm) One of the indisputable masterpieces of Dada cinema, ENTR’ACTE was created, as its title suggests, to function as a diversion in between the two acts of Francis Picabia and Erik Satie’s avant-garde ballet RELÂCHE. Man Ray LE RETOUR À LA RAISON (1923, 2 min, 16mm, silent) ÉTOILE DE MER (1927, 13 min, 16mm, silent) EMAK BAKIA (1927, 18 min, 35mm, silent) “All the films I have made have been improvisations. I did not write scenarios. It was automatic cinema. I worked alone. My intention was to set in motion the compositions I made in photography. As for the camera, I use it to capture something I do not want to paint. But I am not interested in producing ‘beautiful photography’ for the cinema.” –Man Ray, “All the Films I Have Made” (1965) Marcel Duchamp & Man Ray ANEMIC CINEMA (1926, 7 min, 35mm, silent) “Duchamp alternates head-on views of his illusion-producing roto-reliefs with similarly turned discs of words, elaborate French puns printed spirally, creating a fluctuation of illusory depth within a very narrow spectrum (from the slightly convex or slightly concave illusions) to the flat readings. In this, his only film, Duchamp typically crystallized the significance of the graphic film.” –P. Adams Sitney, VISIONARY FILM Total running time: ca. 85 min. CLICK HERE TO BOOK TICKETS NOW!

title: In Which Annie Gives It Those Ones
CIPRÌ & MARESCO PGM 4: WITH(OUT) FREEDOM
description: For all the pessimism and cynicism that animates the cinema of Ciprì & Maresco, there is a visionary tension that prevents the lights from going off completely: a glimmer of hopeless and resplendent defiance (Carmelo Bene saw in their films “the grandiosity of the sacred”). Informed by an eclectic array of cultural influences, there is a vital force that invigorates every frame, a ludic folly that catches the spectators off guard and floods them with amazement.
